dims.title: Native task definition, scoring, horizon, episode loop and reset

result.dimension: Native make_toast task definition, scoring, horizon, episode loop and reset (RoboDojo f57e1633, XPolicyLab 5d0be149, IsaacLab afca7b09, HF assets RoboDojo-Benchmark/RoboDojo main sha 269457a3b42d8d0ae69898a601f2c1487c2f826e)

claims.claim: Variant: Standard = task key make_toast, distinct from make_toast_random
claims.evidence: task_registry.py:10-17 loads class by exact key; make_toast_random differs only in BREAD_Z_LOWER/UPPER -0.05/0.068 vs 0.03/0.065 (make_toast_random.py:9-10 vs make_toast.py:9-10), toaster models index [2,4] vs [0,1] (make_toast_random.yml:15 vs make_toast.yml:15), plus 15 clutter objects and a ProhibitedArea (make_toast_random.yml:117-132). Success and score code are otherwise identical (shared MakeToastCommon).

claims.claim: Episode selection: seed-directory 0, first official saved layout (layoutID0), one env, one attempt
claims.evidence: The concepts exist. seed_manager.py:32-43 uses layout_dir = Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/<config_name>/<eval seed>, matches make_toast_\d+\.json, sorts by suffix, and sets layout_id = enumeration index. At HF main sha 269457a3 the arx_x5/0 directory holds 70 contiguous standard files, make_toast_0..69.json (plus 45 make_toast_random_*). So layoutID0 = make_toast_0.json (LFS sha256 f78afb3f82b6d9ce2399b13a8ce8a1508134565e7e8cd97f8a8532854fbc0b28, 8679 B). main.py:318-323 forces num_envs=1 when eval_batch=false. The native loop does NOT guarantee one attempt on layout 0; see the substitution finding.

claims.claim: Success = native full-success signal, with native partial score reported separately
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:799-806: if self.success[env_idx] then episode_score=1.0; elif process_scores then episode_score = process_scores[env_idx]/100.0 (0.25 or 0.5). The two values are distinct.

claims.claim: Native horizon is 1400 control actions
claims.evidence: make_toast.py:15 self.step_lim = 1400. eval_env.py:368-371 skips the action if take_action_cnt == step_lim and otherwise increments by 1. eval_env.py:845-860 checks success before the step-limit failure, so exactly 1400 actions run and the 1400th is still scored. No off-by-one.

claims.claim: _task.yml assigns 25 episodes to each variant and disables robot self-collision for make_toast
claims.evidence: _task.yml:67-75: make_toast and make_toast_random both set data_source teleop, robot_self_collision false, eval_nums 25. pipeline_utils.py:105-107 sets enabled_self_collisions=False for every robot; pipeline_utils.py:109 returns eval_num.

claims.claim: data_source: teleop is metadata (not permission to feed demonstrations)
claims.evidence: It is correct that this is not permission to use demonstrations. It is not inert metadata: pipeline_utils.py:82-83 `if ... data_source == "teleop": _enable_teleop_physx_stabilization(env_cfg["sim"])`, and pipeline_utils.py:70-72 sets physx enable_stabilization=True. That changes the default in base_env.py:27.

claims.claim: Download the official evaluation-layout subset needed for Make Toast
claims.evidence: The official scripts/init_assets.sh:14-20,101-106 sparse-clones HF dataset RoboDojo-Benchmark/RoboDojo at HF_REVISION default `main` (unpinned) and pulls all Assets/** (Robots, Object, Material, Eval_Layout). A subset can work. Because layout_id is the enumeration index of the files present (seed_manager.py:41-43), a gappy subset silently remaps IDs; make_toast_0.json stays index 0 whenever it is present.

claims.claim: Full success checks both filled slots, bread orientations/placement, exactly two slices on the shelf, lever position and return to robot origin
claims.evidence: make_toast.py:56-67 run_reward. Slot fill: func_parser.py:2219-2301 (bread root xy inside the 4-point slot polygon) and 1048-1124 (0.03 < z_bread - z_slot < 0.065). Orientation is required for all 4 breads, including those on the shelf: func_parser.py:996-1018 with threshold 30 deg. Shelf count: func_parser.py:2581-2592 `return 1.0 if count == N`, i.e. exactly 2. Lever: func_parser.py:1776-1808 ratio > 0.85. Origin: func_parser.py:1631-1644 checks both arms. Imprecisions in the plan's wording: gripper-open is NOT part of full success, and 'orientations' means all four slices upright.

claims.claim: The return-home and remaining-bread conditions are 'hidden finishing conditions'
claims.evidence: The official task page https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/sim-tasks/make-toast/ Scoring row 100 reads: 'Both toaster slots are filled, exactly two bread slices remain on the shelf, the toaster control is pressed down, and the robot returns to origin.' The reference adapter passes this to the model by default: XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/policy.py:880-886 (recipe 'Default on'), 889-902 (appended to the Goal turn), recipes/make_toast.md:24, and docs.py:71-75 ('both arms are back within 0.15 m and 20 degrees of the pose they began the episode in').

claims.claim: Partial score 25/50
claims.evidence: make_toast.py:69-85 registers score_mode='transition' with [25, 50]. Stage semantics are decoded in key_facts. Score is a latched high-water mark (reward_manager.py:323-334).

claims.claim: take_action_cnt counts each per-environment action dictionary
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:364-371 increments by 1 per action dict per env in take_action_batch. take_action (eval_env.py:354-356) wraps one dict. The reference loops call take_action once per chunk element (demo_policy/deploy.py:10-11), so a chunk of N costs N.

claims.claim: Each action expands into 10 physics substeps at 25 Hz observation / 0.004 s physics timestep
claims.evidence: sim_config.yml:1-3 (decimation 1, dt 0.004); arx_x5.yml:9-10 (collect_freq 25); obs_manager.py:43-48 collect_interval = 1/(0.004*25) = 10; eval_env.py:500-504 interpolation_nums = collect_interval; eval_env.py:449-452 steps until the queue empties; eval_env.py:638-642 gives 1 physics step per pop; direct_rl_env.py:8-11 loops cfg.decimation=1 times.

claims.claim: About 56 simulated seconds
claims.evidence: 1400 actions x 10 substeps x 0.004 s = 14,000 physics steps = 56.0 s simulated.

claims.claim: Preserve native interpolation/hold schedule and end-of-action reward-sampling boundaries
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:519-530: the first floor(0.8*10)=8 substeps interpolate linearly with alpha=(i+1)/9 from the MEASURED joint state to the target; the last 2 hold the target. The gripper is additionally rate-limited per substep to 20% of its range from the measured opening (control_manager.py:22-34). Reward is sampled only after the 10th substep (eval_env.py:457 reward_manager.step, 465 is_episode_end).

claims.claim: Freeze simulation while awaiting Astra; the native harness does not advance physics or action count while waiting
claims.evidence: Physics advances only in sim_step calls inside take_action_batch, setup_scene and reset (eval_env.py:258-262, 449-452; task_env.py:87-88). render_sync.py:24-25: '``env.render()`` does not advance physics.' Pinned IsaacLab simulation_context.py:616-627 wraps app.update() with /app/player/playSimulations False/True. Caveat: a bare simulation_app.update() can step physics (simulation_context.py:575 'FIXME: This steps physics as well'), so the adapter must not call one while waiting.

claims.claim: Native reset preparation includes a saved-layout stability procedure, ten render passes and an explicit 200-step setup_scene settling loop, not counted against the 1400
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:250 calls check_layout_stability (layout_manager.py:630-677: 300 physics steps); eval_env.py:256-257 `for _ in range(10): self.render()`; eval_env.py:258-262 200 sim_steps with capture every 5. take_action_cnt is zeroed at eval_env.py:220 and only incremented at 371, so none of these count. The description is incomplete: it omits 300 TaskEnv.reset steps (task_env.py:87-88), 1 reload step (scene_manager.py:188) and 20+20 apply_saved_poses steps (scene_manager.py:206-221). Total 841 physics steps (3.36 s).

claims.claim: Exact native gen_instruction text is the task text
claims.evidence: make_toast.py:87-88 returns ['Pick up two slices of bread, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.']. desc_manager.py:45-48,55-73 uses gen_instruction templates; there are no <label> placeholders, so the text is verbatim. It matches the official task page Instruction.

claims.claim: There is an upstream reference policy remaining-step field that must not be forwarded
claims.evidence: The native observation has no step counter, remaining-step or limit field (obs_manager.py:95-108: vision/state/action/data_format_version/additional_info{frequency}/instruction; eval_env.py:283 adds env_idx). The field exists only in XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/deploy.py:166 `remaining_steps=_remaining_env_steps(task_env)`, at 171-186 (= step_lim - take_action_cnt via trace.py:157-167). It is prompted as 'Env steps remaining before the episode ends: N' (inspect/policy.py:1412-1418).

claims.claim: The 100-planner-call limit appears in a particular robustness ablation, not a universal budget
claims.evidence: Native RoboDojo has no call cap (eval_env.py/main.py). However, the published reference harness defaults to 100 calls per episode: XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/README.md:81 '`L4_INSPECT_MAX_LLM_CALLS` | `100` | per-episode call budget'; inspect/policy.py:161 and 1187-1195 give_up 'LLM call budget exhausted', which the deploy marks failed at inspect/deploy.py:713-714. I did not audit the report's ablation text.

claims.claim: Lever position check means the lever is pressed down
claims.evidence: The check is (q - lower)/(upper - lower) > 0.85 on toaster joint_1 (tag toast_botton: metadata.json passive.functional.toast_botton.parent_joint='joint_1' for both toaster 00000 and 00001; func_parser.py:1796-1807). The limit direction and any return drive live in object.usdz/main.usdc, whose tokens are LZ4-compressed (only a 'Prismatic' token is readable), so they cannot be read without usd-core. Indirect evidence: several trained policies reach non-zero full-success SR on make_toast in the report table (e.g., Xiaomi-Robotics-1 SR 5.335, GalaxeaVLA 3.33), so lever > 0.85 is satisfiable with both arms home.

findings.title: Success requires return-to-origin and an exactly-two-left-on-shelf state that the instruction-only contract never tells Astra; these conditions are public and the official reference gives them to the model
findings.description: Native full success is the AND of: both slots filled, all four slices upright, exactly 2 slices on the shelf, lever ratio > 0.85, and both arms' link6 pose within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of the pose recorded at the end of reset. The instruction Astra receives covers only the first part. The native harness has no go-home, no final hold and no grace period. The episode ends only on success or after 1400 actions. In uc7.1, 'finish' never ends the episode. A run that does everything the instruction says will therefore score at most 50 unless Astra happens to return both arms home on its own: a failure caused by the information design, not by the agent's ability. The plan calls these 'hidden finishing conditions', but the official task page states them publicly. The official GPT-6-Astra reference adapter appends that scoring table to the Goal by default and states the 0.15 m / 20 deg rule in its embodiment notes. LIBERO's official goal had no robot-pose term, so 'same information types as LIBERO' and 'native full success' conflict for this task.
findings.evidence: make_toast.py:56-67 (run_reward includes is_N_A_in_B N=2, all-bread axis checks, all_robot_back_to_origin) vs make_toast.py:87-88 (instruction). func_parser.py:1631-1644 (both target arms; `np.any(np.abs(pos_dis) > 0.15) or rot_dis > 20` fails); func_parser.py:54-59 (origin = EE pose at reset). eval_env.py:841-867 (only success or step_lim end the episode). Official task page Scoring: '100 | Both toaster slots are filled, exactly two bread slices remain on the shelf, the toaster control is pressed down, and the robot returns to origin.' XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/docs.py:71-75: 'the work does not score until both arms are back within 0.15 m and 20 degrees of the pose they began the episode in... Getting home is the last step of the task'. inspect/policy.py:880-886 ('Default on'), 889-902; recipes/make_toast.md:19-24. Local: agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent_client.py:173-177 ('finish ... never ends the episode or sets success'). INPUT_CONTRACT.md:29 and PLAN.md:96 exclude these conditions. Report table make_toast: GPT-6-Astra Score 0.5, SR 0 even with the recipe.
findings.recommendation: Put an explicit choice to the user before implementation. (a) Add the official public task-page Description and Scoring text as a separately versioned 'public benchmark task specification' input. This is what the official reference does, and it is not evaluator-derived. Disclose it as a deviation from LIBERO's instruction-only text, and keep numeric internals (slot polygons, z ranges, 30 deg) out. Or (b) keep instruction-only, pre-register that native full success is expected to be unattainable without spontaneous homing, and make native partial score plus an evaluator-only 'instructed-goal achieved' check the primary reported outcome. Either way, rewrite PLAN.md:96 and INPUT_CONTRACT.md:29 so they no longer call these conditions hidden.

findings.title: The native eval loop silently substitutes layouts and restarts, which conflicts with 'layout 0, one attempt, no automatic retry'
findings.description: Under native main.py/eval_policy.sh, several paths start a different layout or a new process automatically: (1) an unstable layout raises UnStableError in setup_scene; main.py consumes the layout and runs the next one. (2) Any exception during reset/run_eval (ws timeout, adapter error) also consumes the layout and continues with the next, and the aborted episode is not counted. (3) PhysXBrokenError abandons the layout and refills from the queue. make_toast enables the PhysX monitor because its config has an Articulation section. (4) PhysXFatalError re-execs main.py up to 3 times, and eval_policy.sh then restarts up to 10 times with a resume manifest. (5) eval_num defaults to 25. At HF main, seed 0 has 70 standard layouts, so replacements are always available. The plan does not say how these are neutralized.
findings.evidence: main.py:376-377 (`except UnStableError: env.seed_manager.eval_step()`), 378-399 (generic exception -> eval_step), 434-442 (next get_seeds), 372-374 and 401-432 (abandon + refill), 10 and 211-238 (MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS=3, os.execv), 85-100 and 111 (monitor on when Articulation is non-empty; make_toast.yml:1-20); eval_policy.sh:142-185 (ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES default 10 on rc 99/134/139); pipeline_utils.py:109 and main.py:328-334 (eval_num 25, EVAL_NUM cap); eval_env.py:250-255; layout_manager.py:620-677 (stability thresholds: 30 deg/4 cm vs first pose, 10 deg/4 cm over the last 100 of 300 steps, z >= table-0.05). The reference fixes a single layout by writing a resume manifest that abandons all other IDs plus --eval-num: XPolicyLab scripts/run_robodojo_layout_range.sh:2-9,160-192,217-218.
findings.recommendation: Add to stages B/F: eval_num=1, a single-layout resume manifest (abandoned_layout_ids = all IDs except 0) or an equivalent custom loop, ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=0 with in-process restarts disabled, and a rule that UnStableError, PhysX broken/fatal errors and ws errors end the attempt as an infrastructure result with no layout substitution or re-exec. Add a test proving that layout 1 can never start.

findings.title: Native `success` defaults to True, so any early return from the episode function is recorded as a full success
findings.description: EvalEnv initializes success=[True] at every reset. Only is_episode_end turns it into a real outcome: success on reward of about 1, failure at take_action_cnt >= 1400. run_eval scores self.success after eval_one_episode returns, without checking end_flag. If the adapter's episode function returns because of a user stop at a feedback boundary, a handled controller error or a model 'finish', native bookkeeping records success=True, episode score 1.0 and a '_success' video. The official reference adapter guards against this explicitly. The plan's user-stop and error-finalization paths (section 4F) do not mention it.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:114 and 218 (`self.success = [True] * self.num_envs`); 775 (exist_envs taken before the episode); 783; 795-803 (`if self.success[env_idx]: ... episode_score = 1.0 ... tag = "success"`); 841-860 (the only places success flips). XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/deploy.py:331-351 (`_mark_incomplete_episode_failed` sets success False and calls is_episode_end) and 713-714.
findings.recommendation: Require every non-official termination path (user stop, finalization error, model stop, budget) to set success[env]=False and call is_episode_end() before returning, as the reference does. Alternatively, record the official result only from the latched end_flag/success pair set inside is_episode_end. Add a lifecycle test where a user stop yields success=false and score at the partial value.

findings.title: If Astra sits behind the native XPolicyLab websocket, its 120 s client request timeout is shorter than the planned 180 s deadline plus retries
findings.description: EvalEnv constructs WsModelClient without request_timeout_s, so every model_client.call (get_action) uses PolicyEvalClientConfig.request_timeout_s = 120 s. On expiry the client raises WsError(TIMEOUT), documented as 'fatal for the trial'. The exception propagates out of run_eval, and main.py then moves to the next layout (NT-2). The plan separates the simulator worker from the model process and keeps a 180 s per-request deadline with finite retries (up to 3 sends per class), so one decision can far exceed 120 s. Keepalive is not the problem: pings are handled off-thread on both sides. The official reference avoids the issue by running the LLM inside the env-client process between take_action calls, with a 90 s planner hard timeout.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:188-196 (only url/ids/ws_ping_* passed); XPolicyLab client_server/ws/model_client.py:55-71 (None means config default); protocol/client.py:91 `request_timeout_s: float = 120.0`, 520-530 ('callers must treat a timeout as fatal for the trial'); model_client.py:16-20 and model_server.py:393 (`asyncio.to_thread`) show keepalive is fine; GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/README.md:11 ('The eval client is where the LLM runs'), model.py:7, run_fixed_layout.sh:31 (L4_INSPECT_HARD_TIMEOUT_S 90); PLAN.md:72 and :116; UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:33,159-168.
findings.recommendation: Decide the transport explicitly. Either issue Astra calls from the env-side episode function, keeping the model process separate through the project's own IPC with no native ws request, or construct WsModelClient with request_timeout_s >= the worst case ((1 + max retries) x 180 s + backoff) and record that as a harness deviation. Add a timing test with a stub that sleeps more than 120 s.

findings.title: The data_source: teleop override changes physics (PhysX stabilization) and must be preserved and disclosed
findings.description: The plan discloses only the self-collision override and treats data_source: teleop as metadata. process_config also enables PhysX enable_stabilization for teleop tasks. An adapter that builds the env config outside process_config would silently run different physics.
findings.evidence: pipeline_utils.py:70-72 (`sim_cfg["physx"]["enable_stabilization"] = True`), 82-83 (applied when data_source == 'teleop'); _task.yml:68; default False at base_env.py:27; PLAN.md:66.
findings.recommendation: List all make_toast process_config effects as frozen task overrides: self-collision off for both arms, PhysX stabilization on, eval_nums 25, render_interval 10 (default). Hash the resolved sim/robot config in the approval binding.

findings.title: Reset-preparation description should list the exact native sequence and counts
findings.description: The plan names the stability procedure, 10 renders and the 200-step loop, but not the rest. The full native sequence is: scene reload (1 rendered sim step), 300 unrendered TaskEnv.reset steps, apply_saved_poses (20 steps after tables, 20 after objects; articulation apply also calls a bare app.update), the 300-step stability check with explicit thresholds (failure raises UnStableError), 10 renders, the 200-step settle with capture+get_obs every 5 steps, then set_origin_endpose, set_robot_init_state (both grippers commanded open at 0.044), reward_manager.init_state (records the origin EE poses that the return-home check uses), and model_client.call('reset'). That is 841 physics steps (3.36 s), none counted against the 1400.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:238-245, 247-262; task_env.py:83-90; scene_manager.py:159-192 (188 sim_step), 194-221; articulation.py:275-285 (`self.app.update()`); layout_manager.py:580-677; robot_manager.py:97-123 (gripper val = gripper_scale[1] when sign==1; robot_config.yml:10-15 sign 1.0, scale [-0.01, 0.044]); func_parser.py:32-59.
findings.recommendation: Record this sequence and its counts in the preview manifest, and the time origin_endpose is captured (it defines 'return to origin'). Compare origin poses across the two model-free resets as part of the determinism check.

findings.title: The 100-call figure is the published reference harness default, not only an ablation
findings.description: Native RoboDojo has no call cap, so the plan's 'no model-call cap' matches the native benchmark and LIBERO. But the official GPT-6-Astra adapter ends each episode as failed after 100 LLM calls by default and tells the model about that budget. This is a difference from the reference that should be disclosed, not justified as ablation-only.
findings.evidence: XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/README.md:81; inspect/policy.py:161 and 1187-1195; policy.py:175-178 ('Two budgets run down at once and whichever empties first ends the episode'); eval.sh:55; PLAN.md:30.
findings.recommendation: Reword PLAN.md:30: the reference adapter default is 100 calls per episode; native RoboDojo has none; uc7.1 keeps none for LIBERO parity.

findings.title: Exact score semantics differ from the public page and should be written down for the evaluator
findings.description: Transition stage 25 requires both grippers open (normalized >= 0.8, i.e. joint >= 0.0332 m of [-0.01, 0.044]) AND (slot1 or slot2 filled) AND all four slices upright. Stage 50 requires both grippers open AND both slots filled AND all upright, checked only at a later action than stage 25. The score advances at most one stage per action and never decreases (high-water mark, not final state). The public page omits the gripper-open requirement for 25/50 and the all-upright requirement for 100. Slot polygons are disjoint for both Standard toaster models (00000: y [-0.041,-0.011] / [0.014,0.039]; 00001: y [-0.051,-0.006] / [0.004,0.049]), so two distinct slices are needed.
findings.evidence: make_toast.py:69-85; reward_manager.py:133-161, 247-279, 323-334, 589-632; func_parser.py:1523-1535; robot_config.yml:15; toaster metadata.json passive.functional for 00000 and 00001; task page Scoring table.
findings.recommendation: Put the exact boolean (key_facts) in the evaluator-only spec and report the stage reached with the action index at which each stage first passed.

findings.title: The 1400-action horizon is tight relative to the LIBERO reference run; pre-register what a horizon failure means
findings.description: 1400 native actions = 56.0 s simulated. The reference uc7.1 LIBERO t6 success used 1187 actions at 20 Hz = 59.35 s simulated for a two-subgoal single-arm task. make_toast needs at least 2 grasps, 2 slot insertions and a lever press, plus homing of both arms. Every uc7.1 hold/observe/finish tick costs native actions. The official Astra-medium campaign scored 0.5 with SR 0 on make_toast (1 seed, 50 episodes per task).
findings.evidence: make_toast.py:15; sim_config.yml:2; arx_x5.yml:10; /workspace/gpt_field/runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/results_summary.json (steps 1187, task_success true) and trial/summary.json (client_task_prompt 'put the white mug on the plate and put the chocolate pudding to the right of the plate'); UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:28 (LIBERO uncapped); report chunk Gpt6AstraEvalPage-C9ed2XQm.js make_toast row ('GPT-6-Astra' score .5, sr 0) and Figure 1 caption ('1 seed, 50 episodes per task').
findings.recommendation: State in the launch preview that horizon exhaustion is a likely outcome, that it counts as a benchmark failure, and that partial stage and action index are the informative signals. Keep the plan's ban on extending the horizon.

findings.title: Pin and verify the layout-0 identity concretely
findings.description: layoutID0 resolves to Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/arx_x5/0/make_toast_0.json. At HF dataset main sha 269457a3b42d8d0ae69898a601f2c1487c2f826e (lastModified 2026-10-22) it has LFS sha256 f78afb3f82b6d9ce2399b13a8ce8a1508134565e7e8cd97f8a8532854fbc0b28 and 8679 bytes. It holds toaster model 00001 at (0.2537, -0.0769, 0.845) with yaw about -82 deg, bread_shelf at (-0.3392, -0.0222, 0.8031) and 4 breads on shelf slots 0-3. Standard poses are fixed by the saved JSON and replayed (not sampled at reset); the xlim/ylim/rotate ranges in make_toast.yml are generator parameters. init_assets.sh tracks unpinned `main`.
findings.evidence: seed_manager.py:32-43; eval_env.py:137, 229-231; scene_manager.py:194-221; rigid.py:218-222 (`set_local_pose(translation=self.default_pos, orientation=self.default_ori)`); HF tree API listing of Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/arx_x5/0 (70 standard, 45 random); downloaded make_toast_0.json; init_assets.sh:15.
findings.recommendation: Freeze HF revision 269457a3 (or the revision actually installed), verify make_toast_0.json's LFS hash, and keep the complete make_toast_*.json set for seed 0 so ID-to-file mapping matches the official enumeration.

findings.title: Each native joint action must carry both arms; the inactive-arm hold is the adapter's job
findings.description: In joint mode take_action_batch reads action[...] for every target robot, so an action naming one arm raises KeyError. 'One active arm while the other holds' must re-send the idle arm's hold target and gripper in every native action. Interpolation re-anchors each action to the measured joint state. In EE mode, an IK failure silently leaves that arm on its previous command while still consuming an action.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:377-406 (joint branch iterates both target robots: `control_info[key_name] = {"position": action[key_name]}`), 407-423 (EE branch; `if ik_result["status"] == "Success"`), 517-530; control_manager.py:88-94 (missing keys filled from prev_control).
findings.recommendation: Add a contract test that every submitted native action contains left/right arm_joint_state and ee_joint_state, and that the inactive arm's target equals its last command.

findings.title: Native observation 'state' gripper value is the last commanded target, not a measured reading
findings.description: obs_manager fills state/action *_ee_joint_state from control_manager.prev_control, i.e. the last commanded (rate-limited) gripper value normalized to [0,1], not the measured finger joints. INPUT_CONTRACT requires measured and derived values to be labeled.
findings.evidence: obs_manager.py:185-211 (`for key, data in self.robot_manager.control_manager.prev_control[env_idx].items(): ... obs[env_idx]["state"][key] = [val]`); arm joints are measured (obs_manager.py:168-174).

findings.description: Full success needs toaster joint_1 ratio > 0.85 at the same action boundary as both arms being home. If the prismatic lever had a return drive, success would be impossible without holding it. The USD crate tokens are compressed, so limits and DriveAPI could not be read here. Non-zero full-success rates of trained policies in the report suggest the lever stays down.

key_facts: FULL SUCCESS (one boolean, evaluated after each action's 10th substep): success(t) <=> [EXISTS bread b in {bread_0..3}: root_xy(b) covered by polygon of toast_slot1's 4 functional points AND 0.03 < z_root(b) - z_slot1_point < 0.065] AND [same for toast_slot2] AND [FOR ALL 4 breads: some local axis in {+x,-x,+y,-y} within < 30 deg of world +z] AND [count of breads with root_xy inside bread_shelf bbox polygon AND root_z > shelf z_min == 2 exactly] AND [toaster joint_1 (tag toast_botton) (q-lower)/(upper-lower) > 0.85] AND [for BOTH arms: |dx|,|dy|,|dz| <= 0.15 m AND rotation <= 20 deg between current link6 pose and link6 pose recorded at end of reset]. Gripper state is not part of success. Sources: make_toast.py:25-67; func_parser.py:2219-2301, 1048-1124, 996-1018, 2581-2592, 168-204, 1776-1808, 1631-1644, 32-59; transformer.py:21-25, 72-78; robot_config.yml:4 (ee_link link6).

NESTING: rm.check(list) appends one stage (reward_manager.py:64-66). step() ANDs the top-level items (reward_manager.py:383-387). Each item goes through check_once(op='or'): a list = OR over its elements; a nested list inside an OR = AND; inside an AND = OR (reward_manager.py:247-279). The stage pops when all pass at one action (388-389). get_reward returns 1.0 when check/final/trigger lists are empty (527-543).
Initial bread orientation (layout JSON default_ori w=0.7016,x=0.0880,y=0.7016,z=-0.0880) puts local -x at 0.00 deg from +z, so slices start upright and pass the axis check; slices lying flat fail it.

TERMINATION: success latches immediately. is_episode_end sets end_flag and success on reward > 1-1e-3 (eval_env.py:854-857); later take_action calls are skipped (eval_env.py:368-369); success cannot revert. Failure only at take_action_cnt >= 1400 or if success was set False externally (eval_env.py:845-860). There is no native done/end signal; WsModelClient.trial_end exists but EvalEnv never calls it.

HAZARD: success defaults True (eval_env.py:114,218), and run_eval scores self.success without checking end_flag (eval_env.py:795-803). An early return from eval_one_episode counts as success unless marked failed, as the reference does at XPolicyLab inspect/deploy.py:331-351.

HORIZON: step_lim = 1400 (make_toast.py:15); skip if take_action_cnt == step_lim, else +1 per action dict (eval_env.py:368-371); success is checked before the step-limit failure on the 1400th action (eval_env.py:854-860). No off-by-one. 1400 actions = 14,000 physics steps = 56.0 s simulated.

SCORE: score_mode 'transition', [25, 50] (make_toast.py:69-85). Stage 25 = both grippers normalized opening >= 0.8 (joint >= 0.0332 m in scale [-0.01, 0.044]) AND (slot1 filled OR slot2 filled) AND all 4 breads upright. Stage 50 = grippers open AND slot1 AND slot2 AND all upright, checked only after stage 25 passed at an earlier action. One advance per action; never decreases, so it is a high-water mark (reward_manager.py:323-334, 589-632). Episode score = 1.0 if success else stage/100 (eval_env.py:799-806). Benchmark score = total_score/eval_time*100 (eval_env.py:827-830).

TIMING: dt 0.004 s, decimation 1, render_interval 10 (sim_config.yml:1-3); collect_freq 25 (arx_x5.yml:10), so collect_interval 10 (obs_manager.py:43-48). Each action = 10 physics substeps: 8 linear-interpolation substeps (alpha = i/9) from MEASURED joints to target, then 2 hold substeps (eval_env.py:500-530). The gripper is also limited to <= 20% of its range per substep from the measured value (control_manager.py:22-34). No rendering during substeps (eval_env.py:638-642). Reward/score sampled once per action after the last substep (eval_env.py:457,465).

PRE-EPISODE (not counted; take_action_cnt zeroed at eval_env.py:220, incremented only at 371): reload 1 rendered step (scene_manager.py:188), TaskEnv.reset 300 unrendered steps (task_env.py:87-88), apply_saved_poses 20+20 steps (scene_manager.py:206-221), stability check 300 steps with 30deg/4cm vs first pose and 10deg/4cm over last 100 steps (layout_manager.py:620-677; failure raises UnStableError at eval_env.py:254-255), 10 renders (eval_env.py:256-257), 200-step settle with capture every 5 (eval_env.py:258-262). Total 841 physics steps (3.36 s). Then set_origin_endpose, set_robot_init_state (grippers commanded to 0.044 = open), reward init_state recording the origin EE poses, model_client.call('reset') (eval_env.py:241-245).

WAITING/TIMEOUTS: no wall-clock limit in eval_env.py/main.py. Physics does not advance while the policy computes; env.render() does not step physics (render_sync.py:24-25; IsaacLab simulation_context.py:616-627). WsModelClient request_timeout_s defaults to 120 s (protocol/client.py:91) and is not overridden (eval_env.py:188-196); a timeout is a fatal WsError (client.py:520-530) that main.py turns into 'consume layout, start next' (main.py:378-399, 434-442). Keepalive 20 s/20 s pings are handled off-thread (model_client.py:16-20; model_server.py:393).

OBSERVATION: the native obs has no step counter, remaining steps or step limit: keys vision/state/action/data_format_version/additional_info{frequency}/instruction plus env_idx (obs_manager.py:95-108; eval_env.py:283). The remaining-step field exists only in XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF (inspect/deploy.py:166,171-186; prompted at inspect/policy.py:1412-1418). The native gripper 'state' is the last commanded value (obs_manager.py:185-211).
INSTRUCTION: exactly 'Pick up two slices of bread, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.' (make_toast.py:87-88; desc_manager.py:45-73; matches the official task page).

LAYOUTS: Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/<config_name arx_x5>/<--seed>/<task>_<n>.json, sorted by n, layout_id = enumeration index (seed_manager.py:32-43). Assets come from HF dataset RoboDojo-Benchmark/RoboDojo at unpinned main (init_assets.sh:14-16,101-106); main sha today 269457a3b42d8d0ae69898a601f2c1487c2f826e. Seed dir 0 holds 70 standard (make_toast_0..69) and 45 random files; seed dirs 0,1,2 exist. Layout 0 = make_toast_0.json (LFS sha256 f78afb3f82b6d9ce2399b13a8ce8a1508134565e7e8cd97f8a8532854fbc0b28, 8679 B; toaster model 00001 at (0.2537,-0.0769,0.845), shelf at (-0.3392,-0.0222,0.8031)). Poses are replayed from the JSON, not sampled (eval_env.py:137,229-231; scene_manager.py:194-221; rigid.py:218-222). eval_nums 25 = the first 25 VALID layouts in order; unstable or exception layouts are skipped and replaced (main.py:353-442).

TASK OVERRIDES via process_config for make_toast: enabled_self_collisions=False for both arms, PhysX enable_stabilization=True (data_source teleop), eval_num 25, render_interval 10 unchanged, EVAL_NUM env var can lower eval_num (pipeline_utils.py:70-110; _task.yml:67-70; main.py:328-334). The PhysX warning monitor is enabled because make_toast.yml has an Articulation section (main.py:85-100,111).

AUTO-RETRY PATHS in the native harness: UnStableError leads to the next layout (main.py:376-377); a generic exception leads to the next layout (378-399); PhysXBroken abandons and refills (372-374, 401-432); PhysXFatal re-execs up to 3 times (main.py:10, 211-238); bash retries up to 10 (eval_policy.sh:142-185). Single-layout pinning in the reference: run_robodojo_layout_range.sh:2-9,160-192,217-218 (manifest abandons other IDs, --eval-num count).

GO-HOME: the native harness has no automatic go-home, final hold or grace period (eval_env.py:841-867). The official reference expects the policy to return home itself and tells the model: XPolicyLab GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/docs.py:71-75 and the default-on recipe (inspect/policy.py:880-902; recipes/make_toast.md:24). The public task page Scoring row 100 also says 'the robot returns to origin'.

REFERENCE CALIBRATION: official Astra report table, make_toast row: GPT-6-Astra Score 0.5, SR 0 (medium effort, recipe on, 1 seed x 50 episodes per task). Trained VLAs reach non-zero SR (Xiaomi-Robotics-1 5.335, GalaxeaVLA 3.33), so full native success is attainable. Reference harness defaults: effort medium, 100 LLM calls per episode, 90 s planner hard timeout (inspect/policy.py:160-161; run_fixed_layout.sh:26,31).

Random variant differences: toaster models [2,4] (vs [0,1]), z range (-0.05, 0.068) (vs (0.03, 0.065)), 15 clutter objects plus ProhibitedArea; scoring and success code otherwise shared (make_toast_random.py:9-10; make_toast_random.yml:15,117-132).

verdicts.corrected_statement: Native full success is the AND of: both slots filled, all four slices upright, exactly two slices left on the shelf, lever ratio > 0.85, and both arms' link6 within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of the pose captured at the end of reset. The instruction does not mention returning to origin. Spontaneous success is very unlikely but not impossible. From the URDF, the zero-joint origin link6 is about (+-0.30, -0.352, 0.921) m with the tool axis along world +y. The layout-0 toaster and bread_0 roots lie 0.275 m and 0.315 m further along +y. So after the instructed work, each arm must deliberately retreat at least about 0.13-0.17 m in y and undo any top-down reorientation to within 20 deg. The qualitative conditions are public (task page, Scoring row 100), and the reference adapter sends them by default. The numbers appear only in source code and in the reference's embodiment notes. The report does not say whether its campaign ran with the recipe on; on is only the adapter default. The user must choose before implementation: (a) add the public task-page Description/Scoring text as a disclosed, versioned extra input; or (b) keep instruction-only and pre-register a primary outcome that does not depend on uninstructed homing.

verdicts.corrected_statement: Native success defaults to True and is flipped only inside is_episode_end, on reward of about 1 (success) or at the step limit / external failure. run_eval scores self.success with no end_flag check. Any early return from the episode function is therefore recorded as success: score 1.0 and a _success video. The live early-return paths in this plan are a user stop at a feedback boundary, immediate error finalization and any adapter-side termination. A model 'finish' is not one of them in a faithful port, because uc7.1's finish is a one-step hold that never ends the episode.
verdicts.reasoning:
How success is set and scored:
- eval_env.py:114 and 218 set `self.success = [True] * self.num_envs`.
- is_episode_end (845-860) sets success False only when take_action_cnt >= step_lim or when success was already set False externally.
- reward_manager sets it False only on query overflow (reward_manager.py:294-296, 373-374); make_toast has no query.
- run_eval: exist_envs is taken before the episode (775), eval_one_episode runs (783), then `if self.success[env_idx]:` adds total_score += 1.0, episode_score = 1.0, tag 'success' (795-803). Videos are named _<cam>_success (921-925).

The reference guards against this: XPolicyLab inspect/deploy.py:331-351 (_mark_incomplete_episode_failed sets success False and calls is_episode_end), used at 713-714.

The plan's user-stop and error-finalization paths (PLAN.md:118) are exactly early-return paths. PLAN.md:94 states the principle ('successful process exit is not full task success') but not the mechanism.

Minor overstatement: 'model finish' is not an early-return path. In uc7.1, observe/finish become a relative zero motion with steps=1 (src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent.py:361-367) followed by a new model call (agent.py:405-406).

verdicts.corrected_statement: This applies only if the Astra model process is placed behind RoboDojo's native WsModelClient/XPolicyLab websocket. In that case every model call is cut at the 120 s default, and that timeout is fatal for the trial; under native main.py the run then moves to the next layout. uc7.1's 180 s per-send deadline, plus overload/transient retries with backoffs of up to 60 s, can exceed 120 s even though typical uc7.1 request cycles were well under that (at most about 81 s in t6). The plan leaves the IPC unspecified. It must choose LLM-in-env-client (as the reference does), its own IPC, or an overridden request_timeout_s recorded as a harness deviation.
verdicts.reasoning:
Where the 120 s comes from:
- eval_env.py:188-196 passes only url, ids and the ws_ping_* settings.
- XPolicyLab client_server/ws/model_client.py:53-71 keeps the config default when a value is None.
- client_server/ws/protocol/client.py:91 sets `request_timeout_s: float = 120.0`.
- PolicyEvalClient.call passes no timeout_s, so request() uses the config value (client.py:520).
- A timeout raises WsError(TIMEOUT) with the comment 'callers must treat a timeout as fatal for the trial' (523-530). That reaches main.py's generic exception path (378-399, 434-442).

Keepalive is not the issue: pings are handled on a background loop thread (model_client.py:16-20), and the server runs methods via asyncio.to_thread (model_server.py:393).

The reference avoids the problem:
- README.md:11: 'The eval client is where the LLM runs'.
- model.py:1-7 is a no-op server.
- run_fixed_layout.sh:31 sets L4_INSPECT_HARD_TIMEOUT_S 90.

The plan separates the processes (PLAN.md:72) and keeps the 180 s deadline and retries (PLAN.md:116). UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:33 defines 180 s per HTTP open plus full SSE. Lines 158-168 allow up to 3 sends for the overload class and 2 transient retries counted independently, with backoff of up to 60 s each.

In t6, cumulative budget.elapsed_s ran from 70.3 s at request 1 to 724.9 s at request 14, so each cycle (including local control) was at most about 81 s.

The risk is conditional but concrete. Severity stays major because one slow decision would kill the attempt and, via NT-2, could start another layout.

[major][feasibility, horizon/episode loop] The likely post-'done' phase is not bounded in model calls or wall time.
- In uc7.1, 'observe' and 'finish' each run a 1-step zero motion and then request a new model decision (src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent.py:361-367 `"steps": 1`; 405-406 `_need_agent = True`). finish 'never ends the episode or sets success' (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent_client.py:173-176).
- Under the plan, each tick costs one native action and simulation is frozen while waiting on Astra (PLAN.md:98). There is no model-call or wall-time cap (PLAN.md:21, 100).
- The native episode ends only at full success or action 1400 (eval_env.py:845-860). Full success also needs the uninstructed return-home (NT-1).
- The probable sequence is therefore: Astra completes the instructed goal, declares completion, and keeps observing, finishing or making small corrections until action 1400. In the worst case that is one Astra-high call per remaining action.
- t6 averaged about 52 s per request cycle (trial/requests/000014-...result.json budget.elapsed_s 724.86 over 14 requests). For example, 500 remaining actions could mean up to about 500 subscription calls, or about 7 h.
- In LIBERO this phase was rare because instruction = goal. The LIBERO protocol also forbids adding automatic stall cutoffs (UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:153).
The plan should pre-register how this phase is handled: for example, an operator stop at a feedback boundary with the NT-3 failure marking, triggered by an evaluator-only 'instructed goal achieved' flag. It should also state the expected call and time exposure before approval.

[major][decision needed, horizon] The native horizon is likely binding, and Astra will not be told about it.
- The LIBERO uc7.1 t6 run needed 1187 policy steps at 20 Hz (results_summary.json 'steps': 1187; protocol line 22 'OSC_POSE, 20 Hz'), i.e. 59.35 s simulated, for two pick-and-places ('put the white mug on the plate and put the chocolate pudding to the right of the plate').
- Native make_toast allows 1400 actions x 10 substeps x 0.004 s = 56.0 s (make_toast.py:15; env_cfg/sim/sim_config.yml:1-3; env_cfg/arx_x5.yml collect_freq 25). That has to cover two thin-slice grasps, two slot insertions inside a 0.03-0.065 m height window (make_toast.py:9-10), a lever press and, for full success, both arms returning home.
- PLAN.md:86 keeps uc7.1 control limits in physical units, so motion time per task is comparable. uc7.1 also budgets about 190 control steps for one native-macro calibration (agent_client.py:158-159).
- uc7.1 prompts contain no episode step-limit wording (grep of the client), and the LIBERO protocol used no cap (protocol line 28).
- INPUT_CONTRACT.md:24 withholds the remaining budget. The reference reports it each turn because 'until it is reported the model has no way to know it exists' (XPolicyLab inspect/policy.py:1412-1418; inspect/deploy.py:166, 171-186).
This is the same parity dilemma as NT-1: LIBERO had no limit, so it had nothing to report. The user should decide whether to state the fixed 1400-action / 56 s limit (a static public benchmark fact) or to pre-register horizon exhaustion as a likely outcome that says little about ability.

[minor][feasibility, reset] Model-free native resets through EvalEnv still need a running websocket policy server.
- EvalEnv.__init__ raises if deploy_cfg has no port (eval_env.py:178-180).
- It constructs WsModelClient, which connects with a handshake at construction (XPolicyLab client_server/ws/model_client.py:80-81). PolicyEvalClientConfig retries 180 x 5 s, capped at 900 s, before raising (protocol/client.py:98-108).
- Every reset calls model_client.call('reset') (eval_env.py:245).
PLAN.md:68 and :108 call for 'model-free' resets with 'no credentials or model transport'. Bypassing EvalEnv would drop the native setup_scene stability check, 200-step settle and origin capture (eval_env.py:238-262), which PLAN.md:108 says to preserve. The plan should specify one of two options and hash it into the preview/approval binding: a credential-free no-op ws stub (the reference ships one: GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/model.py:1-7, 'No-op policy-server model'), or a reviewed EvalEnv subclass that replaces the client.

dims.title: Native robot, camera, observation and action interface

result.dimension: Native robot, camera, observation and action interface (RoboDojo f57e1633 + XPolicyLab 5d0be149 + HF asset pack main@269457a3)

claims.claim: Official arx_x5 / dual_x5 configuration with head, left-wrist and right-wrist RGB cameras
claims.evidence: env_cfg/arx_x5.yml:3-7 (scene default, robot dual_x5, camera camera_config); env_cfg/camera/camera_config.yml:7-37 (cam_head, cam_left_wrist, cam_right_wrist, rgb annotators only); wrist cameras are generated from the X5 embodiment entry 'cam_wrist' and renamed cam_left_wrist (robot0) / cam_right_wrist (robot1) in env/robot_manager/robot_manager.py:464-476; HF Assets/Robots/x5/robot_config.yml:20-27.

claims.claim: Native ARX has six arm joints plus a gripper per arm
claims.evidence: Action space is 6 + 1 per arm (env_cfg/robot/_robot_info.json:3-4 arm_dim [6,6], ee_dim [1,1]). Physically each arm has TWO independently simulated prismatic finger joints joint7/joint8 (HF X5A.urdf:252-287, 0-0.044 m along +/-y of link6; robot_config.yml:8 gripper_joints_name ['joint7','joint8']; robot_config/x5.py:31-32,46-51 both PD-actuated). The native observation's single gripper value is command-derived, not measured (obs_manager.py:185-207).

claims.claim: 25 Hz control on 250 Hz physics; each counted action expands to 10 physics substeps; 1400 actions = ~56 simulated seconds
claims.evidence: env_cfg/sim/sim_config.yml:1-2 (decimation 1, dt 0.004); arx_x5.yml:10 (collect_freq 25); obs_manager.py:43-48 collect_interval = 1/(dt*freq) = 10; eval_env.py:500-504 interpolation_nums = collect_interval; eval_env.py:638-642 one sim_step per control step; eval_env.py:368-371 take_action_cnt += 1 per action dict; task/RoboDojo/tasks/make_toast.py:15 step_lim 1400 -> 1400 x 0.04 s = 56 s.

claims.claim: Commands can be routed through the native action path, preserving its interpolation/hold schedule and end-of-action reward sampling
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:475-560: per action, substeps 1-8 interpolate linearly from the MEASURED joint position to the target (alpha=(i+1)/9), substeps 9-10 hold the target; gripper interpolated the same way then clamped per substep to +/-20% of range around measured joint7 (control_manager.py:22-34); velocity target is 0 (control_manager.py:13-20, robot_manager.py:382-405). Reward/success sampled after every action (eval_env.py:457,465,841-867). Joint-mode actions must contain both arms' arm and gripper keys (eval_env.py:377-400 index action[key_name] for every target robot).

claims.claim: The simulation can be frozen while awaiting Astra or approval
claims.evidence: Physics advances only inside take_action/step and reset (eval_env.py:446-452, 638-642; task_env.py:87-88). Rendering does not step physics: render_sync.py:25 'env.render() does not advance physics'; IsaacLab fork afca7b09 source/isaaclab/isaaclab/sim/simulation_context.py:625-627 sets /app/player/playSimulations False around app.update(). No extra pause mechanism is needed, but the adapter must not call take_action while waiting.

claims.claim: The adapter must implement robot-only IK/differential kinematics; the native stack does not provide an equivalent
claims.evidence: Native eval also accepts an EE mode: left_ee_pose/right_ee_pose [x,y,z,qw,qx,qy,qz] (link6 flange, env frame) solved per action by CuRobo IK (eval_env.py:337-352, 407-424; robot_manager.py:325-338). On IK failure the arm key is omitted and control_manager.py:88-94 silently re-uses the previous arm command while the step is still counted. The reference Astra adapter rejects this mode (XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/deploy.py:191-198). A URDF (HF Assets/Robots/x5/X5A.urdf, 9,218 B) and CuRobo yml exist, so adapter-owned IK is feasible and is the better choice.

claims.claim: CuRobo may be used if it reads only permitted robot/static inputs
claims.evidence: CuroboPlanner (MotionPlanner, BatchMotionPlanner(10), IK) is always built at env init for robot type x5 (robot_manager.py:51-52, 539-550), so it is an evaluation-time dependency. Its world is a single hard-coded 3.0x3.0x0.05 m table cuboid whose top is at world z 0.74, i.e. 2.5 cm below the 0.765 table top (curobo_planner.py:486-503; table_height = 0.74 - 0.765 at robot_manager.py:548; table top 0.765 per XPolicyLab pose.py:55-57). It has robot self-collision spheres for 9 links and none for the fingers (HF curobo_tmp.yml:6-15). There is no object geometry and no world update. The table plane is static scene knowledge that the uc7.1 controller lacks (no table terms in agent_speedup_v2_user_check_{control,motion,fragments}.py).

claims.claim: Camera intrinsics can be computed for the delivered pixels
claims.evidence: Intrinsics and extrinsics are not delivered by default (arx_x5.yml:17-18 false). The RoboDojo helper derives K from config with fy=fx and a centred principal point (camera_manager.py:454-467). Head Gemini_345Lg: 640x480, f 10, h_ap 22.212, v_ap 14.266 (env_cfg/camera/template.py:1-7). These apertures are inconsistent: aperture aspect 1.557 vs pixel aspect 1.333, and both are set with maintain_square_pixels=False (camera_manager.py:329-332). fx = 288.13 px, while fy is 288.13 (square pixels) or 336.46 (from v_ap). The wrist d435 is consistent: fx = fy = 397.04 px (template.py:15-21).

claims.claim: One world frame can be defined
claims.evidence: *_ee_pose positions are relative to the env origin, with world-axis orientation (robot_manager.py:140-170). get_camera_extrinsics returns camera-to-WORLD poses in USD camera axes (camera_manager.py:469-491). num_envs is forced to 1 when eval_batch is false (main.py:318-326), so env_0's origin is expected at (0,0,0). This must be verified at runtime (scene.env_origins) and recorded.

claims.claim: The head camera can define the shared directions; external_view_v1 is maintained with the new calibration
claims.evidence: cam_head has no mount_link, so it is a static prim /World/envs/env_0/Camera_<i> (camera_config.yml:32-37; camera_manager.py:197-201) with no randomization config. Pose (0,-0.41,1.308), Euler XYZ-intrinsic (30,0,0) (utils/rotations.py:6-38). Offline: optical axis (0,0.5,-0.866), image-right = world +X, roll 0 deg. The external_view_v1 frame is computed generically from rotation_world_from_camera (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_spatial.py:195-211), using the same x-right/y-up/-z-forward convention as USD. Result: right_xy=(1,0), away_xy=(0,1). Unlike LIBERO's robot-facing agentview, 'behind' here means away from the robots.

claims.claim: Each wrist transform must be derived from its mount and the current robot pose
claims.evidence: The wrist camera xform is created as a child of /World/envs/env_0/robot{0|1}/camera (robot_manager.py:438-440; camera_manager.py:192-196). The camera link is fixed to link6 via hand_to_camera_mount and camera_joint (HF X5A.urdf:202-228), with local pose [0,0,0.001] and Euler XYZ [0,-80,-90] (robot_config.yml:20-27). Offline FK at home puts the camera about 0.085 m ahead of and 0.051 m above the link6 origin, with the optical axis 30 deg below the tool axis. The pose can come either from the prim (get_world_pose) or from the observed link6 pose plus the fixed mount.

claims.claim: No depth, point cloud or segmentation is in the native observation
claims.evidence: camera_config.yml:1-30 enables only rgb annotators (distance_to_image_plane is commented out); arx_x5.yml:15-16 depth false, approximate_depth false; obs_manager.py:139-148 adds depth only if that annotator exists. Each image is uint8 RGB (480,640,3), cropped from RGBA (obs_manager.py:122-129; camera_view.py:17-18).

claims.claim: The full URDF/kinematics and complete joint limits stay inside the controller
claims.evidence: The URDF limits are placeholders: +/-10 rad for joints 1-5 and +/-3.14 for joint6 (HF X5A.urdf:54,83,112,141,170,199). CuRobo uses that URDF with position_limit_clip 0 (curobo_tmp.yml:434,499). The reference reads the real limits from the live articulation, asset.data.soft_joint_pos_limits and joint_vel_limits (inspect/deploy.py:229,235), and uses the URDF only offline (278-289). USD limits (ARX.usd, binary crate) are unverified here.

claims.claim: robot_self_collision is false for make_toast; preserve and disclose it
claims.evidence: task/RoboDojo/config/_task.yml:67-70. utils/pipeline_utils.py:105-107 sets enabled_self_collisions False per robot, and robot_manager.py:614-621 applies it to each arm's PhysX articulation (default True at robot_config/x5.py:17). The flag affects intra-articulation link pairs only. The two arms are separate articulations (dual_x5.yml coupled False; robot_manager.py:493-500), and no inter-robot collision filtering was found, so arm-arm and arm-environment contacts are still simulated (inferred; verify).

claims.claim: The upstream reference policy exposes a remaining-step field that must not be forwarded
claims.evidence: XPolicyLab inspect/deploy.py:166 remaining_steps=_remaining_env_steps(task_env) and :171-186; inspect/policy.py:1412-1418 appends 'Env steps remaining before the episode ends'. The native obs dict has no such field (obs_manager.py:95-220).

claims.claim: Native reset preparation: saved-layout stability check, 10 render passes, 200-step setup_scene loop, plus preceding preparation
claims.evidence: task_env.py:83-90: reload_scene, robot reset, 300 physics steps (render False), camera reset (+1 step at camera_manager.py:452), capture re-init. eval_env.py:247-264: apply_saved_poses, check_layout_stability, 10 renders, 200 sim_steps with obs every 5. Then origin capture and init state (eval_env.py:241-243). That is at least 501 physics steps, about 2.0 s, before action 1.

claims.claim: The exact native gen_instruction is the observed instruction
claims.evidence: desc_manager.py:41-48 builds obs['instruction'] from env.gen_instruction templates. The make_toast template has no <label> placeholders: 'Pick up two slices of bread, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.' (make_toast.py:87-88).

claims.claim: Seed-directory 0 / layoutID 0 is an existing official layout
claims.evidence: seed_manager.py:32-45 maps layout id to the sorted index of Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/<config_name>/<seed>/make_toast_<N>.json. HF dataset main@269457a3 has dirs arx_x5/0,1,2, and make_toast_0.json exists (8,679 B, sha256 f78afb3f82b6d9ce2399b13a8ce8a1508134565e7e8cd97f8a8532854fbc0b28). Files _1, _2, _24, _25, _49 and _50 also exist.

claims.claim: A finger sign/range audit is required when porting uc7.1
claims.evidence: The LIBERO uc7.1 request (runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/trial/requests/000002-ee86fcebbe99489586c8bab7fdeb0ab0.request.json, context.capabilities.direct_motion) has gripper_open=0, gripper_closed=1. RoboDojo is the inverse: 1 = open (0.044 m), 0 = closed (-0.01 m target). See eval_env.py:387-400 with sign 1 and scale [-0.01,0.044] (HF robot_config.yml:12-15), and XPolicyLab docs.py:50.

claims.claim: The native camera dimensions differ from 512x512, so a padded/rescaled canvas would be needed
claims.evidence: All three cameras render 640x480 (template.py:2,16). LIBERO delivered native 512x512 with no crop (request geometry.image width/height 512, source_transform 'raw_mujoco_rgb_vertical_flip_no_crop').

findings.title: Gripper channels misdescribed: the native gripper 'state' is a clamped last command, two measured finger joints exist, and holds must re-send the requested command
findings.description: The plan assumes one gripper channel per arm ('Never fabricate a second measured finger sensor'). The native obs scalar <arm>_ee_joint_state is not a measurement. It is the normalized gripper target applied at the last physics substep, which is clamped to within +/-20% of range (0.0108 m) of measured joint7. When the jaw is blocked by bread it reads up to 0.2 below the true opening. The simulator has two genuinely measured prismatic finger joints per arm (joint7, joint8). LIBERO uc7.1 sent two measured finger joints, a finger gap, joint velocities and the last gripper command. The native obs has none of these, so the 'same type of info' requirement can only be met by reading them from the articulation. Holds matter here. Every joint-mode action must carry both arms' arm and gripper keys, so the inactive arm's hold is re-sent every tick. Upstream found that echoing the observed gripper value lets a grasped object slide out. Layout 0 probably needs a cross-arm transfer (NI-10), so this hold path will be exercised.
findings.evidence: env/observation_manager/obs_manager.py:185-207 (state[...ee_joint_state] from control_manager.prev_control, normalized); env/robot_manager/control_manager.py:22-34 (gripper_eps 0.2 clamp around measured joint7); eval_env.py:377-400 (both arms' keys indexed); HF Assets/Robots/x5/robot_config.yml:8-15 (joint7/joint8, mimic [joint8,1,0], scale [-0.01,0.044]); X5A.urdf:252-287; robot_config/x5.py:31-32,46-51; XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/policy.py:626-634: 'RoboDojo reports <arm>_ee_joint_state from the previous command after its 20%-of-range clamp, not from the finger position, so re-sending it parks the jaw ... the object slides out of a closed hand during the next transfer'; LIBERO request 000002 text fields finger_joints_m (2), finger_gap_mm, joint_velocity_rad_s (7), last_gripper_command; func_parser.py:1523-1535 (evaluator uses the measured joint mean).
findings.recommendation: Define the ARX state schema explicitly. Measured: joint1-6 position and velocity, joint7 and joint8 positions (m) read from articulation data. Derived: a jaw gap from a mesh-based formula (see NI-8). Command: the last requested gripper command (open/close or 0..1). Optionally include the native applied-target scalar, labelled 'applied target (clamped), not measured'. For the inactive arm, re-send the last commanded joint target and the last REQUESTED gripper value, never the observed scalar. Add a model-free hold test that grasps, holds one arm, moves the other, and checks for no slip.

findings.title: uc7.1 fragment parameters cannot be transplanted: ARX tracks about 0.05 rad per action and starts in a folded, near-singular pose
findings.description: Each native action is a 40 ms absolute joint target with zero velocity target. It is interpolated over 8 substeps from the measured joints and then held for 2, under PD stiffness 4400 and damping 40. Upstream measurements show that targets above about 0.05 rad per action do not land. Offline FK at the all-zero home pose (elbow folded, interior angle 24.5 deg) gives TCP position-Jacobian singular values of 0.599, 0.306 and 0.041 m/rad, weakest along world +Y (forward). Forward motion is therefore limited to about 2 mm per action at 0.05 rad until the elbow unfolds. uc7.1's transit step of 0.02 m per tick at 20 Hz (0.016 m per action at the same speed) would need roughly 0.4-0.5 rad per action in that direction, about 8-10x the clean ceiling. Contact steps, arrival tolerances, stall windows (12/16 steps, 0.8 mm) and minimum gripper steps (close 12, open 8 at 20 Hz) were all tuned for OSC at 20 Hz. The ARX jaw covers its full range in about 4-6 actions. The 1400-action cap is 56 s simulated, while the LIBERO t6 uc7.1 run used 1187 steps at 20 Hz (about 59 s), so slow tracking eats directly into a binding horizon.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:475-531; control_manager.py:13-20; robot_manager.py:382-405; robot_config/x5.py:24-30 (home joints 0), 37-51 (4400/40, velocity_limit_sim 5); XPolicyLab inspect/deploy.py:64-81 ('under 1% of moves land more than 100 mm off target up to 0.054 rad per step, 62% miss at 0.081 and 88% at 0.108, so 0.05 is the last measured-clean value'; gripper full range in four env steps); EEF policy.py:32-49; embodiment_docs.py:29-34 (folded at all-zero joints); offline numpy FK from HF X5A.urdf (TCP 0.1501 m) by this reviewer; agent_speedup_v2_user_check_fragments.py:25-43; results_summary.json steps 1187; make_toast.py:15.
findings.recommendation: Before freezing the controller, add a model-free ARX tracking characterization: per-joint step response at 25 Hz, landing error against delta-q per action, jaw open/close time, and conditioning along typical paths from home. Clamp delta-q to about 0.05 rad per action per joint, use damped least squares near the fold, and re-derive per-tick translation and rotation caps, arrival tolerances, stall thresholds and minimum gripper steps in 25 Hz native-action units. Record every conversion in the adapter diff and preflight.

findings.title: The native eval loop would run extra episodes, swap layouts on faults or exceptions, and self-restart, which breaks the single-attempt guarantee
findings.description: The plan's single-use supervisor guard works at process level, but RoboDojo's own main loop retries and substitutes layouts inside the process. By default it runs eval_nums=25 sequential layouts. On a PhysX break it abandons the seed and refills with the next layout. On UnStableError, or any generic exception (including an adapter error), it moves on to the next layout. On fatal errors it re-execs itself up to 3 times, and eval_policy.sh retries up to 10 times, resuming from a manifest. The PhysX monitor is active for make_toast because its config has an Articulation section. If the implementation drives the episode through main.py or eval_policy.sh, Astra could silently get a second attempt on layout 1, or run after the approved layout was replaced. The plan never mentions this machinery.
findings.evidence: src/eval_client/main.py:10 (MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS=3), 85-121 (monitor for Articulation tasks; make_toast.yml:1), 211-238 (os.execv), 330-334 (EVAL_NUM can only lower eval_num), 353-442 (abandon and refill at 401-432; UnStableError at 376-377; generic exception at 378-399, then next seed); utils/pipeline_utils.py:109 with _task.yml:70 (eval_nums 25); scripts/eval_policy.sh:142-175 (ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES default 10 for rc 99/134/139); eval_env.py:250-255, 671-709 (resume manifest).
findings.recommendation: Use an adapter-owned single-episode driver. It should reproduce main.py's config assembly exactly (process_randomization, process_config, num_envs=1, camera.default_frequency, sim.seed, add_zero_delay_kit_args before AppLauncher, --enable_cameras, kit extensions), call reset(seed=[0]) once, and treat PhysXBroken, PhysXFatal, UnStableError, any exception, or execv as terminal infrastructure failures, with no refill, resume or bash retry. Add a fault-injection test proving no second episode or layout can start.

findings.title: No automated camera-validity checks despite known upstream failures (albedo-less frames, black wrist views, stale frames)
findings.description: Stage A only requires that a render succeeds, and stage E shows images to a human. XPolicyLab documents silent render failures on this stack (Isaac Sim 5.1 / Kit 107). With texture streaming on, frames lose all albedo: grey channels, black white bowls. That shift alone dropped Pi_05 from 6.91% to 1.07%. Tiled wrist cameras under cloned articulations go black for num_envs>1. Captures are one observation stale unless zero-delay Kit settings are active. The pinned RoboDojo eval_policy.sh sets no texture-streaming flag. A model run on such images would fail for reasons unrelated to the agent, and albedo loss is easy to miss by eye.
findings.evidence: XPolicyLab@5d0be149 scripts/robodojo_sim_env.sh:127-134 ('Texture streaming must stay off ... frames with no albedo at all ... dropped Pi_05 from the published 6.91% to 1.07%'), 145 (--/rtx-transient/resourcemanager/enableTextureStreaming=false etc.), 148-153 (wrist views black for num_envs > 1), 227-232 (double-buffered stale frame); RoboDojo render_sync.py:7-26, 50-63, 127-163 (+1 pass if zero-delay inactive; args must be added before AppLauncher); main.py:123-126; scripts/eval_policy.sh:121-131 (KIT_ARGS only enable extensions).
findings.recommendation: Add machine checks to stage A and E, run on all three cameras. Images must be non-black and show per-channel and texture variance, for example the RoboDojo/XPolicyLab robodojo_render_smoke centre_spread criterion. Frames must be fresh: command a known small joint motion and confirm it appears in the very next get_obs. Record the kit args and renderer settings in the config hash, and keep num_envs=1. Treat any failure as an installation result, never an attempt.

findings.title: Native EE mode and CuRobo facts settle the 'prove CuRobo inputs' item: table cuboid present, and IK failures are silent
findings.description: Native *_ee_pose actions are link6 (flange, not TCP) poses in the env frame. CuRobo solves IK per action (32 seeds, 1 mm / 0.02 tolerance, robot self-collision on). On failure the previous arm command is silently held and the step still counts, with no error to feed back. Nothing in the call constrains continuity of successive IK solutions. The CuRobo world is robot spheres plus a hard-coded 3x3x0.05 m table cuboid (top at world z 0.74), with no objects and no fingers. *_tcp_pose and *_delta_ee_pose pass validation but are never executed. Using native CuRobo as-is adds a static table-floor constraint that uc7.1 never had.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:337-352, 371, 407-424, 595-607; control_manager.py:88-94; robot_manager.py:51-52, 325-338, 539-550; env/planner_manager/curobo_planner.py:337-408 (359-363 solve_pose, return_seeds=1), 486-503, 525-539; HF curobo_tmp.yml:6-15, 434, 497-503; XPolicyLab inspect/deploy.py:191-198 (reference rejects the native EE mode).
findings.recommendation: Use action type 'joint' with adapter-owned IK that clamps per step (NI-2) and reports failures explicitly. If CuRobo is used for IK or planning, build it with an empty world, or record the table plane as an explicitly disclosed static non-uc7.1 input with user approval. Do not use the native ee mode.

findings.title: Camera calibration details: head fy is ambiguous, frames are mixed, and the axis convention must be pinned
findings.description: Native K and T are not delivered. The head camera's config apertures do not match its pixel aspect, so fy is either 288.13 px (RoboDojo's square-pixel helper) or 336.46 px (from v_ap). Offline projection puts the difference at up to 33 px vertically at the arm bases and about 12 px at the shelf front edge. Camera extrinsics are world-frame, USD-axis (-Z forward, +Y up) camera-to-world matrices, while ee poses are env-relative. external_view_v1 needs rotation_world_from_camera in the same x-right/y-up convention that LIBERO used. An OpenCV or Isaac 'world'-axes matrix would silently flip directions.
findings.evidence: arx_x5.yml:17-18; camera_manager.py:321-337 (pinhole, no distortion), 454-467, 469-491; template.py:1-7, 15-21; robot_manager.py:140-170; spatial.py:195-211; LIBERO request external rotation_world_from_camera x-column = world +Y (same convention).
findings.recommendation: Derive K for the delivered pixels and validate fx and fy, plus wrist extrinsics, with a robot-only projection test: project FK of link6 and finger links into rendered head and wrist frames, with a pixel-error budget. Freeze the head-camera frame in USD/MuJoCo convention (expected right_xy (1,0), away_xy (0,1), roll 0, not inverted). Record scene.env_origins and convert all poses into one env frame.

findings.title: 512x512 padded canvas vs native 640x480
findings.description: All three native views are 640x480. The plan's preferred aspect-preserving 512x512 canvas means a 0.8 downscale to 512x384 content plus 64 px bands, about 36% fewer pixels and resampled intrinsics. LIBERO parity was native renders with no resampling, and the reference report sends native 640x480 (JPEG q95).
