[major, conditional on LP-1 option A] The plan does not cover a post-completion request loop or the context-token ceiling.
- Native episodes end only on full success or at 1400 actions (upstream src/eval_client/eval_env.py:841-866).
- uc7.1 'finish' and 'observe' are each a 1-step zero-displacement motion that never ends the episode (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent.py:361-364; capabilities.finish 'does not stop the evaluator').
- In t6 a premature finish (request 11) was followed by 3 corrective requests, because a visible error remained.
- In Make Toast with return-home withheld, an instruction-complete agent keeps being re-prompted with no visible error. Each finish/observe costs 1 native action and one request; t6 averaged 28.8 s per request (stream elapsed 402.6 s / 14).
- All text is retained, so t6 input grew about 5.5K tokens per turn (7,145 to 82,735 over 14 requests, server usage). The frozen client raises BudgetExceeded once a request's input exceeds 1,050,000 tokens (astra.py:28, 511-513). That is about 190 turns at t6's rate, fewer with three views and two arms, so it is reached before the horizon whenever turns average under about 7 actions.
- PLAN.md:21/100 bar added call and time caps, and the protocol bars new automatic cutoffs (UC7_1 protocol line 153).
The plan should estimate the request count under the horizon and pre-register the possible terminal causes: horizon, context-ceiling error and user stop. It should also define the operator's response to a post-completion loop.

[minor] The execution system prompt is embodiment-specific but has no contract row. AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent_client.py:51-202) is 10,925 chars, identical in all 14 t6 requests (one sha256, e7d96588...). It hard-codes 'one Franka Panda' (line 52), 'The two images are external and wrist, upright and uncropped' (56-57), '20 Hz' (twice), 'OSC', 'gripper0_grip_site', '0.097 m' and '0.079 m'. LP-6 covers only the planning prompt. INPUT_CONTRACT.md:5-27 has no row for either instruction text, and the plan promises only a generic 'prompt/schema/capability diff' (PLAN.md:58, 127). Add a contract rule: only embodiment and sensor facts change, each replaced by a measured ARX/Isaac value with provenance; the behavioural text is kept verbatim and diffed against the frozen hash.

dims.title: uc7.1 execution-stack portability and horizon feasibility

result.dimension: uc7.1 execution-stack portability to dual ARX, and feasibility within the native 1400-action horizon

claims.claim: take_action_cnt counts each per-environment action dictionary; each action expands into 10 physics substeps (25 Hz control, 0.004 s physics); 1400 actions is about 56 simulated seconds
claims.evidence: Upstream @f57e163: src/eval_client/eval_env.py:368-371 (skip when cnt == step_lim or end_flag, else cnt += 1 per env action); env/observation_manager/obs_manager.py:43-44 collect_interval = 1/(dt*collect_freq) with dt 0.004 (env_cfg/sim/sim_config.yml:2) and collect_freq 25 (env_cfg/arx_x5.yml:10), so 10; eval_env.py:500-504 builds 10 MetaControls, 449-452 steps until the queue is empty, 638-642 one sim_step per pop; task/RoboDojo/tasks/make_toast.py:15 step_lim = 1400. 1400 x 0.04 s = 56 s.

claims.claim: Route commands through the native action path and preserve its interpolation/hold schedule and end-of-action reward-sampling boundaries
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:519-530: the first floor(0.8*10)=8 substeps interpolate linearly from the measured joints to the target and the last 2 hold it. reward_manager.step and is_episode_end run once per action (eval_env.py:457, 465). Success requires reward > 1-1e-3 at that boundary (eval_env.py:854-857).

claims.claim: Native ARX has six arm joints plus a gripper per arm
claims.evidence: env_cfg/robot/_robot_info.json: "arm_dim": [6, 6], "ee_dim": [1, 1]. env/robot_manager/robot_config/x5.py:24-33 lists joint1-6 plus finger joint7/joint8 (both init 0.044), and :38-51 the arm/gripper actuators.

claims.claim: The frozen uc7.1 client, geometry validation, state layout and primitives contain single-Panda assumptions
claims.evidence: contact_skills.py:265-270: StepView requires an 8-D state with gap=(q1-q2)*1000, Panda sign. astranomy_agentic_motion.py:98: Panda closure (q1-q2)/0.08; :28 CONTROL_HZ=20. action.py:16-17, 86-93: robosuite OSC_POSE scaling (0.05 m, 0.5 rad, gripper +/-1). agent_speedup_v2.py:1920: action.shape must be (7,); :1799 Panda RobotModel. agent_client.py:52 says 'one Franka Panda'. robocasa_user_check_geometry.py:59-61 requires cameras exactly {external, wrist} and the Panda gripper contract.

claims.claim: Audit every state8, seven-joint Panda, finger sign/range, grasp-site offset, axis-angle/quaternion and workspace assumption
claims.evidence: All listed assumptions exist. Axis-angle state[3:6]: fragments.py:201. Grip offset 0.097: astranomy_agentic_geometry.py:37 and agent_client.py:196. Panda finger ranges [[0,0.04],[-0.04,0]]: astranomy_agentic_geometry.py:40. JOINT7_LIMIT_RAD: agent_speedup_v2_robot.py:67. Concrete trap: ARX init joint7=joint8=+0.044 (x5.py:31-32), so the Panda formula reads an open ARX gripper as 0 mm gap / closure 1.0. The audit list misses several items: native obs joint/gripper 'state' is the commanded value (F2), the speed mapping (F1), embodiment constants embedded in the prompt (F4), the post-horizon silent no-op and IK-failure hold (F6), and hold re-anchoring (F7).

claims.claim: Start with one active arm per fragment while the other holds its last commanded state
claims.evidence: Feasible, because every native action must carry both arms. eval_env.py:377-445 indexes action[key] for every target robot (a missing key raises KeyError); the allowed keys are at eval_env.py:595-607. But 'last commanded state' differs from uc7.1's hold, which is a zero displacement from the measured pose (agent.py:529-536; fragments.py:157-158 'hold entry pose').

claims.claim: Respect native 250 Hz physics / 25 Hz control instead of transplanting 20 Hz gains, and charge multi-tick fragments one native action per tick
claims.evidence: uc7.1 constants are 20 Hz step counts and caps: fragments.py:22-43, 144 ('control_hz': 20); astranomy_agentic_motion.py:28; agent_client.py:117, 145. LIBERO physics was 500 Hz: t6 trial/summary.json collision.counts.physics_substeps 29675 over 1187 steps, i.e. 25 per step. One native action can command any joint target, interpolated within 8 substeps (eval_env.py:519-530) and limited only by velocity_limit_sim 5 rad/s (x5.py:41), so per-tick charging is required to avoid undercounting.

claims.claim: Before choosing CuRobo or another backend, prove it uses only permitted robot/static robot-calibration inputs
claims.evidence: The native ee-mode IK is CuRobo with a 3x3x0.05 m table cuboid world (env/planner_manager/curobo_planner.py:486-503), table_height=0.74-root_z (env/robot_manager/robot_manager.py:539-551), self-collision and 32 seeds (curobo_planner.py:525-539). It is not robot-only, so the plan's caution is justified.

claims.claim: Freeze simulation while awaiting Astra or approval
claims.evidence: Physics advances only inside take_action -> step (eval_env.py:449-452, 638-642) and setup_scene. If the XPolicyLab websocket contract is used, synchronous model methods run in asyncio.to_thread (XPolicyLab@5d0be14 client_server/ws/model_server.py:390-396), and the client keeps its own event-loop thread for keepalive (client_server/ws/model_client.py:15-20, 75-94). A 180 s Astra wait therefore does not drop the connection.

claims.claim: Preserve ten render passes and the explicit 200-step setup_scene settling loop separately from the 1400-action allowance
claims.evidence: eval_env.py:256-262 runs 10 render() calls and 200 sim_step() physics steps (0.8 s). These are not counted in take_action_cnt, which is reset at eval_env.py:220.

claims.claim: The native horizon differs explicitly from the unlimited LIBERO episodes
claims.evidence: UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:28 sets no total time, action or call cap. :33 says fragment step limits are not episode caps. :45 says uc7.1 adds no uc8 speed changes, so the uc7 runs share uc7.1's motion parameters.

claims.claim: Report: Astra medium by default; the 100-planner-call limit belongs to a robustness ablation
claims.evidence: Report chunk Gpt6AstraEvalPage-C9ed2XQm.js (sha256 3caf165e...) contains 'reasoning effort medium by default, one tool call per turn' and 'Interaction-time robustness uses the same L3 Inspect EEF harness ... and 100 planner calls unless noted'. The harness 'plays the interpolated chunk open-loop at the embodiment control rate (25 Hz on the dual-arm tabletop robot)'.

findings.title: Controller-speed mapping is unspecified and decides whether the 1400-action horizon binds
findings.description: uc7.1 caps each commanded step at 0.02 m (transit) or 0.005 m (contact) per 20 Hz action, but LIBERO's OSC_POSE controller realized only about 25% of each command. In RoboDojo the native path is a stiff joint-position PD (stiffness 4400, damping 40) driven by linear interpolation that reaches the target within 8 of 10 substeps. A per-action cap carried over 'in physical units' would therefore likely be realized almost fully, giving about 0.4-0.5 m/s transit and 0.1-0.125 m/s contact: 4-5x LIBERO's realized 0.1 / 0.024 m/s. Contact and stall behaviour would also change (stall window 16 steps against a stiff position controller). Matching LIBERO's realized speed instead puts the make_toast estimate at about 1.1k-3.3k native actions, against a 1400 cap. The plan says only 'preserve ... limits in physical units' and 'record conversions'. It chooses neither mapping, makes no horizon projection, and stage C's completion check omits realized speed and action budget.
findings.evidence: fragments.py:26-31 (transit action_translation_m .02, contact .005). Measured realized/commanded median ratio 0.258 / 0.246 / 0.255 in the uc7.1 t6/t8/t9 traces. Saturated transit 5.04 / 3.77 / 4.58 mm per step; contact 1.08-1.25 mm per step. This matches reports/agent_speedup_analysis_20261026/uc7_runs.md:204 ('Arm speed is 24% of the command: 4.8 mm/step in transit, 1.17 in contact'). Native path: robot_config/x5.py:38-45 and eval_env.py:519-530. 4 of 12 successful LIBERO uc7/uc7.1 attempts took more than 56 simulated seconds (1141, 1187, 1572 and 2245 steps at 20 Hz). Estimates are in key_facts.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation, pre-register one mapping in the adapter diff. (a) Per-action cap parity: disclose that realized speeds become about 4-5x LIBERO's and that contact/stall dynamics differ; the horizon is then expected to hold at about 400-650 actions. (b) Realized-speed parity: disclose that the horizon is then expected to bind. Add a model-free, robot-only timing diagnostic to stage C: actions per 0.30 m transit, per 0.08 m contact move, per gripper close/open, arrival overhead, and the realized/commanded ratio. Write a make_toast horizon projection from it. Record the mapping, and whether the model-visible step bounds (120/240, MIN_GRIPPER_STEPS 12/8, stall 12/16, motion 1-5 steps) are kept as counts or rescaled x1.25, in the launch manifest. Never retune after a model attempt.

findings.title: Native observation 'state' for arm joints and grippers is the last command, not a measurement
findings.description: RoboDojo's ObsManager.get_obs first writes the measured arm joints, then overwrites state.<side>_arm_joint_state with control_manager.prev_control, the last commanded substep target. It also sets state.<side>_ee_joint_state to the last commanded, rate-limited gripper value normalized to [0,1]. Only ee_pose is measured. uc7.1's local loop and model feedback depend on measured fingers: set_gripper completes on a stable measured gap, a sustained gap rise triggers maintained_grip_gap_changed, and finger_joints_m / joint_position_rad / finger_gap_mm are model-visible. If the adapter takes these from the native observation dict, the measurements silently become commands. set_gripper would always look stable, slip detection would never fire, and Astra would see commanded closure presented as measured state.
findings.evidence: Upstream obs_manager.py:168-174 writes measured joints; :185-211 overwrites both *_arm_joint_state and *_ee_joint_state from prev_control; :176-183 ee_pose comes from get_real_endpose (measured body_link_pose_w). control_manager.py:22-34 and 81-86 show prev_control holding the rate-limited command. uc7.1 dependencies: fragments.py:278-289 (gap-rise yield) and 294-301 (gap-stable completion); agent_client.py:493 (finger_joints_m = state[6:8]); agent.py:188, 218 (finger_gap_mm).
findings.recommendation: In the simulator worker, read measured channels through robot-only accessors: robot_manager.get_joint (joint_pos), get_end_effector_real_val (both finger joints), and get_real_endpose plus a fixed ARX TCP offset. Expose commanded values separately and label them. Add a contract test in which a closure blocked by an object shows the measured gap differing from the command. Never forward the native state dict as 'measured'.

findings.title: Most of the execution stack must be forked or rewritten, not wrapped; the plan understates the port scope
findings.description: What ports across is the decision protocol (belief/plan/why/type/execution JSON, history, review/approval, direction contract) and the fragment state-machine logic. The I/O layer is bound by module-level imports and hard type/shape checks: StepView (8-D Panda state, Panda finger sign, LIBERO image flip, two cameras), ActionAdapter (OSC_POSE), measured_pose/ShortTargetExecutor (20 Hz, Panda closure), the base policy's 7-D [-1,1] action contract and Panda RobotModel, the LIBERO sim worker, the Panda/MuJoCo geometry validator and the 2-panel video recorder. The plan forbids global monkey patches, so subclasses and wrappers cannot replace these; they need versioned forks. The macro-path modules also run at reset and appear in every request context even when unused. Module classification is in key_facts.
findings.evidence: fragments.py:17-19 (imports), 178-179 (isinstance StepView), 185 and 258 (ActionAdapter.adapt returns a 7-D OSC action), 201 (state[3:6] axis-angle). contact_skills.py:265-270, 283. action.py:16-17, 86-93. agent_speedup_v2.py:1799 and 1920. agent.py:74-85 (StableScene, relation layer, fulfiller and macro session at reset), 155-170 (native_evidence in every request), 595 (macro invalidate after every direct action). agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:21, 45-46, 88. robocasa_user_check_geometry.py:59-61. agent_speedup_v2_video.py:36, 79.
findings.recommendation: In PLAN section 3 and stage C, list (i) files reused byte-identically (e.g., _framework.py, _context.py, transport/history/review), (ii) forked files with per-function rationale in the core-to-adapter diff, and (iii) what 'uc7.1 parity' means for this adapter (decision schema plus arm field, history policy, review, direction contract, local control law) versus what is re-implemented. Budget effort accordingly.

findings.title: The frozen prompt and schema embed Panda, 20 Hz, two-camera and OSC constants
findings.description: The model-visible instructions state the embodiment, rates, caps, frame names and gripper geometry. All of these become wrong for dual ARX at 25 Hz with three cameras. The plan mentions a prompt/schema diff in general but does not enumerate these items, and the step bounds are part of the JSON schema the model sees.
findings.evidence: agent_client.py:52-53 ('one Franka Panda'), 56-58 ('two images ... external and wrist', 'six most recent observation pairs'), 117 ('At 20 Hz'), 118-120 (0.30/0.08 m envelopes, 0.02/0.005 m caps, 0.1 rad, 'OSC'), 140-141 (gripper0_grip_site, robot0_right_hand), 145 ('steps is 1..5 at 20 Hz'), 159 (macro calibration about 190 control steps), 196-199 (0.097 m grip offset, Panda pads, 0.079 m gap). The execution schema has no arm field (fragments.py:46-64) and bounds max_steps at 120 / sum 240 (fragments.py:57, 137). Geometry schema: astranomy_agentic_geometry.py:23, 33-47.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate every embodiment-bearing sentence and constant in the versioned prompt/schema diff, with its ARX/RoboDojo replacement and provenance (or its removal). Keep all other wording byte-identical. Tie the step-bound choice to F1. Contract-test the rendered prompt and schema.

findings.title: Decide up front whether to keep or drop the native macros (hold/turn/place_on/release)
findings.description: The model is offered native macros that depend on Panda-specific v2 machinery (Panda RobotModel facts, CalibratePlus, StableScene, held-frame estimator, relation layer). None of the recorded attempts used them. Calibration alone is documented at about 190 control steps, roughly 14% of the native horizon. The plan says to audit macros individually but does not decide.
findings.evidence: agent.py:139-146 and agent_client.py:154-170 offer the macros; agent_schema has type 'macro'. agent_speedup_v2_types.py:753-778 builds RobotModel from agent_speedup_v2_robot.py:49-82 Panda constants. In all 13 recorded uc7/uc7.1 attempts with actions, only the execute_fragment and local_motion primitives ran and there were 0 macro grants (trace count). reports/agent_speedup_analysis_20261026 wf1 summary: 'Native macros were never used'. agent_client.py:159: about 190-step calibration.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the macro action type and its context fields for the RoboDojo adapter, disclosed as a capability removal in the diff and preflight, or port it as a separately reviewed component with ARX facts. Do not leave a macro option whose prerequisites can never be met.

findings.title: The native action path has silent no-ops the adapter must surface
findings.description: Once take_action_cnt reaches 1400 or the episode ends, native take_action silently skips the action without raising. A loop that does not check end_flag would keep 'executing' fragments and sending Astra requests against a frozen terminal state. In ee mode the action is counted before IK runs, and an IK failure silently keeps the previous command. An unreachable target therefore consumes actions with no explicit signal, and a 6-DoF ARX will hit IK limits more often than the 7-DoF Panda.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:368-369 (skip at limit or end_flag), 371 (count) then 415-424 (control set only on IK 'Success'), control_manager.py:88-94 (missing control filled from prev_control), eval_env.py:841-867 (is_episode_end).
findings.recommendation: Check end_flag and take_action_cnt after every native action, and stop fragments and model requests at termination. For any IK failure (own solver or CuRobo), end the segment with an explicit robot-measured status, decide and disclose whether it is reported as a stall-equivalent (LIBERO parity) or a new feedback type, and count the consumed action.

findings.title: The inactive arm should hold its measured pose, not its last command
findings.description: uc7.1's hold is a zero displacement from the measured pose. Holding the 'last commanded state' of an arm whose last fragment stalled keeps a stiff joint-position PD pushing toward a target up to one capped step away, into the obstacle, while the other arm acts.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:82 says the other arm 'holds its last commanded state'. agent.py:529-536 implements hold as relative [0,0,0] from the measured pose; fragments.py:157-158 says 'hold entry pose'. Native path: eval_env.py:514-530 interpolates toward the commanded joint vector; control_manager.py:88-94 reuses prev_control; x5.py:42 stiffness 4400.
findings.recommendation: Hold the inactive arm at the joint vector measured at hand-off (or at its last measured arrival), keep its gripper command, and report both in the per-arm feedback.

findings.title: Cross-side reach, handoff need and 6-DoF orientation feasibility are unverified
findings.description: The standard layout puts the bread shelf on the left-arm side and the toaster on the right-arm side. Whether one ARX X5 can pick from the shelf and insert into the toaster depends on the layout and on the ARX URDF, which lives in downloaded assets and cannot be checked now. If one arm cannot reach both, the model must orchestrate a handoff from sequential one-arm fragments, adding several fragments and hundreds of actions per slice. A 6-DoF arm also cannot reach some position-plus-orientation targets that the 7-DoF Panda could, for example the bread yaw re-alignment for a toaster rotated -105..-75 deg.
findings.evidence: task/RoboDojo/config/make_toast.yml:5-9 (toaster table-frame x in [0.04,0.35], y in [-0.12,-0.03], yaw -105..-75) and :26-29 (shelf x in [-0.35,0.0], y in [-0.20,0.0], +/-15 deg). env_cfg/robot/dual_x5.yml:6,14 (bases at x=-0.3 and +0.3, y=-0.45). Cross-side horizontal distances run up to about 0.75 m. robot_class/x5.py:18-24 loads urdf/curobo.yml from Assets/Robots (not in the repo). _robot_info.json arm_dim 6.
findings.recommendation: Before launch, compute a robot-only reach and orientation map per arm over the table workspace as a human-facing diagnostic, not a model input. Include the handoff cost in the F1 horizon projection. Rely on F6's explicit IK-infeasibility feedback.

findings.title: Full success is a simultaneous conjunction that includes lever >= 85% and both arms at origin; lever retention depends on the asset
findings.description: Success is evaluated at every action boundary and requires every check to hold at once. The lever must still be at >= 85% of its joint range after the pressing arm leaves and both arms are within 0.15 m per axis and 20 deg of their reset poses. Whether the toaster lever stays down after release depends on its USD joint drive, which cannot be checked from the repo. The return-to-origin requirement is absent from the instruction (the plan already notes this). Each moved arm's homing adds actions.
findings.evidence: make_toast.py:56-67, 87-88. reward_manager.py:383-389 (one check_list entry must fully pass in a single step). func_parser.py:59 (origin captured at reset), 1631-1644 (per-axis 0.15 m, 20 deg). env/scene_manager/objects/articulation.py:388-470 (articulated assets carry DriveAPI targets).
findings.recommendation: Add an evaluator-only, model-free check that the installed lever stays at >= 85% after release. Include homing of every moved arm in the horizon projection.

findings.title: Reference point: Astra-medium with RoboProbe scored make_toast Score 0.5, SR 0
findings.description: Under the native horizon with a 25 Hz Cartesian-chunk harness, Astra-medium essentially never placed even one slice correctly (score 0.5 is about one 25-point partial across 50 episodes). The single high-effort pilot will most likely end at the horizon with a partial score.
findings.evidence: Report JS Table 2 row {dim:'generalization',task:'make_toast',cells:[{score:.5,sr:0},...]}, with column order J=[GPT-6-Astra, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-Flash, DM0.5, ...]. 'Generalization cells are the mean of Gen-Std and Gen-Rand'. The best listed cell is SR 5.335.
findings.recommendation: State this expectation in the preview, and keep the plan's reporting of termination cause, native partial score and action count.

SUB-GOAL STEPS from per-decision fragments, 20 Hz:

uc7.1 t6 pudding: 145 / 82 / 138 / 147 (total 512), plus 1 'finish' hold and a 307-step regrasp/re-place.

Articulated interactions in uc7: t2 knob about 200-300 steps; t3 drawer close about 422.
Per-object pick-place averages across 2-object tasks: 324-1122 steps, median about 460.
MOTION RATES. Pooled over the 13 attempts with actions: 13,812 steps over 35.71 m of EEF path, i.e. 387 steps/m (per-run range 314-660).

Only execute_fragment and local_motion primitives ran; 0 native-macro grants in any run.
A rejected answer, observe or finish costs 1 hold action (agent.py:529-536; t6 step 880). Inference itself costs 0 actions.
uc7.1 CAPS (fragments.py:22-43, 185):
transit: 0.02 m/step, envelope 0.30 m / 1.2 rad, tolerance 4 mm / 0.06 rad
contact: 0.005 m/step, envelope 0.08 m / 0.5 rad, tolerance 2 mm / 0.04 rad
rotation 0.1 rad/step; at most 6 segments, 120 steps per segment, 240 per fragment; set_gripper minimum 12 close / 8 open; stall check 0.8 mm over a 12-step window after 16 steps
direct motion: 1-5 steps, 0.05 m / 0.35 rad (astranomy_agentic_motion.py:103-107)
NATIVE ROBODOJO FACTS (@f57e163):
1400 actions x 0.04 s = 56 s sim.
Each action is 10 substeps of 0.004 s: 8 interpolated from measured joints, 2 holding the target.
Every action must carry both arms: <side>_arm_joint_state (6-D) + <side>_ee_joint_state (1-D, range [0,1]), or <side>_ee_pose (7-D) solved with CuRobo IK that includes a table cuboid.
Gripper target limited to 20% of range per substep relative to the measured opening (control_manager.py:22-34).
Arm PD: stiffness 4400, damping 40, velocity limit 5 rad/s, effort 100; robot gravity disabled (x5.py:12-13, 38-45).
obs 'state' joints/gripper are the last command (obs_manager.py:185-211); ee_pose is measured, wxyz, relative to env origin, of ee_link (not the TCP).
LIBERO physics ran 25 substeps per step (500 Hz); RoboDojo runs 250 Hz.
HORIZON ESTIMATE. Assumptions:

verdicts.reasoning: Verified at f57e163. obs_manager.py:168-174 writes the measured arm joints. Then :185-211 iterates over control_manager.prev_control and, because arx_x5.yml:12 sets joint_states: true, overwrites state['left_arm_joint_state'] and the right-arm equivalent with prev_control positions. The key names come from robot_manager.py:81-86, :340-344 and :563-573. The same loop writes state['<side>_ee_joint_state'] as the normalized gripper command. Only <side>_ee_pose (get_real_endpose -> body_link_pose_w, robot_manager.py:131-170) is measured. After an action, prev_control holds substep 10, which is exactly the arm target (eval_env.py:529-530), so the arm 'state' is the last command. Correction to the stated consequence: the gripper value is not the raw command. process_gripper_val (control_manager.py:22-34, applied on every pop :81-94) clamps the command to within 20% of the gripper range of the measured opening. The native gripper state therefore runs up to 20% of range ahead of the measurement, and equals the target once the measured opening is within 20% of it. A close blocked by an object thinner than ~20% of range reads the same as an empty close. A bread slice plausibly falls in that range, but gripper_scale lives in the asset robot_config.yml, not in the repo (pipeline_utils.py:9-16). Thicker objects read biased but still move with the measurement. So 'always stable / never fires' is overstated. Still, the grasp-width evidence LIBERO gave as measured would be lost or biased: finger_joints_m from state8 (agent_client.py:493), finger_gap_mm (agent.py:188, 218) and the local predicates (fragments.py:278-301). The plan's 'expose genuine measurements' (PLAN.md:84) and allowlist rule (INPUT_CONTRACT.md:33) do not mention this native trap. Major stands: it decides whether a LIBERO information category, measured proprioception, stays genuine.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Native state.<side>_arm_joint_state is exactly the last commanded joint target. state.<side>_ee_joint_state is the command clamped to within 20% of the gripper range of the measured opening, so it runs ahead of the measurement and reads fully closed whenever the fingers stop within 20% of range of the target. Grasp-width evidence is therefore masked for thin objects and biased otherwise. Measured channels must come from robot_manager.get_joint / get_end_effector_real_val / get_real_endpose.

new_issues: [major, feasibility_risk; extends F1] Blocked contact under the native joint PD is estimated at roughly 30-300x stiffer than LIBERO's OSC, and uc7.1's contact and stall rules were set on the compliant OSC. Evidence: x5.py:38-45 (K 4400 Nm/rad, D 40, effort 100 Nm per joint). eval_env.py:514-530 re-interpolates every action from the measured joints to the commanded target and then holds it. A uc7.1-style law (target = measured + capped error) therefore keeps a constant 5 mm (contact, fragments.py:29-30) or 20 mm (transit) lead while blocked. fragments.py:41-43 and 311-325 yield only after at least 16 actions with <0.8 mm improvement over 12, i.e. 0.64 s at 25 Hz. LIBERO used OSC_POSE kp=150 with fixed impedance (/venv/fm_dno/lib/python3.10/site-packages/robosuite/controllers/config/osc_pose.json, recorded in trial/simulator.json:73). Its Cartesian stiffness is Lambda*kp, ~1.5e2-7.5e2 N/m for 1-5 kg task-space inertia (estimate), a few N per blocked 5 mm lead. The native joint PD gives K_x = 4400*(J J^T)^-1, ~2e4-1e5 N/m for 0.2-0.5 m lever arms (estimate), i.e. O(100 N), limited at 100 Nm per joint, sustained for at least 0.64 s per stall. uc7.1 leans on contact moves: the contact profile takes 48.6% of motion steps and stalls 15% (uc7_runs.md:205-206). make_toast needs slot insertion and a lever press. PLAN.md:86 says only 'Preserve target-error control-field intent and limits in physical units'. Recommendation: pre-register in stage C how blocked contact is bounded (e.g., cap the joint-target lead over the measured joints while tracking error persists), disclose it as a controller conversion, and run a model-free blocked-motion diagnostic that reports peak joint torque/contact force before any model attempt. These figures are order-of-magnitude and unmeasured.

[minor, contract] The native <side>_ee_pose action path is not a robot-only controller. eval_env.py:407-424 sends ee actions to robot_manager.solve_ik -> CuroboPlanner (robot_manager.py:325-338, 539-550, table_height = 0.74 - root z). Its InverseKinematics is built with a scene_model holding a 3.0 x 3.0 x 0.05 m 'table' cuboid and self_collision_check=True (curobo_planner.py:486-503, 525-539), and an IK failure silently keeps the previous command (eval_env.py:420-424, control_manager.py:88-94). LIBERO uc7.1 had no collision model ('no ... collision planner', fragments.py:5). INPUT_CONTRACT.md:27 requires 'Robot-only kinematics; no simulator scene collision world'. The CuRobo proof that PLAN.md:86 demands would therefore fail for the native ee path as-is. Recommendation: pre-select the <side>_arm_joint_state path (6-D arm + 1-D gripper per arm, _robot_info.json; eval_env.py:377-405) with the adapter's own robot-only IK. Otherwise, disclose the table cuboid and self-collision filter as a new controller input and report IK status for every action.

[minor, decision_needed; ties F1 to the info contract] The agent is never told about the 1400-action horizon, and the uc7.1 prompt assumes no episode budget. Evidence: make_toast.py:15 sets step_lim 1400. UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:28 says LIBERO set no total time, action-count or call-count cap. INPUT_CONTRACT.md:24 keeps the remaining budget evaluator-only. The prompt mentions only per-segment budgets (agent_client.py:116-117). Because the agent cannot trade care for speed against a limit it never sees, a horizon termination would partly reflect the adapter's speed mapping (F1), not only the agent's ability. Recommendation: choose the speed mapping in advance so that the model-free horizon projection leaves clear margin. Also state in advance how a horizon termination will be reported: as a native failure, with projected versus consumed actions. Telling Astra about the limit would be a new information category that needs explicit user approval. The plan's current choice not to forward it is consistent with 'same info'.

findings.title: Host driver 610.43.02 is outside Isaac Sim 5.1.0's validated branch, and a public report shows 5.1.0 segfaulting on exactly this driver
findings.description: Potential blocker for running native RoboDojo on this host. The plan treats driver 610.43.02 as a neutral inspection fact. Isaac Sim 5.1.0 was tested on Linux driver 580.65.06, and RoboDojo recommends driver 570/580 on Ubuntu 22.04; this box runs 610.43.02 on Ubuntu 24.04.4. A June 2026 NVIDIA forum report describes Isaac Sim 5.1.0, headless, on an 8-GPU box, segfaulting in librtx.scenedb.plugin.so after the driver changed from 580 to 610.43.02. NVIDIA staff answered that 610.43.02 is not a production-branch driver and closed the thread unresolved. A second NVIDIA-staff thread (RTX 4090, Ubuntu 24.04.4, driver 595.71.05) shows the same librtx.scenedb crash signature, diagnosed as an unvalidated driver and confirmed across several GPU models. The driver is host-injected and cannot be changed here. The docs banner marks 5.1.0 as no longer supported. RoboDojo pins Isaac Sim 5.1.0 with IsaacLab 2.3.2, so an Isaac Sim upgrade would not be the Standard environment. vulkaninfo working here does not exercise the RTX scenedb path. If the crash reproduces, nothing in this container can fix it, and adapter work done before the check would be wasted.
findings.evidence: nvidia-smi 'Driver Version: 610.43.02 ... CUDA UMD Version: 13.3'; /etc/os-release 'Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS'; https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/5.1.0/installation/requirements.html (Driver 'Linux: 580.65.06', OS 'Ubuntu 22.04/24.04', banner says 5.1.0 no longer supported); https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/usage/install-and-download/ ('570 or 580 recommended', Ubuntu 22.04 recommended); docker/README.md:47 'tested on Ubuntu 22.04'; https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/isaacsim-crash-when-update-gpu-driver/371975 (5.1.0 headless, 'Driver Version: 610.43.02', 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)', backtrace in librtx.scenedb.plugin.so; NVIDIA: 'Driver version 610.43.02 is not from the production branch.'); https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/isaac-sim-5-1-0-crashes-on-startup-with-rtx-4090-on-ubuntu-24-04-4-segfaulting-in-librtx-scenedb-plugin-so-after-iommu-was-disabled/371957 ('Driver 595.71.05 is not validated for Isaac Sim 5.1.0'); /workspace/CLAUDE.md:374.
findings.recommendation: Make the first Stage A action a minimal, model-free Isaac Sim 5.1.0 headless RTX camera smoke on one idle, user-assigned GPU, before any adapter code. Options: the upstream zero-action demo_policy with EVAL_NUM=1 on a non-pilot task, or an AppLauncher script that renders one tiled camera frame. Pre-declare a stop rule: a librtx/scenedb segfault, or a hang on the first rendered frame, means native RoboDojo is not runnable on this host. Record it as an installation result and move to a host with the 580.65.06 production driver (Ubuntu 22.04 preferred). Do not attempt driver swaps, forward-compat libraries or an Isaac Sim upgrade under the Standard label. List OS 24.04, driver 610 and the non-Docker install as disclosed environment deviations.

findings.title: 'One selected GPU' is unspecified; native defaults would render on nvidia-smi GPU 0 (the live training job) with multi-GPU rendering enabled
findings.description: RoboDojo pins its GPU only through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Upstream validated this only in Docker, where --gpus hides the other devices. Natively, all 8 /dev/nvidia nodes are visible to Vulkan/Kit. eval_policy.sh exports CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<device_id> but never passes --device, so AppLauncher keeps 'cuda:0' and sets active_gpu = physics_gpu = 0. SimulationApp then emits '--/renderer/activeGpu=0', which Isaac Sim 5.1 documents as the nvidia-smi index. It also emits '--/renderer/multiGpu/enabled=True' with max_gpu_count None ('use all available'). The fork launches isaaclab.python.kit for every mode, and that file has no multiGpu/maxGpuCount keys; the upstream-style headless.rendering.kit has maxGpuCount=1. On this box nvidia-smi GPUs 0-3 belong to the live 4-GPU Pi05_past training run (21,394 of 24,564 MiB used each, 33-100% util, ~3.1 GB free); GPUs 4-7 are idle. Likely outcomes: renderer contexts on a busy GPU, possible OOM of the user's training job, or a CUDA-vs-Vulkan device mismatch. On the minor-number trap: Vulkan enumeration here follows nvidia-smi/PCI order (vulkaninfo GPU4 UUID e1a460e9 = smi 4 = bus 81:00.0 = /dev minor 7). The reversed-minor trap that affects MuJoCo EGL therefore does not apply to Kit, and translating indices to minor numbers would pick the wrong GPU.
findings.evidence: scripts/eval_policy.sh:105-108 'export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${device_id}"' and :146-161 (no --device); IsaacLab fork app_launcher.py:389 '"device": ([str], "cuda:0")', :710-711 (physics_gpu and active_gpu = self.device_id), :697 (multi_gpu False only when distributed), :729-749 (isaaclab.python.kit in every branch), :794 (kit_args appended to sys.argv); apps/isaaclab.python.kit: 0 lines matching multiGpu|maxGpuCount|activeGpu; apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit:76 'renderer.multiGpu.maxGpuCount=1'; isaacsim-core 5.1.0.0 simulation_app.py:74-77 (active_gpu None, physics_gpu 0, multi_gpu True, max_gpu_count None), :110, :399, :415-418, :531-533 (unknown args appended after its own args); https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/5.1.0/installation/install_faq.html '/renderer/activeGpu=0: sets the active GPU according to nvidia-smi'; https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/how-to-make-isaac-sim-use-only-one-gpu/272718 'CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 still uses all of them'; docker/README.md:223-224; nvidia-smi (0-3 at 21394 MiB, 4-7 at 1 MiB); vulkaninfo --summary UUID order vs nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid; memory gpu-minor-order-reversed.md:11, pi05-past-implementation.md:13-17.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit GPU contract to Stage A and to the approval-bound launch config. First get the user's GPU assignment; memory notes record per-project allocations, and the DexMimicGen note marks 6,7 off-limits for that work. Set CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-<uuid> for the assigned GPU. Keep AppLauncher --device cuda:0 so physics, CuRobo and Warp use ordinal 0 inside the visible set. Add kit args '--/renderer/multiGpu/enabled=false --/renderer/multiGpu/autoEnable=false --/renderer/multiGpu/maxGpuCount=1 --/renderer/activeGpu=<nvidia-smi index>'. Make the check fail closed unless all of these hold: SimulationApp's printed 'Starting kit application with the following args' line shows the overrides after its own activeGpu/multiGpu args; Kit's GPU table marks only the intended Bus-ID active; nvidia-smi shows no memory change on any other GPU during load, reset and render. Never use /dev minor numbers for Kit.

findings.title: The native eval harness auto-restarts and substitutes layouts, which conflicts with 'one attempt, layoutID0, no automatic retry'
findings.description: The plan forbids automatic whole-task retries and scene reselection, but it does not neutralize RoboDojo's built-in recovery, which is live for make_toast. (a) eval_policy.sh relaunches main.py up to ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=10 times on exit codes 99, 134 or 139. (b) main.py self-restarts via os.execv up to MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS=3 and resumes from a manifest keyed by ROBODOJO_RUN_ID. (c) On PhysXBrokenError it abandons the broken seed and refills from the seed queue, which runs the next layout. (d) On UnStableError it skips to the next layout. (e) The PhysX monitor that triggers these paths is enabled because make_toast.yml has a non-empty Articulation section (the toaster). If the adapter reuses eval_policy.sh, main.py or their loop, a mid-attempt simulator fault can silently become a second episode on make_toast_1. That breaks single-attempt accounting and turns an installation fault into an apparent task attempt. Separately, if make_toast_0 is natively unstable at reset, the native order would skip to make_toast_1, and the plan has no rule for that case registered in advance.
findings.evidence: scripts/eval_policy.sh:142 'MAX_BASH_RETRIES="${ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES:-10}"', :169-180 ('99|134|139) ... restarting'); src/eval_client/main.py:10 'MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS = 3', :211-238 (os.execv self-restart, then sys.exit(99)), :149-183 and :345-346 (resume manifest), :372-432 ('Abandon broken-env seeds, refill from the seed queue, and retry this round'), :376-377 (UnStableError -> eval_step), :85-100 and :111 (monitor enabled iff Articulation); task/RoboDojo/config/make_toast.yml:1 'Articulation:'; PLAN.md:22 'no automatic whole-task retry', :24 'without selecting a different scene', :116-118 'single-use attempt guard ... No queued task or automatic new attempt'.
findings.recommendation: The adapter's simulator worker should run a fixed single-seed list [layout 0] with no refill, no execv or bash retry (ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=1 if any upstream wrapper is reused), no resume manifest, and a fresh ROBODOJO_RUN_ID. Any PhysXFatal, PhysXBroken or UnStable event becomes a terminal simulator-error record, never a new episode. Before the preview, register what happens if make_toast_0 is natively unstable: either stop, or follow the native skip rule to the next numeric layout, stated in advance. Add contract tests that inject each failure type and assert that no second reset occurs.

findings.title: CuRobo and a generated curobo.yml are mandatory for native env init; the generation step is missing from the plan
findings.description: Even a model-free load requires a working CuRobo install and Assets/Robots/x5/curobo.yml. robot_manager.py imports CuroboPlanner, which imports curobo at module import. It then builds a planner for x5, because dual_x5.yml sets no need_planner and the default is True. x5.py loads <robot>/curobo.yml, but the HF asset tree ships only curobo_tmp.yml. curobo.yml is produced by running 'python utils/update_embodiment_config_path.py' from the repo root, which writes absolute ${ASSETS_PATH} paths into Assets. That step appears only on the docs page, not in install.sh, init_assets.sh or verify_install.sh. Consequences: (1) Stage A needs this step. (2) It modifies the asset tree after any download checksum. (3) The absolute path ties the config to the final install location (the docker README documents the 'X5A.urdf is not a file' failure). (4) CuRobo, with a table-height obstacle, is loaded in the simulator process even if the adapter never uses it for control; this matters for the Stage C backend audit.
findings.evidence: env/robot_manager/robot_manager.py:15 (from env.planner_manager.curobo_planner import CuroboPlanner), :51-52 (cfg.get("need_planner", True) -> _setup_planner), :539-550 (CuroboPlanner(... yml_path=robot.curobo_yml_path, table_height=0.74 - root_pose[2])); env/planner_manager/curobo_planner.py:3-7; env/robot_manager/robot_class/x5.py:24; env_cfg/robot/dual_x5.yml (no need_planner key); HF tree Assets/Robots/x5 at 269457a3: curobo_tmp.yml 12,526 B, no curobo.yml; utils/update_embodiment_config_path.py:25,55,72-76; https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/usage/install-and-download/ ('python utils/update_embodiment_config_path.py'); docker/README.md:193-197.
findings.recommendation: In Stage A, build CuRobo as a required dependency. Run the generator from the final vendor root after the assets are in place. Hash curobo_tmp.yml as an upstream input and the generated curobo.yml separately as derived config, and include it in the approval-bound config hash. Tell the controller reviewer that a CuroboPlanner exists in-process by default.

findings.title: The first Kit start must download URDF importer 2.4.31 from the remote registry; it is not bundled and not checksummed
findings.description: The fork's isaaclab.python.kit, used for every launch, requires isaacsim.asset.importer.urdf at exactly version 2.4.31. The isaacsim 5.1.0.0 wheels bundle only 2.4.30 (in isaacsim-asset). Neither extscache wheel contains any URDF importer: I read their ZIP central directories over HTTP range requests (33,380 and 1,095 entries). Kit's extension solver must therefore fetch 2.4.31 from the enabled remote registries at first startup. That is a component resolved over the network at run time and not covered by pip hashes, and with 5.1.0 out of support its continued availability is not guaranteed. Upstream Isaac Lab pins this version deliberately (fixed-joint merging behavior), so it cannot be dropped.
findings.evidence: apps/isaaclab.python.kit:41 '"isaacsim.asset.importer.urdf" = {version = "2.4.31", exact = true}', :256-265 (registries on ovextensionsprod.blob.core.windows.net and cloudfront; 'registryEnabled = true'); isaacsim_asset-5.1.0.0 wheel isaacsim/exts/isaacsim.asset.importer.urdf/config/extension.toml version 2.4.30; isaacsim_extscache_kit (3,021,340,845 B) and isaacsim_extscache_kit_sdk (1,345,115,764 B) central directories have no 'importer.urdf' entries; docker/README.md:189-191 (a fresh setup 'pulls Isaac Sim extensions'); https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/main/_modules/isaaclab/sim/converters/urdf_converter.html (pins 2.4.31).
findings.recommendation: Allow network access during the first Stage A launch. Capture the resolved extension version, source registry, on-disk path and file hashes from the Kit log into the install manifest. Treat a failure to resolve it as an installation result. Then verify that later launches use the same local copy (no registry download in the log), so frozen runs cannot silently pick up a different extension build.

findings.title: Isaac Sim runtime libraries libXt.so.6 and libXinerama.so.1 are missing, and the plan has no system-package step
findings.description: install.sh installs only cmake, build-essential and ffmpeg. The upstream Dockerfile adds a headless GL/EGL/Vulkan/X runtime set and, later, libxt6, with a comment that Isaac Sim's MaterialX render libraries fail to load at startup without libXt.so.6. On this box libXt.so.6 and libXinerama.so.1 are absent; the other listed libraries are present. These would be container-global apt installs, outside the isolated runtime/, and lost on recycle. Separately, the Dockerfile writes a second Vulkan ICD and then pins VK_ICD_FILENAMES, because two ICDs for the same GPU wedge RTX init on the first frame. This box has exactly one ICD (/etc/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json), so a native port must not copy the ICD-writing step.
findings.evidence: scripts/install.sh:73-83; Dockerfile:65-92 (apt list incl. libxinerama1 at :88), :205-211 ('libXt.so.6 is required by Isaac Sim's MaterialX render libs ... fail to load at startup'), :108-117 (writes /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json), :212-220 (VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/etc/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json; 'two ICDs for the same GPU wedge RTX init'); ldconfig -p: libXt.so.6 and libXinerama.so.1 missing; dpkg: libxt6/libxt6t64 and libxinerama1 not installed; /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d absent, /etc/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json present (api 1.4.341).
findings.recommendation: Add a reviewed system-package step: apt-get install libxt6 (resolves to libxt6t64 on noble) and libxinerama1. Record it in the provisioning manifest as a container-global change that must be reapplied after a recycle. Set VK_ICD_FILENAMES=VK_DRIVER_FILES=/etc/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json in the worker environment. Never create /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json.

findings.title: The official asset script pulls all 41.3 GB at a moving revision; a pinned make_toast subset is about 0.52 GB
findings.description: The plan correctly asks for a subset. Without sizes, though, the default path is init_assets.sh, which sparse-checks out all of Assets/** from HF revision main and pulls every LFS object: 41,269,513,111 B at main = 269457a3. With the LFS object store plus checked-out copies, that is roughly 83 GB on a shared, non-persistent disk with 191 GiB free. Breakdown: Material 26.07 GB, Object 12.62 GB, Room 1.69 GB, Traj 0.63 GB, Robots 125 MB, Eval_Layout 83 MB, Sensor 27 MB, Background 25 MB. Layout 0 needs only Robots/x5, bread, bread_shelf, camera_stand, toaster, material_0122, material_0564, Simple_Room_nolight, Background and Sensor, about 518 MB. Room, Material and Background are selected by name, and each selected folder holds exactly one top-level USD/MDL, so a name-preserving subset loads byte-identical files.
findings.evidence: scripts/init_assets.sh:14-20 (HF_REPO_ID, HF_REVISION=main, REQUIRED_ASSET_SUBDIRS), :101-108 (sparse-checkout set Assets; lfs pull --include="Assets/**"); HF API treesize at 269457a3 (sizes above); HF commit list (269457a3 and ffdfc52e on 2026-10-22 touch only data/RoboDojo_real); env/scene_manager/layout_manager.py:263-275 and :336-342 (by-name selection unless random); env_cfg/scene/default.yml (no random keys); HF listings: Room/Simple_Room_nolight has one .usd, material_0122 has Mahogany_Planks.mdl, material_0564 has Wood_Tiles_Fineline.mdl; scripts/internal/verify_install.sh:110-113.
findings.recommendation: Download a pinned subset (revision 269457a3b42d8d0ae69898a601f2c1487c2f826e) with HF API or huggingface_hub allow-patterns. Record each file's LFS sha256 from the API and verify it after download. Keep the directory skeleton the loaders and verify_install.sh expect: Robots, Object/RoboDojo, Material, Eval_Layout/RoboDojo, Room, Background, Sensor. Include both toaster indices (2.8 MB total) and all 70 seed-0 make_toast layouts (about 0.6 MB) so the fallback rule from PROV-03 stays possible.

findings.title: Gitlink pins and installer-effective commits differ today, and the curobo pin lives on a non-main branch
findings.description: The plan records only the XPolicyLab gitlink and defers locking the IsaacLab and CuRobo gitlinks to installation. The concrete state needs a recorded decision. IsaacLab gitlink afca7b09 equals fork main. The curobo gitlink d17b54ce is the head of fork branch isaacsim-warp18 and has diverged from main 895c6517. The four Warp-compat source files are byte-identical between them; main adds 37 files (ARX X5 URDF and meshes, magicsim_arx_x5.yml, magicsim_dual_arx_x5.yml, Isaac Sim examples). XPolicyLab gitlink 5d0be149 is 27 commits behind main c43a7465. So 'reproduce the installer' (main heads) and 'use the pins' (gitlinks) produce different environments. There are also two vendoring traps. curobo's setuptools_scm config has no fallback_version, so building from a tarball or any copy without .git fails. A dangling submodule .git pointer makes import raise LookupError, which is why the Dockerfile strips those pointers.
findings.evidence: .gitmodules:3-12 (personal forks, branch = main); git ls-remote: curobo refs/heads/isaacsim-warp18 = d17b54ce32cba095c0b000c4c58777075d11de0e, refs/heads/main = 895c6517243f8cb091c73c018c8167192d39599a; GitHub compare d17b54ce...895c6517: 'diverged', ahead_by 2, behind_by 1, 41 files; XPolicyLab compare 5d0be149...c43a7465: 'ahead' 27; raw diffs of curobo/_src/util/warp.py and three wp_* kernel files: identical; curobo/content/configs/robot/magicsim_dual_arx_x5.yml returns 404 at the pin and 200 at main; curobo pyproject.toml:162-164 (no fallback_version); curobo/_src/util/version.py:20-32; Dockerfile:194-201; planning_manifest.json:22-23.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the gitlinks: IsaacLab afca7b09, curobo d17b54ce, XPolicyLab 5d0be149. Check them out with 'git submodule update --init' without --remote (or 'git fetch origin <sha>'), and assert HEAD equals the gitlink afterwards. Disclose that upstream's installer would currently produce curobo 895c6517 and XPolicyLab c43a7465. Use real git checkouts, or set SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_NVIDIA_CUROBO, and record each repo's tree hash.

findings.title: Running upstream install.sh on this box would leak outside the isolated runtime, and the result needs a hashed lock
findings.description: 'Inspect and reproduce in isolation' is the right approach; the hazards specific to this box should be written down. (1) conda is not on PATH in non-interactive shells, so setup_conda would download Miniconda3-latest into $HOME/miniconda3 and run 'conda init bash', editing /root/.bashrc. (2) If conda is on PATH, 'conda create -n RoboDojo' lands in /venv/RoboDojo (per .condarc envs_dirs), not under robodojo_uc71/runtime. (3) The '--from' path swallows activation failures with '|| true', so 'python -m pip' could install torch 2.7.0 and isaacsim into whatever env is active; interactive shells auto-activate /venv/main. (4) It runs an unpinned 'pip install --upgrade pip' and installs unpinned requirements (huggingface_hub, open3d, transforms3d, pillow, matplotlib, scikit-learn). (5) There is a deliberate pin conflict: RoboDojo re-pins starlette==0.45.3 after IsaacLab requires ==0.49.1. (6) Caches default to $HOME: pip already holds 1.1 GB there, plus Warp kernel and CUDA JIT caches. verify_install.sh also hard-codes a named conda env ('conda run -n RoboDojo').
findings.evidence: scripts/install.sh:89-95 (Miniconda install + conda init), :107, :139, :117-119, :214-217 ('... 2>/dev/null || true'), :29 and :60 (starlette==0.45.3) vs IsaacLab source/isaaclab/setup.py:40 ('starlette==0.49.1'); 'which -a conda' returns nothing in a non-interactive shell; /root/.bashrc:102-115 and :129 (auto-activates /venv/main); /root/.condarc envs_dirs [/venv, /opt/miniforge3/envs]; scripts/requirements.txt:1-7; scripts/internal/verify_install.sh:204-209,226; isaacsim simulation_app.py:444-445 ('--portable'); docker/smoke_docker.sh:186-188 (Warp kernel cache).
findings.recommendation: Never run install.sh or init_assets.sh directly. Script the equivalent steps against an explicit prefix: 'conda create -p <runtime>/env python=3.11' from conda-forge (python-3.11.16 is already cached), or a uv venv with Python 3.11. Place PIP_CACHE_DIR, WARP_CACHE_PATH, CUDA_CACHE_PATH and the Kit portable root under runtime/. After install, write a hashed lock (pip freeze plus wheel sha256s) and save 'pip check' output, noting the starlette conflict as an inherited upstream deviation. Run verify_install.sh with --skip-conda --skip-isaac and replace those two checks with prefix-based equivalents.

findings.title: Launching Isaac Sim requires accepting the NVIDIA Omniverse EULA, and upstream accepts it silently through an environment variable
findings.description: Isaac Sim's kit_app.py accepts the EULA when OMNI_KIT_ACCEPT_EULA is set to yes, y or 1, and writes an EULA_ACCEPTED file. Otherwise it blocks on an interactive input() prompt, which would hang or raise EOFError under a supervisor. RoboDojo's install.sh exports OMNI_KIT_ACCEPT_EULA=YES; the Dockerfile also sets ACCEPT_EULA=Y and PRIVACY_CONSENT=Y. Setting these accepts a license, and makes a consent setting, on the user's behalf, and the plan does not mention it.
findings.evidence: isaacsim_kernel-5.1.0.0 wheel isaacsim/kit/kit_app.py:19-43 ('By installing or using Omniverse Kit, I agree to the terms of NVIDIA OMNIVERSE LICENSE AGREEMENT (EULA)'; input('Do you accept the EULA? (Yes/No): ')); scripts/install.sh:155; Dockerfile:33-35.
findings.recommendation: Before installation, ask the user to accept the NVIDIA Omniverse License Agreement explicitly and to decide on the PRIVACY_CONSENT setting. Record the decision in the provisioning manifest, then set the variables only in the isolated worker environment.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-checked. On this host, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version` gives 610.43.02; the header reads 'KMD Version: 610.43.02  CUDA UMD Version: 13.3', and /etc/os-release reads 'Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS'. The Isaac Sim 5.1.0 requirements page shows '⚠ Unsupported release: Isaac Sim 5.1.0 is no longer supported', OS 'Ubuntu 22.04/24.04' and Driver 'Linux: 580.65.06' ('Isaac Sim was tested on these driver versions'). The RoboDojo install doc says 'NVIDIA driver 570 or 580 recommended on Linux' and 'Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux x64) recommended'. docker/README.md:47 says '(tested on Ubuntu 22.04)'. Forum topic 371975 (read as JSON) reports Isaac Sim 5.1.0 / Kit 107.3.3 on 8x RTX A6000, Ubuntu 22.04.5, 'Running in headless mode', 'Driver Version: 610.43.02', a backtrace in librtx.scenedb.plugin.so!carbOnPluginStartup and 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)'. Staff moderator VickNV replied 'Driver version 610.43.02 is not from the production branch.', and the topic was closed on 2026-06-17 without a fix. In topic 371957 (RTX 4090, Ubuntu 24.04.4, driver 595.71.05), staff wrote the driver 'is not validated for Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and causes crashes in librtx.scenedb.plugin.so during RTX renderer initialization... confirmed across multiple GPU models (RTX 4070, 4090, 5070 Ti, 5080, 5090)'. In IsaacSim GitHub #517, the only workaround other than a driver downgrade is disabling Vulkan to force D3D12, which is Windows-only. CLAUDE.md:374 and PLAN.md:64 both rule out changing the driver. In addition, a deterministic segfault (rc 139) would be retried by eval_policy.sh:169-180 (see new issues). Three overstatements: (1) the plan already makes the model-free render check the Stage A gate and calls a failure 'an installation result' (PLAN.md:68), so adapter work is wasted only if stages run out of order; (2) native install is RoboDojo's main documented path (install doc §3 'Clone & install RoboDojo natively'), so a non-Docker install is not a deviation to disclose; (3) Ubuntu 24.04 is within Isaac Sim 5.1.0's listed OS support and deviates only from RoboDojo's 22.04 recommendation. It is not a blocker: it is unproven on this host, and the plan stops before any Astra attempt if rendering fails.
verdicts.corrected_statement: There is a high, publicly documented risk that Isaac Sim 5.1.0 RTX will not start on this host's 610.43.02 driver. The driver is outside the validated 580.65.06 branch, and there is a staff-acknowledged librtx.scenedb crash on 610.43.02 and on R590 drivers, including RTX 4090 on Ubuntu 24.04.4; no Linux workaround is known. The plan should run a minimal headless Kit RTX camera smoke first in Stage A, before asset download or adapter work. It should pre-register a stop rule (segfault or first-frame hang means an installation result, then move to a 580-branch host) and disclose driver 610 and the 22.04 vs 24.04 difference. Do not list native installation as a deviation.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-checked the full chain. eval_policy.sh:105-108 exports CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<device_id>, and :146-161 passes main.py's own --device_id but no AppLauncher --device; robodojo.sh:522 maps --env-gpu to --device_id the same way. The fork's app_launcher.py:389 defaults device to 'cuda:0'; :710-711 sets physics_gpu = active_gpu = device_id (0); :697 sets multi_gpu=False only in distributed mode; :729-749 picks isaaclab.python.kit in every branch; :794 appends kit_args to sys.argv. Upstream Isaac Lab v2.3.2 app_launcher.py:727 picks isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit, which has 'renderer.multiGpu.maxGpuCount=1' at :76. The fork's isaaclab.python.kit has no multiGpu, maxGpuCount or activeGpu key (grep exit 1), so the fork removes upstream's single-GPU cap. I extracted isaacsim-core 5.1.0.0 simulation_app.py by range request: :74-77 defaults active_gpu None, physics_gpu 0, multi_gpu True, max_gpu_count None; :399 emits --/renderer/multiGpu/enabled; :415-420 emits activeGpu/cudaDevice and emits maxGpuCount only if set; :531-533 appends unknown args after its own. The 5.1.0 FAQ says '/renderer/activeGpu=0 sets the active GPU according to nvidia-smi'. The 6.1.0 FAQ adds that activeGpu 'selects one physical GPU using the order reported by nvidia-smi' and that only activeCudaGpus 'honors CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES'; 5.1.0's SimulationApp has no active_cuda_gpus option (grep exit 1). Separately, CuroboPlanner builds DeviceCfg() (cuda:0) and runs warmup at env init (curobo_planner.py:70-80), so the CUDA pin is also needed for CuRobo. Live state: smi GPUs 0-3 use 21394/24564 MiB each and belong to train_p2n_vla.py --devices 0,1,2,3 (ps); GPUs 4-7 use 1 MiB. Bus-to-minor mapping (smi 4 = 81:00.0 = minor 7, and so on) matches /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus. I did not rerun vulkaninfo. One supporting sentence is wrong: 'Upstream validated this only in Docker, where --gpus hides the other devices.' Upstream's main path is native install, its Docker smoke runs '--gpus all' (smoke_docker.sh:215; README:223 '--gpus all exposes every GPU'), and its parallel batch runner pins only through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (smoke_all_tasks.sh:980,991). Exactly where Kit renders is inferred from code and docs, not observed on this host, and whether a later duplicate --/renderer/... arg wins is unverified, so the fail-closed check is essential.
verdicts.corrected_statement: The plan's 'one selected GPU' has no mechanism. RoboDojo pins only through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, both natively and in its own '--gpus all' Docker and batch paths. With the fork's defaults, Kit receives --/renderer/activeGpu=0 (documented as the nvidia-smi index, not CUDA order) and --/renderer/multiGpu/enabled=True with no maxGpuCount, because the fork dropped upstream's maxGpuCount=1 kit. Rendering therefore likely lands on smi GPU 0 and/or all GPUs, including the four that hold the live training job with about 3.1 GB free each. Add an explicit GPU contract: the user's assignment, a CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES UUID, kit overrides for activeGpu and multiGpu, and a fail-closed check of Kit's GPU table and per-GPU nvidia-smi memory.

verdicts.reasoning: Every cited path holds at f57e1633. eval_policy.sh:142 has 'MAX_BASH_RETRIES="${ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES:-10}"', and :169-180 restarts on '99|134|139' (that is 9 relaunches, 10 runs in total). main.py:10 has 'MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS = 3'; :211-238 does os.execv, then sys.exit(99); :149-183 and :345-346 handle the resume manifest keyed by ROBODOJO_RUN_ID; :372-432 has 'Abandon broken-env seeds, refill from the seed queue, and retry this round'; :376-377 maps UnStableError to seed_manager.eval_step(), then :434-439 calls get_seeds, which returns the next layout (seed_manager.py:62-77). :85-100 and :111 enable the monitor when the Articulation list is non-empty, and make_toast.yml:1 is 'Articulation:' with the toaster. eval_env.py:247-255 shows setup_scene raising UnStableError from check_layout_stability, which the plan explicitly keeps (PLAN.md:108). One nuance: on PhysXFatal, execv plus resume re-runs make_toast_0 itself, because the layout in progress is neither in eval_result details, from which completed IDs are built (eval_env.py:681-701), nor in abandoned. PhysXBroken and UnStable move on to make_toast_1. Either way a hidden second reset or episode happens. The plan's anti-restart mechanism (supervisor autorestart=false, startretries=0; PLAN.md:116) cannot see an execv (same PID) or a bash loop inside the supervised command. The plan's model-free preview resets (PLAN.md:108, 'Confirm ... initial stability') would expose a natively unstable layout 0 before any model call, but no rule is registered for that case. A stale exported ROBODOJO_RUN_ID would also resume an earlier manifest.

Dockerfile:108-117 writes a second ICD, and :212-220 pins VK_ICD_FILENAMES because 'two ICDs for the same GPU' wedge RTX init. Related: the RoboDojo install doc's Vulkan step ('sudo apt install libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-tools') should be skipped here, as the doc allows ('Skip this step if vulkaninfo already reports a working Vulkan installation'), because mesa-vulkan-drivers would add more ICDs.
verdicts.corrected_statement: libXt.so.6, which Isaac Sim's MaterialX render libraries need at startup per Dockerfile:205-211, is missing and needs a reviewed container-global apt step (libxt6, which is libxt6t64 on noble). That step is lost on recycle. libXinerama1 is missing too, but upstream gives no evidence that headless Isaac Sim needs it; install it only to mirror the Docker image. The HF tree API returns an lfs.oid for each file (for example X5A.urdf 7aaa308a...). The plan's wording ('package ... USD/config ... checksums') does not exclude the two items the finder names, so 'not covered' is overstated. verdicts.reasoning: The gate (PLAN.md:68) is right, and a zero-action policy exists at XPolicyLab 5d0be149: policy/demo_policy/deploy.py (eval_one_episode) and deploy.yml (eval_batch: false). docker/README.md:105-111 says '`success_rate: 0.0` is **expected**'. But 'one selected GPU' has no mechanism, and native defaults do not select a single GPU (activeGpu=0, multiGpu enabled, no maxGpuCount; see PROV-02), on a host where smi GPUs 0-3 hold a live training job. A smoke run through eval_policy.sh would also auto-retry the rc 139 segfault class (new issues). This is the same root issue as PROV-02.

new_issues: The upstream installer accepts Anaconda's Terms of Service on the user's behalf. Where conda is absent it does so after installing Miniconda (install.sh:96-98: '"$HOME/miniconda3/bin/conda" tos accept --override-channels --channel https://repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/main' and '/pkgs/r'). Where conda exists, install.sh:102-103 runs the same accept silently ('2>/dev/null || true'). This is a second license acceptance besides the Omniverse EULA (PROV-10). This box already has /opt/miniforge3 with /root/.condarc 'channels: conda-forge, channel_priority: strict', so creating the runtime env from conda-forge with --override-channels, or with uv, avoids the Anaconda channels entirely. Fold this into the PROV-10 license decision. Severity: minor.

A model-free smoke that reuses eval_policy.sh would hide the PROV-01 crash class. rc 139 is in the automatic retry set (eval_policy.sh:169-180: '139 - SIGSEGV (CUDA driver segfault)', default ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=10, 'sleep 5' between attempts). A deterministic librtx.scenedb segfault (forum 371975: 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)') would therefore trigger about 9 more full Kit startups before the script gives up. Upstream's own smoke lowers this limit only to 2 (smoke_docker.sh:216 '-e ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=2'). Any Stage A smoke should set ROBODOJO_MAX_BASH_RETRIES=1 (no relaunch), or call main.py directly. It should record the first exit code and log as the installation result, and use a fresh ROBODOJO_RUN_ID so a stale resume manifest (main.py:345-346) is never picked up. Severity: minor.

The native EvalEnv cannot be constructed or reset 'model-free' without a reachable WebSocket policy server. eval_env.py:8 imports WsModelClient at module import. eval_env.py:178-180 raises if deploy_cfg has no port, and :188-196 constructs WsModelClient(url=ws://host:port, ...). XPolicyLab 5d0be149 client_server/ws/model_client.py:81 connects with handshake=True inside __init__, so construction fails if no server is listening. eval_env.py:245 reset() calls model_client.call(func_name="reset"). The Stage A completion check (PLAN.md:68, 'no credentials or model transport are involved') therefore needs either XPolicyLab's demo_policy server running locally (smoke_docker.sh starts it 'on the host using the native RoboDojo conda env') or a worker subclass that replaces the client. The plan should say which. This WebSocket boundary is also the natural split between the simulator worker and the model process that Stage B asks for (PLAN.md:72). Severity: minor.

findings.title: Hidden return-to-origin condition is withheld from Astra, so a correctly made toast would score as a native failure
findings.description:
Native full success requires every robot back at its origin end pose. The native instruction omits this, and INPUT_CONTRACT forbids adding it to the task text. uc7.1's own prompt gives the model no way to discover it: 'finish' 'never ends the episode', the model is told to 'recheck unfinished spatial relations', and 'There is no give_up action'.

As written, an agent that inserts both slices and presses the lever but leaves an arm near the toaster fails, with a partial score of at most 50. The only exception is an arm that happens to end within 0.15 m and 20 degrees of its start pose. The episode then continues until action 1400 or a user stop, and observe/finish turns cost 1 action each. Illustratively, 500 extra turns at the 31-55 s per call seen in LIBERO uc7.1 would mean about 4-8 h of subscription use.

The condition is not evaluator-private. The official task page publishes it, the official Astra harness at the pinned XPolicyLab gitlink sends it to the model by default, and it is a benchmark-wide convention. The plan frames it as a run_reward detail and decides the matter itself.
findings.evidence:
Upstream code: make_toast.py:65 'rm.all_robot_back_to_origin()' inside run_reward; :88 'Pick up two slices of bread, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.' reward_manager.py:829 'pos_threshold=0.15, rot_threshold=20'. eval_env.py:854-860.

Public disclosure: https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/sim-tasks/make-toast/ Scoring row '100 Both toaster slots are filled, exactly two bread slices remain on the shelf, the toaster control is pressed down, and the robot returns to origin.' The same row appears in XPolicyLab@5d0be14 inspect/recipes/make_toast.md:24. inspect/policy.py:880-901 appends 'TASK RECIPE:' to the Goal turn, with L4_INSPECT_USE_RECIPE 'Default on'.

Benchmark-wide: an AST scan of the 54 task modules at f57e163 finds 47 that call *_back_to_origin in run_reward, and 0 whose gen_instruction strings mention return, origin or home.

Plan and uc7.1 behaviour: INPUT_CONTRACT.md:29 'return-home check ... not to be imported from run_reward into the model's task text'. src/gpt_field/agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent_client.py:173-177. agent_speedup_v2_user_check_agent.py:361-366 (observe/finish is a 1-step zero motion). LIBERO control time per call: t6 766.7 s / 14 calls, t9 1045.6 s / 34 calls.
findings.recommendation:
Put this to the user before Stage C with three options:
1. Plan default: instruction only, plus an evaluator-only diagnostic recording the first action at which every native run_reward check except all_robot_back_to_origin holds.
2. Reference-harness parity: append the public Scoring table or recipe. This deviates from protocol §2, which keeps success criteria from the model.
3. One benchmark-level, task-agnostic adapter rule for all RoboDojo tasks, for example that episodes end with both arms back at their start poses. INPUT_CONTRACT.md:29 already anticipates a 'public benchmark-wide instruction', and this rule respects the no-per-task-skill rule.

Record the choice in INPUT_CONTRACT and in the preview. Correct the 'imported from run_reward' framing, since the condition is public.

findings.title: Keeping the hidden 1400-action cap departs from the LIBERO no-cap rule and is likely binding at uc7.1's recorded pace
findings.description:
Protocol §1 forbids any total time, action or call cap for full tasks. The plan keeps the native 1400-action horizon (56 s simulated), hides it from the model, and treats any uncapped continuation as a later, separately authorized diagnostic. This is disclosed, but the user was not asked.

The cap is likely to bind. Two of the three recorded uc7.1 LIBERO successes used more simulated time than 56 s: t6 1187 steps = 59.4 s and t9 1572 = 78.6 s, against t8 997 = 49.9 s, all at 20 Hz. Four of the 12 recorded uc7/uc7.1 successes exceeded 56 s. These were single-arm tasks simpler than make_toast, which needs two picks, two oriented insertions, the lever and a return of both arms, and the plan's one-active-arm control is serial.

The reference harness instead reports the remaining env steps in every observation. Because the plan hides the budget, the model behaves the same before action 1400 with or without the cap; the cap only cuts off what happens after it.
findings.evidence: Protocol line 28: '不设置任务总时间、动作数或调用数上限'. PLAN.md:100 'differs explicitly from the unlimited LIBERO episodes'. make_toast.py:15. eval_env.py:858-860. trial/summary.json steps for runs agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001 (1187), _t8_20261028_002 (997), _t9_20261028_001 (1572); uc7 runs 1141 and 2245. XPolicyLab inspect/policy.py:905-913 ('The environment has its own step limit, reported with each observation as the env steps remaining') and :1412-1417; inspect_deploy.py:171-187.
findings.recommendation:
Ask the user to pick one:
- (i) Keep the hidden 1400 cap (plan default).
- (ii) Keep the 1400 cap and add a remaining-actions field. This matches the reference but is a new information type relative to LIBERO.
- (iii) Freeze the official Standard verdict and the transition-mode partial score at action 1400. If authorized up front, continue the same attempt uncapped to obtain a LIBERO-protocol result, reported separately and never replacing the Standard result. This needs step_lim raised in the adapter's env instance and the score snapshotted at action 1400.

In every case, also report the action index at which each sub-goal was reached.

findings.title: Other choices that shape what Astra can do or what the result means are made inside the plan without a decision list
findings.description:
Beyond C1 and C2, the plan fixes these defaults on its own:
- (c) One active arm per fragment while the other holds. The reference harness lets one call move both arms at once, and serial control costs time under a 56 s budget.
- (d) Padded 512x512 canvases instead of native frames; see C10.
- (e) Official layoutID 0 instead of a LIBERO-style relayout. This is justified, but not presented as a choice.
- (f) One pilot instead of the 25-episode Standard set. The reference Astra-medium result on make_toast is score 0.5 and SR 0%, and no listed policy exceeds 5.335% SR, so one episode will very likely fail and says little about rate.
- (g) Video fps is conditional: 'Keep 20fps output if matching the prior video format'.
- (h) It is open whether the initial-plan schema gains an arm assignment and a third camera cell.
- (i) It is open what happens if a uc7.1 native macro cannot be ported: stop, or run a relabeled fragments-only variant.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:82 'Start with one active arm per fragment while the other holds its last commanded state'. XPolicyLab policy.py:130-131 'Naming dimensions of both arms moves them simultaneously along time-aligned paths', and :396 mode 'bimanual'. findings.title: No live model smoke or minimal runnable milestone before the single approved attempt
findings.description:
Every pre-pilot check is model-free: Stage C diagnostics are 'never full task attempts', and the only model call before approval is one planning request. The new dual-ARX execution path, the 18-image history, the new schemas and the new prompts would first meet Astra in the one approved Standard attempt. Any plumbing, schema or controller defect would consume the pilot and produce a result unrelated to the agent's ability.

The user's recorded preference is live-first: build the minimal end-to-end path, run a quick plumbing check and a short smoke, then go live, with model calls for smokes allowed without asking. Zero-action infrastructure failures also happen: 1 of the 4 uc7.1 LIBERO attempts was one.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:90 'These are bounded diagnostics, never full task attempts or task demonstrations sent to the model'. memory v2-live-first-model-calls-ok.md:16-17 ('Build the minimal end-to-end path ..., run a quick plumbing check and a short smoke, then go live'; 'Model calls for checks and smokes are fine without asking'). memory agent-speedup-v2-plan.md:115, user on 2026-10-20: 'can i have a runable version? we did too much checks and evaluation'. runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t8_t9_20261028_001/task_8/trial/summary.json: status subscription_error, steps 0, requests_sent 1 (HTTP 520).
findings.recommendation:
Add a milestone between C/D and E: a minimal end-to-end loop, then a capped live smoke of a few execution calls. Label it diagnostic and never report or reuse it. Run it on a non-pilot official layout (layoutID 1 or later) or on another RoboDojo task, so the pilot layout stays unseen.

After the smoke, allow only plumbing fixes, with no make_toast-specific tuning (the general-framework rule). Then freeze, preview and approve. Optionally ask whether a zero-action infrastructure failure may be re-attempted under the same approval.

findings.title: Some pre-pilot verification goes beyond the LIBERO protocol, with no split into pilot-blocking and deferred work
findings.description:
Items justified by the new embodiment:
- the ARX state and geometry audit
- robot-frame and controller diagnostics
- native action-accounting tests
- three-camera reset and preview
- extending the approval hash to static calibration, which is cheap; the old hash was known to omit geometry.

Items that are LIBERO parity, not new scope:
- separate simulator and model processes
- physics-substep contact sampling
- full-file hashing
- the private supervisor.

Items beyond the protocol and not needed for the first official result:
- byte-level payload inspection as a stage gate ('prove the declared boundary')
- a new versioned release/support/rest evaluator, which the plan leaves possibly before the pilot
- nine contract-test categories
- exact equality of a broader hash as a hard stop on Isaac, where the protocol only requires the observation digest.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:78 'byte-level payload inspection, denylisted-field tests ... prove the declared boundary'. PLAN.md:102 'Plan a separate, versioned evaluator-only check'. PLAN.md:106. Protocol lines 23 and 59. t6 preview_manifest.json:51. trial/collision.json:13. launch_manifest.json (399 file hashes). memory uc7-direction-semantics-fix.md:44 (old hash covers only images, state8 and prompt). memory agent-speedup-v2-plan.md:115.
findings.recommendation: Mark each item 'pilot-blocking' or 'post-pilot'. Keep an allowlist schema test plus a scan of the serialized request for denylisted keys. Defer the new evaluator and any contact analysis beyond record-only logging. Keep the protocol's two-reset digest check, with a documented tolerance fallback.

findings.title: Several LIBERO protocol reporting and operation rules are dropped silently or carried only in part
findings.description:
The plan does not mention:
1. The §7 direction-check layer. It is N/A for make_toast, but the plan should say so.
2. The §8.2 cross-check of requests/ against summary.model_calls.requests_sent and the budget, 'never run_state.model_calls only', the per-kind breakdown, unknown-usage counts, and the formulas for new versus reused requests.
3. The §9 embedded caption and its limitation (target-error field, not obstacle distance or a collision proof).
4. The --stream-progress diagnostic flag.
5. The §8.1 exclusions: initial planning, approval wait, environment start and reset (Isaac startup is long) and post-terminal diagnostics; also that steps/25 simulated time is not completion time.
6. The §4.1 preflight properties (no credentials, no model call, no simulator) and the start --auto-approve caveat for the new CLI.
7. The preflight.json, launch_audit.json and preview_audit.json artifacts that the Task 8 run produced.
findings.evidence: Protocol lines 182, 214-216, 222, 27, 200-202, 70, 145. runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t8_t9_20261028_001/task_8/README.md: 'run_state.model_calls=0 ... 以请求文件和 summary.model_calls.requests_sent=1 为准', plus that task directory's listing. PLAN.md:122 says only 'Report request sends/accepted/errors/retries, planning separately, tokens, subscription/API-key accounting'.

findings.title: Some facts about the reference harness are wrong or missing, and the source audit did not cover XPolicyLab
