findings.title: Ambiguities between PLAN, INPUT_CONTRACT and the provenance files
findings.description:
1. PLAN.md:58 allows importing the uc7.1 core read-only from the shared tree or snapshotting it. INPUT_CONTRACT.md:42 requires the frozen release and no inherited later changes, which only the snapshot guarantees.
2. Arm identity is added to execution targets and fragments (PLAN.md:82), but it is unclear whether the planning prompt and schema change. The prompt is written for 'one parallel-jaw gripper (about 79 mm maximum opening)', and part cells w/x cover only two images.
3. 'One environment' overrides the pinned num_envs: 10 but is not disclosed as an override, unlike the self-collision setting.
4. INPUT_CONTRACT has no row for the execution 'capabilities' block that LIBERO sends in every request.
5. planning_review.json reviewed_at 18:51:02 is earlier than the final PLAN.md write at 18:51:38, and its 'independent_reviews' are unattributed one-liners.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:58; INPUT_CONTRACT.md:16,42. t6 review request instructions ('You plan for a robot arm with one parallel-jaw gripper (about 79 mm maximum opening)'; 'w is the part's cell in image 4 and x its cell in image 2'). sim_config.yml:5 'num_envs: 10'. t6 trial request 000001 context.capabilities: control_hz 20, max_segment_steps 120, max_execution_steps 240, native_macros [hold, turn, place_on, release]. ls --full-time of robodojo_uc71/.
findings.recommendation: Choose the snapshot. State that the planning schema, prompt and validator diffs are frozen before the first planning request. List num_envs=1 as a disclosed override. Add a capabilities/action-interface row to INPUT_CONTRACT. Re-run planning_review after the final edits, and record its timestamp and who or what reviewed.

findings.title: Stages lack effort estimates, measurable exit criteria, feasibility checks and failure branches
findings.description:
Stage D (native action path and per-tick accounting) is a prerequisite for Stage C's controller and diagnostics. Exit criteria are not measurable: B says 'prove' the boundary, C gives no tracking or hold tolerances, E lists tests without pass criteria, and D has none.

The plan has no effort estimate and no consolidated decision checkpoints. It has no go/no-go for:
- Isaac Sim failing to render
- an ARX arm being unable to reach the shelf or the toaster; the shelf and toaster sit on opposite x-sides of the table and the arms are at x = ±0.3
- whether uc7.1's relation vocabulary (hold/turn/slide/place_on/place_in/push_to/release) can express 'press the lever down' and an upright slot insertion; there is no model-free check of this.

Storage: the t6 run takes 784 MB, of which trace.jsonl is 702 MB, at about 0.59 MB per record with two 512x512 images. Three cameras raise this by about 1.5x, /workspace is not persistent, and no off-box sync is planned.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md stage texts; PLAN.md:38. dual_x5.yml:6,14. make_toast.yml:5 (toaster xlim [0.04, 0.35]) and :26 (bread_shelf xlim [-0.35, 0.0]). t6 planning prompt step vocabulary. du of the t6 run directory; trace.jsonl first record 586,290 bytes. planning_manifest.json:88 workspace_is_volume false.
findings.recommendation: Merge D into C or move it ahead. Give each stage a measurable exit check and a failure branch (stop, report or ask). Add an effort estimate and checkpoints after A and after C. Add a model-free reachability and schema-expressibility check that stays general, not tuned to this task. Add an off-box sync (for example HF) for run artifacts.

findings.title: The preferred padded 512x512 canvas puts a quarter of the uc7.1 planning grid on padding
findings.description: Every RoboDojo camera template renders 640x480. An aspect-preserving 512x512 canvas therefore holds 512x384 of content, a 0.8x downscale, with 64-px bars at top and bottom. The uc7.1 planning grid is 8x8 numbered cells of 64 px on a 512 image, so rows 1 and 8 (16 of 64 cells) would fall entirely on padding. This changes what cell numbers mean compared with LIBERO, which delivered native 512x512 renders without resizing.
findings.evidence: env_cfg/camera/template.py:1-21 (GEMINI_345LG, THIRD_VIEW, D435, LARGE_D435 all 'resolution': (640, 480)). camera_config.yml:32-34 cam_head is a Gemini_345Lg; the wrist camera type was not verified. Protocol line 24: '原生 512×512；保留冻结版本的图像变换'. t6 planning request: 'cells 1-64 row-major from the top left', four 512x512 PNGs.
findings.recommendation: Let the user choose between native 640x480 delivery with the grid drawn over the content, and a padded canvas with the grid restricted to the content area. Record the choice in INPUT_CONTRACT and show it in the preview.

The plan's previews/ plus runs/<attempt>/ covers these categories; direction_audit has no counterpart.
Reference Astra (medium, L3 harness) on make_toast, Generalization cell = mean of Std and Rand over 50 episodes: score 0.5, SR 0%. Best listed SR is 5.335% (Xiaomi-Robotics-1).

Reference harness defaults (XPolicyLab@5d0be14): effort medium; 100 LLM calls per episode; image_horizon 2; task recipe appended, with the scoring row that includes 'robot returns to origin'; remaining env steps in every observation; bimanual move_eef; joint action type.
RoboDojo at f57e163: 47 of 54 task modules check *_back_to_origin in run_reward, and 0 of 54 instructions mention it. make_toast tolerance is 0.15 m and 20 degrees.

Native episode rules: step_lim 1400, collect_freq 25, dt 0.004, 10 substeps per action, 56 s simulated. Success only when all checks hold (reward > 1-1e-3), otherwise failure at 1400. arx_x5.yml sets intrinsic_matrix and extrinsic_matrix to false, so native policies receive no camera calibration.

LIBERO uc7.1 successes: t6 1187 steps, 14 calls, 604.86 s; t8_002 997 steps, 14 calls; t9 1572 steps, 34 calls. That is 59.4 / 49.9 / 78.6 s simulated against RoboDojo's 56 s. 4 of 12 uc7/uc7.1 successes exceeded 56 s.
In uc7.1, 'finish' and 'observe' are 1-step zero motions; 'finish' never ends the episode, and there is no give_up action.

Scratch downloads (untrusted data, nothing executed) are in /tmp/claude-0/-workspace/6db53f70-7510-4b1b-9d87-79dcd2a46bba/scratchpad/review_consistency/dl/. Hashes match the manifest for eval_env.py, obs_manager.py, seed_manager.py, reward_manager.py and the report chunk.

verdicts.reasoning:
Re-verified at the pinned commit; files downloaded to challenge_consistency/rd.

The condition is real and must hold in the same step as the rest:
- make_toast.py:56-66: run_reward registers one check group that includes rm.all_robot_back_to_origin() at :65.
- reward_manager.py:376-389: a group is popped only when every check in it holds in the same step.
- eval_env.py:854-860: success needs reward > 1-1e-3; otherwise the episode fails at step_lim=1400 (make_toast.py:15).
- Tolerance: reward_manager.py:829 sets pos 0.15 and rot 20. func_parser.py:1642 applies a per-axis test, np.any(abs(dpos) > 0.15) or rot > 20 deg, for every target arm. The origin is the end pose captured at reset (func_parser.py:54-59, called from eval_env.py:243).
- The partial score is a transition ladder [25, 50] (make_toast.py:69-85) containing neither the lever nor the return, so without the return the best result is a fail at 50.
- The instruction (:88) omits the return.

It is public, not evaluator-private. The task page Scoring row reads '100 Both toaster slots are filled, exactly two bread slices remain on the shelf, the toaster control is pressed down, and the robot returns to origin.' The planning manifest itself lists that page for 'public scoring' (planning_manifest.json:36-38), yet PLAN.md:96 calls these 'Evaluator-only details' and 'hidden finishing conditions'.

The reference harness tells the model in two ways:
- by default, through the recipe (XPolicyLab@5d0be14 inspect/policy.py:880-902; recipes/make_toast.md:24);
- always, in the embodiment notes of every system prompt (docs.py:71-75, wired through deploy.py:41-48 and policy.py:181): 'the work does not score until both arms are back within 0.15 m and 20 degrees of the pose they began the episode in ... Getting home is the last step of the task ... keep enough env steps in hand to make it.'

uc7.1 gives the agent no way to learn of the condition: 'finish' never ends the episode and there is no give_up (agent_client.py:173-177), and observe/finish are 1-step zero motions (agent.py:361-367).

Why blocker: a manipulation-complete episode becomes a native failure for a reason the agent cannot infer, while the benchmark's own reference model is told. LIBERO instructions state every qualitative sub-goal, so 'same info type' would be met only in form.

Three corrections, none of which weakens the finding:
- My AST scan agrees that 47/54 tasks check the return. However, 6 of those 47 instructions do say 'then reset the robot arm' (align_blocks, classify_objects_by_language, pour_by_language, solve_equation, stack_blocks_by_language, store_tools_in_toolbox). So '0 mention it' is true only for the keywords searched.
- The report says only that the model sees 'the official instruction'. Whether the campaign had the recipe on is unstated, and docs.py makes that question moot.
- The cost figure counts video time. Model latency per call was 18.0-29.0 s (model_pipeline_s_by_kind: t6 406.4 s/14, t8_002 360.7 s/14, t9 613.6 s/34), and wall time per call excluding video was 24-43 s. 500 turns is therefore about 2.5-6 h, not 4-8 h.

The LIBERO protocol forbids episode caps.
- Protocol line 28: '不设置任务总时间、动作数或调用数上限' (no cap on total task time, actions or calls).
- The user earlier explicitly rejected a 15-minute cap (AGENTS.md:2168).

The plan keeps the native cap and hides it.
- PLAN.md:21 and :98-100 keep 1400 actions and say the plan 'differs explicitly from the unlimited LIBERO episodes'.
- INPUT_CONTRACT.md:24 keeps the remaining budget evaluator-only.
- The cap is disclosed in the plan but not offered to the user as a choice.

The cap is likely to bind.
- Steps for the uc7.1 successes, from each trial/summary.json:
  - t6: 1187 steps, 59.35 s
  - t8_002: 997 steps, 49.85 s
  - t9: 1572 steps, 78.6 s
- Among uc7 successes, fix_full t0 took 1141 steps (57.05 s) and relayout t0 took 2245 (112.25 s). That makes 4 of 12 successes longer than 56 s; the uc7 task-1 runs were not successes.
- These steps are physical motion time. In t6, step_budget.by_phase shows framework_fragment 1186 of 1187. PLAN.md:86 preserves limits in physical units, so seconds carry over.
- The reference harness reports remaining steps and moves both arms, yet its own docstring says the step limit is what ends episodes: inspect/deploy.py:171-177, 'This, not the LLM call budget, is what actually runs out'. Its embodiment notes also tell the model to keep steps in hand for the return home (docs.py:74-75).

The argument that a hidden cap only truncates the run is sound. A model that does not know the limit behaves identically before action 1400, so option (iii) costs nothing extra up to that point.

Citation nuance: the EEF agent's actual system message is policy.py:163-182, which overrides inspect/policy.py:905-918. Both state the step limit.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Evidence and conclusion hold. One addition: the reference harness itself documents that the step limit is the usual episode-ender (inspect/deploy.py:174-175), even with the remaining-step field and bimanual moves. This decision must be made together with C1 (see new_issues).

verdicts.reasoning:
A decisions table would help, but most of the listed items are disclosed defaults or implementation details.

- (c) The one-active-arm text (PLAN.md:82) and the reference's simultaneous moves (policy.py:130-131) are verified. However, the reference's own notes advise 'move one arm at a time whenever either target is uncertain' (docs.py:82-84), so a serial default is defensible. It matters mainly through C2's cap.
- (d) is C10.
- (e) Layout 0 is the natural reading of 'standard version'. Protocol line 29 is one layout per approval, so this is no real open choice.
- (f) PLAN.md:26 and README.md:9 already say one pilot gives no rate. The base rate is verified: report chunk column J[0] is gpt-6-astra with make_toast {score:.5, sr:0}, and the maximum SR is 5.335 (Xiaomi-Robotics-1). Pre-registering the layout order is a good addition.
- (g) The conditional fps (PLAN.md:120) is trivial.
- (h) PLAN.md:72 already commits to six images with 'separate camera selectors'. The schema detail belongs to the reviewed diff (PLAN.md:127).
- (i) PLAN.md:88 says 'return an explicit implementation gap rather than quietly run a reduced method under the original label', so this branch is only partly open.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Before Stage C, put to the user only C1, C2 and C10, plus arm concurrency (c) because it interacts with the 1400 cap. Pre-register the layout order for any later expansion and cite the reference base rate (Astra 0.5 score / 0% SR; best listed SR 5.335%). The other items are disclosed defaults or implementation details already covered by the reviewed-diff requirement.

verdicts.reasoning:
The new execution path first meets Astra in the approved attempt.
- Every check before approval is model-free (PLAN.md:68, :90, :108).
- The only model call is one planning request (PLAN.md:110).
- The deliverables include no live execution check (PLAN.md:126-131).
- So the new dual-ARX execution prompts, schema, capabilities and 18-image history (INPUT_CONTRACT.md:18) are first sent to Astra in the approved attempt.

A defect there would use up the pilot. Protocol line 87 consumes the approval before the first execution request: '即使随后零动作就失败，也不能复用已消费的审批' (even if it then fails with zero actions, the consumed approval cannot be reused).

The user's recorded preference is live-first:

gaps.title: Process and thread architecture is unspecified: the frozen transport rules out hosting the executive behind the native websocket, and the fork's Kit hang detector (120 s) meets long frozen waits
gaps.why_it_matters:
Suggested severity: major; blocker if the websocket split is adopted. PLAN.md:72 says only 'Separate the simulator worker from the model process'. Two reviewers float hosting the executive behind the native XPolicyLab websocket: NT-4 analyses that placement, and the provisioning new issue calls the ws boundary 'the natural split ... that Stage B asks for (PLAN.md:72)'.

Why the websocket placement fails. The protocol requires a 180 s deadline (protocol:27), and the frozen transport implements it with a main-thread SIGALRM. Off the main thread, `_request_deadline` raises `request_deadline_unavailable`: 'Request deadline requires a POSIX main thread' (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_transport.py:104-110). The file hash efcfa14a matches uc71_release_manifest.json. That code is never retried; only server_is_overloaded and four stream/network codes are (agent_speedup_v2_client.py:149-150, 903-914). The XPolicyLab server runs a sync model method as `await asyncio.to_thread(method, *args)` (model_server.py:393), which is not the main thread. An async wrapper around the blocking transport would instead stall the 20 s/20 s keepalive pings (model_server.py:58-59, 110-111; protocol/client.py:112-113). Either way the first execution request fails with 0 actions. The plan has no live execution smoke (C4), so this would consume the single approved attempt.

The LIBERO layout works. There the runner's main thread owns every model call, and t6 shows 14/14 results 'valid' with request_deadline_s 180 under 'POSIX main-thread SIGALRM'.

Simulator side. While the model thinks, the worker's main thread blocks in `for line in sys.stdin` (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:93-99). The RoboDojo IsaacLab fork sends every AppLauncher branch, including headless with cameras, to isaaclab.python.kit (fork app_launcher.py:729-749). Upstream Isaac Lab v2.3.2 uses headless.rendering.kit for that case (app_launcher.py:727), and that kit has no hang-detector setting. The fork's kit sets `hangDetector.enabled = true` and `hangDetector.timeout = 120` (apps/isaaclab.python.kit:172-173). The protocol allows one send to run 180 s, plus backoff waits of up to 60 s (protocol:163-168). The t6 maximum was 68.3 s, and a uc7 relayout planning request has already hit 180 s. Kit documentation says the detector 'will notify the user that a hang is detected and can crash the application if the user chooses'. What it does in headless mode is unverified. PLAN.md:98 'Freeze simulation while awaiting Astra' was checked only at the eval_env/main.py level, not at the Kit level.
gaps.what_to_check:
(1) Write into Stage B that the uc7.1 runner process makes every Astra call on its main thread, as in LIBERO. The Isaac worker should be a child process on the existing JSON-lines protocol (agent_speedup_v2_sim.py:312 Popen pattern). EvalEnv's ws client should be satisfied by a credential-free no-op server, or removed by a reviewed subclass. Explicitly reject hosting the executive behind XPolicyLab ws or inside the Isaac process. Add a unit test showing that a deadline-enabled request issued from the adapter's real call site does not raise request_deadline_unavailable.
(2) Add a model-free Stage A test. After reset, block the worker's main thread for 300 s without app.update, then run one hold action and get_obs. Record any hang-detector log, crash dump or exit code, and compare articulation and object state hashes from before and after the wait. If Kit crashes, set `--/app/hangDetector/enabled=false` (or a timeout above the worst-case decision wait) through kit_args. Bind that in the launch manifest and disclose it as a launch-setting change. Any keep-alive must be shown not to step physics.
(3) Consider one capped live execution smoke from the real adapter process before approval. The user allows smokes: memory v2-live-first-model-calls-ok.md, 'Model calls for checks and smokes are fine without asking'.

gaps.title: No positive or negative control shows the adapter can register native success, the partial score and termination; lever retention and attainability on Standard are unproven
gaps.why_it_matters:
Suggested severity: major. Every scoring check in the plan is on the failure side: 'native score is initially incomplete' (PLAN.md:68), 'initially incomplete success' (PLAN.md:108) and '1400-action termination' (PLAN.md:128). Diagnostics are 'never full task attempts' (PLAN.md:90), and INPUT_CONTRACT.md:40 allows ground truth only 'for checking correctness'. Nothing shows the success branch working through the adapter's own action path. That branch needs reward_manager.step and is_episode_end after every native action (eval_env.py:457,465), the latch on reward > 1-1e-3 (eval_env.py:854-857), skipped actions after the end (eval_env.py:368-369), and the adapter recording official success and completion time.

Three verified facts make this load-bearing.
(a) Native `success` starts True (eval_env.py:114,218). A broken end-flag path can turn an early return into success (NT-3), and a naive 'initially incomplete' check that reads env.success fails at reset.
(b) Lever retention is unverified (NT-13, F9 notes). Layout 0's toaster has `physics: {type: articulation}` with no reset_drive (make_toast_0.json sha f78afb3f; articulation.py:245-246), so behaviour after release depends on the USD drive. Full success needs the lever ratio above 0.85 and both arms home at the same action (make_toast.py:58-66).
(c) The evidence that full success is attainable comes from Generalization cells that pool Standard and Random. Standard uses toaster models [0,1] (config make_toast.yml:12-15; layout 0 has category_idx 1) and a 0.03-0.065 m slot window (make_toast.py:9-10). Random uses other models and a -0.05 to 0.068 m window (make_toast_random.py:9-10). Attainability on Standard alone was not established by any reviewer.

If the success branch is broken or unreachable on this layout, a pilot failure cannot be told apart from a harness failure, which meets the blocker definition 'fail for a reason unrelated to the agent's ability'. This goes beyond C9 and the consistency reachability suggestion, which concern kinematic and vocabulary reach, not scoring.
gaps.what_to_check:
Add an evaluator-only control suite, labeled offline and never model-visible, that runs through the adapter's real worker and action path before the preview. Get the user's explicit OK that it is not a 'full task attempt' under PLAN.md:90.
(i) Positive control. After reset, write bread_0 and bread_1 upright into toast_slot1 and toast_slot2 within the z-window, set toaster joint_1 past 0.85 of its range, and leave both arms at their reset pose. Send one hold action. Expect reward above 1-1e-3, success and end_flag latched, the adapter reporting official success and stopping, and later actions as no-ops.
(ii) Score ladder. One slot filled with both grippers open should score 25, then 50 at a later action. Assert exactly one reward step per native action.
(iii) Negative controls, each of which must record no success: one arm 0.2 m off its origin; the lever at 0.5; three slices off the shelf; one slice tipped; and an operator stop at action 5, which must record failure rather than the True default.
(iv) Lever retention. Drive joint_1 to its pressed limit, release it, hold 200 native actions with no contact, and log the ratio.
(v) On the live leaderboard, confirm in the Standard column, not the Generalization cell, that some policy has a nonzero full success rate on make_toast.

gaps.why_it_matters:
Suggested severity: minor to major, depending on the C1/C2 horizon decisions.

The frozen client retries only server_is_overloaded (HTTP 503 or no status) and four stream/network codes (agent_speedup_v2_client.py:139-150, 903-914). The codes rate_limit_exceeded and insufficient_quota are recognized (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_transport.py:45-52) but never retried. The attempt therefore finalizes immediately (PLAN.md:118) and cannot be rerun (protocol:163-166, 170).

The t6 budget records max_api_calls, max_cost_usd and max_wall_time_s as null, with 'account subscription limits apply' (trial/requests/000014-4e083fb9766f4577ba39084f81be8944.result.json). Input tokens per request rose from 7,145 to 82,735, about 5.5K per turn, for 646,475 in total over 14 requests. Cumulative input therefore grows roughly quadratically: about 7M tokens at 50 requests, 28M at 100 and 100M at 190. These figures are before the third view and dual-arm text are added.

The native_task, astra_report and libero_parity new issues expect a long post-completion or observe loop under the uncapped horizon. A quota stop is therefore a plausible ending that is unrelated to the agent and could fall at any point in the episode. PLAN.md:122 covers only request and token accounting.

Three reviewers say measured: the native_interface key facts ('state.{left|right}_arm_joint_state[6] is measured'), the NI-1 challenge ('The native obs action block copies the measured arm joints (obs_manager.py:173-174)') and the libero_parity key facts. Verified at f57e1633: obs_manager.py:173-174 write the measured joints, then the prev_control loop (obs_manager.py:190) overwrites both blocks for arm keys, action at :209 and state at :211, with the last commanded substep target. prev_control is updated on every substep pop (control_manager.py:81-86,117-131), and the last 2 of 10 substeps hold the action target (eval_env.py:519-531). Port_feasibility is right. Native state and action arm joints and grippers are command echoes; only <side>_ee_pose (get_real_endpose, obs_manager.py:177) is measured. Measured joints for INPUT_CONTRACT row 11 must come from robot_manager.get_joint, not from the native obs dict.

Horizon binding. Port_feasibility Mapping S ('about 400-650 actions ... Not binding') assumes near-full tracking of uc7.1's 0.02 m per action transit cap, and this is unmeasured. Native_interface NI-2 reports upstream measurements that joint targets above about 0.05 rad per action do not land, and that near the folded home pose forward TCP motion is about 2-3 mm per action (sigma_min 0.041 m/rad). Both arms start at that pose and must end there for full success. Under NI-2, Mapping S is optimistic, so the 'not binding' scenario should not be used until a model-free per-action TCP-speed measurement exists.

Remedy conflict over native main.py. NT-2, NI-3 and PROV-03 recommend bypassing or neutralizing main.py's retry and layout-substitution loop. But PhysX broken-env detection and the NaN backstop are wired only through main.py (main.py:111-121,270; EvalEnv default physx_monitor_enabled=False at eval_env.py:63). Each remedy trades auto-retry for the loss of native physics-validity detection unless the adapter replicates it (gap 3).

Architecture conflict. The provisioning new issue calls the XPolicyLab websocket 'the natural split between the simulator worker and the model process that Stage B asks for', and NT-4 analyses that placement under the 120 s client timeout. The frozen uc7.1 transport rules the placement out. Its deadline needs the process main thread (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_transport.py:104-110), and XPolicyLab runs sync model methods via asyncio.to_thread (model_server.py:393). Every request would fail with the non-retryable request_deadline_unavailable before any 120 s timeout applies.

Severity disagreements to reconcile. (a) The return-home and hidden-conditions finding is a blocker in NT-1, astra_report F1 and consistency C1, but the LP-1 challenge downgrades it to major. (b) On the 100-call statement at PLAN.md:30, libero_parity claim:26 says the plan matches the report ('REFUTED -> note'), while astra_report claim:6/F2 says the plan is wrong (CONFIRMED -> minor) and NT-7 and C7 rate it minor. Both readings are factually right: the report page mentions 100 calls only in its robustness section, while the linked paper §3.3 and the harness default (inspect/policy.py:161) apply the cap to every benchmark run. The final review should cite both sources.

t6 timing figures use different denominators. native_task's 'about 52 s per request cycle' is budget.elapsed_s 724.86 / 14 and includes control and video between requests. libero_parity's '28.8 s per request' is stream time 402.6 / 14, model time only. The 604.86 s completion time is control time minus video. Any estimate of post-completion-loop exposure (for example '500 calls, about 7 h') should state which figure it uses.

Reset preparation totals. native_interface gives 'at least 501 steps, about 2 s simulated'. native_task's verified sequence is 1 reload + 300 TaskEnv.reset + 20+20 saved-pose settling + 300 stability check + 200 settle, at least 841 physics steps or about 3.4 s. The gap is the stability check and the saved-pose steps. It does not affect the 1400-action count, but the PLAN.md:108 reset record should use the full sequence.

findings.title: Stage B must pin the executive to the uc7.1 runner's main thread and forbid hosting it behind the ws server or inside Isaac
findings.description:
As written, PLAN.md:72 allows any split between simulator and model. The frozen transport works only on the POSIX main thread with no ITIMER_REAL already active (transport.py:103-113).

Hosting the executive behind the XPolicyLab ws server fails either way:
- With a sync Model, the call runs via asyncio.to_thread. It raises request_deadline_unavailable before any HTTP send. The error is not retried, so the attempt ends as subscription_error with 0 actions.
- With an async inline wrapper, the call blocks the server's event loop. Every long decision then depends on a keepalive drop, a single reconnect and a cached replay.
- In both cases, EvalEnv's ws client has a default request_timeout_s of 120 s, and the client treats a timeout as fatal for the trial. That is below the 180 s protocol deadline.

The stop and finalization handlers also only work on the main thread. Off it they silently do nothing, so PLAN.md:118's 'user stop at complete feedback boundaries' would be lost.

Hosting inside Isaac breaks two other requirements. It puts credentials in the simulator process, against PLAN.md:58. It also runs the frozen core under Isaac's Python 3.11 instead of the frozen 3.12.14 runner environment.

The approval is claimed before the simulator starts, so the first bad request uses up the single approved attempt, as Task 8 did.
findings.evidence: transport.py:108-113. XPolicyLab@5d0be149 model_server.py:390-396, 549, 628. protocol/client.py:91 'request_timeout_s: float = 120.0'; lines 523-530 'callers must treat a timeout as fatal for the trial'. RoboDojo@f57e1633 src/eval_client/eval_env.py:188-196 passes no request_timeout_s. Main-thread-only handlers: scripts/evaluate_bowl_field_history.py:177-179 (termination_as_interrupt yields without a handler off the main thread) and scripts/evaluate_agent_speedup_v1.py:288-290 (_FinalizationSignals.install returns early off the main thread). The LIBERO wrapper forwards a stop as SIGINT (runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/run_once.py:52-59). Python versions: /workspace/gpt_field/.venv is Python 3.12.14 (protocol:23 names it as the main process); RoboDojo scripts/install.sh:107 'python=3.11'. Approval claim before sim start: evaluate_agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:590-595. All cited local files hash-match uc71_release_manifest.json.
findings.recommendation:
Write into Stage B:
- The uc7.1 runner process, in /workspace/gpt_field/.venv (Python 3.12), issues every Astra request, both planning and execution, on its main thread, as in LIBERO.
- The Isaac worker is a child process spawned with the V2SimProcess Popen pattern (agent_speedup_v2_sim.py:306-319) under _simulator_without_credentials, speaking JSON lines on a dup'd file descriptor.
- EvalEnv's mandatory WsModelClient is satisfied by a credential-free no-op XPolicyLab server, as the official GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF does, or removed by a reviewed override.
- Hosting the executive behind the XPolicyLab ws server or inside the Isaac process is explicitly rejected.

Add two tests:
- From the adapter's real call site, monkeypatch protocol._open_public as tests/test_agent_speedup_v2_user_check_transport.py:137-147 does. A deadline-enabled request must raise request_deadline_exceeded, not request_deadline_unavailable, with no ITIMER_REAL active.
- A SIGINT or SIGTERM sent through the single-use wrapper finalizes the attempt at a feedback boundary.

findings.title: Kit's hang detector (on, 120 s) meets frozen Astra and approval waits, and its headless behavior is untested
findings.description:
The fork sends headless camera runs to isaaclab.python.kit, which turns the hang detector on with a 120 s timeout. Kit's default is off, and upstream v2.3.2's headless rendering kit does not set it.

PLAN.md:98's freeze means Kit gets no app.update while the worker waits on stdin. That happens:
- During the prepare planning request, because LIBERO keeps the worker alive through it.
- During each execution decision. t6 peaked at 70.2 s; the protocol allows 180 s per send, waits of up to 60 s, and several sends per decision.
- During human approval, if the adapter keeps Isaac alive while 'awaiting ... approval' (PLAN.md:98). That idle could last minutes to hours.

LIBERO never leaves a simulator idle across human approval. prepare closes it before review, and run starts a fresh one.

Kit's docs say the detector notifies the user and can crash the application, and that 'extensions can choose to disable it'. Observed uc7.1 waits all stayed under 120 s (0 of 66 requests). So the risk is infrequent, but it would end the single attempt for a reason unrelated to the agent.

Upstream's own Astra integration also blocks Kit's main thread on every LLM call. It caps each attempt at 90 s, so it says nothing about waits over 120 s.
findings.evidence: yuechen0614/IsaacLab@afca7b09 app_launcher.py:729-749 and apps/isaaclab.python.kit:172-173. isaac-sim/IsaacLab@v2.3.2 app_launcher.py:727 (headless.rendering.kit, 0 hangDetector lines). Kit configuring guide: '/app/hangDetector/enabled (default: false)'. kit_core_iapp_interface.html: 'can crash the application if the user chooses'. Prepare keeps the sim alive: evaluate_agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:251-306. The sim is closed before review (lines 304-306, 903) and a fresh one is started for the run (scripts/evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:1364-1369). t6 trace.jsonl max decision_latency_s is 70.2. Retry limits: protocol:163-168. Upstream cap: XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/run_fixed_layout.sh:31 'L4_INSPECT_HARD_TIMEOUT_S...:-90'. IsaacLab simulation_context.py:575-576 'FIXME: This steps physics as well'; lines 616-618 and 625-627 wrap app.update in playSimulations=False.
findings.recommendation:
Add a model-free Stage A test. After reset, block the worker's main thread for at least 300 s with no app.update, then run one hold action and get_obs. Record Kit logs, crash dumps and the exit code. Compare articulation state, object state and all three images against a control run with no idle.

If anything fires or the result is ambiguous, launch with kit_args '--/app/hangDetector/enabled=false'. Prefer this to a longer timeout, because the wait per decision has no fixed cap. Bind it in the launch manifest and disclose it as a launch-setting change with no effect on task or physics.

Any keep-alive must go through IsaacLab's render path, which sets /app/player/playSimulations=False around app.update. Never call a bare app.update. Show that the keep-alive does not change later images or native action accounting.

State the process lifecycle explicitly. Either follow LIBERO (close Isaac after prepare; at run, start fresh and check the approved observation hash), or justify a persistent process with the detector disabled and proof that the state does not drift while idle.

findings.title: Reusing the LIBERO JSON-lines client unchanged would kill a slow Isaac start at 120 s, after the approval is already claimed
findings.description:
SimProcess._request kills the worker if a reply takes longer than LiberoConfig.response_timeout_s, which defaults to 120 s. The worker is built lazily on the first 'metadata' request. So Kit start-up, EvalEnv construction and the WsModelClient connect must all fit in one 120 s budget. If no server is up, that connect keeps retrying for up to 900 s.

Native reset shares the same per-operation budget. It includes a stability check, 10 renders and 200 settle steps, plus a model_client.call('reset').

The approval is claimed before sim.start, so a start-up timeout in the approved run uses up the attempt with 0 actions. The RoboCasa adapter already needed 300 s.

Ordering matters too:
- make_toast has an Articulation section, so main.py starts the PhysX monitor, which dup2's pipes over file descriptors 1 and 2. The protocol fd must be duplicated before the monitor and AppLauncher start, as the uc7.1 worker does.
- stdout cannot carry the protocol: eval_env prints per-action progress there, and WsModelClient prints RECONNECT lines.
- SimProcess.close kills only the direct child process.
findings.evidence: /workspace/gpt_field/src/gpt_field/libero.py:42 'response_timeout_s: float = 120.0'; lines 609-617 'simulator response timed out; worker terminated'. agent_speedup_v2_sim.py:315; agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:94-95 and 102-103. robocasa_user_check_sim.py:46 'response_timeout_s: float = 300.0'. Approval claim: evaluate_agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:590-595. XPolicyLab model_client.py:81 connects at construction; protocol/client.py:102-108 sets 180 attempts and 900 s. RoboDojo eval_env.py:245, 247-264 and 372-375; main.py:85-121; physx_warning_monitor.py:449-450 and 478-484 (blob 7c32221b); task/RoboDojo/config/make_toast.yml:1 'Articulation:'.
findings.recommendation:
Specify per-operation worker timeouts for start/metadata, reset, step and evaluator operations. Measure them in Stage A on a cold cache and bind them in the launch manifest.

Fix the start-up order: no-op server first, then the worker. Inside the worker: duplicate the protocol fd, redirect stderr, start the PhysX monitor, then AppLauncher.

At close, kill the process group and verify that no Kit descendants remain.

Run Stage E's two model-free resets through the exact launch topology, with the same timeouts and cache paths, so start-up timing is proven before approval.

findings.title: Native restart and resume paths restart the whole episode and are invisible to supervisor startretries=0
findings.description:
On a PhysX fatal error, RoboDojo's main.py re-execs itself in the same PID up to 3 times. eval_policy.sh then retries up to 10 times on exit codes 99, 134 or 139. The PhysX monitor's watchdog force-exits with rc=99 45 s after a fatal error that nothing handled.

os.execv keeps the PID, so the supervisor's autorestart=false and startretries=0 (PLAN.md:116) cannot detect it. The resume manifest would then continue the evaluation, which breaks the one-attempt rule (PLAN.md:22). The plan never says the worker bypasses main.py's loop and eval_policy.sh.
findings.evidence: RoboDojo@f57e1633 src/eval_client/main.py:10 'MAX_INPROC_RESTARTS = 3'; line 236 os.execv; lines 237-238 sys.exit(99). scripts/eval_policy.sh:142 'MAX_BASH_RETRIES=...:-10'; lines 169-180 retry on 99|134|139. src/eval_client/physx_warning_monitor.py:212 FATAL_FORCE_EXIT_GRACE_S=45.0; line 936 os._exit(99).
findings.recommendation: State that the worker calls create_eval_env, reset and take_action directly, and never runs main.py's eval loop or eval_policy.sh. Disable or ignore the resume manifest. Treat a PhysX fatal, rc 99 or worker EOF as an infrastructure error that ends the attempt with no restart. Add a lifecycle test showing that a simulated worker exit finalizes the attempt.

findings.title: Add one capped live execution smoke from the real process topology, kept off the pilot layout
findings.description:
The failure modes in GAP0-1 to GAP0-3 only appear under real model latency in the real process topology. The first execution request is usually the longest wait (t6 step 0: 70.2 s).

The plan has no live execution smoke. The user allows capped smokes, and the runner already supports --stop-after-steps and smoke settings.

Running the smoke on the pilot layout itself would preview the model's behavior on the exact test scene. That conflicts with the spirit of PLAN.md:24's selection rule.
findings.evidence: t6 trace.jsonl decision_latency_s, step 0 = 70.2. Memory file v2-live-first-model-calls-ok.md: 'one-episode or capped smokes' and 'Model calls for checks and smokes are fine without asking'. evaluate_agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:807 '--stop-after-steps'; execution_options takes smoke/smoke_steps (lines 298-302). protocol:28: full attempts never use smoke mode or --stop-after-steps.
findings.recommendation: Before asking for approval, run one capped diagnostic: the planning request, the first 1-2 execution requests and a few native actions. Use the real runner, the Isaac child and the no-op server, on a different official make_toast layout. Give it its own review and output, label it a smoke, never count it as the Standard attempt, and report its request counts separately.

findings.title: Upstream's own Astra integration is precedent for a no-op server and for keeping HTTP outside Isaac, but not for long waits
findings.description:
XPolicyLab policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF works as follows:
- It serves a no-op ws Model that only satisfies the harness.
- It ignores model_client and runs the LLM loop inside the Isaac client process.
- It runs each HTTP call in a short-lived subprocess with a hard deadline, enforced by communicate(timeout) plus killpg rather than by signals.
- It blocks Kit's main thread for up to 90 s per attempt, with 3 retries by default.

So it supports the no-op server and the 'HTTP outside Isaac' choices. It does not cover waits over 120 s, and it does not meet PLAN.md:58, because its API key lives in the Isaac process environment.

findings.title: No control exercises the adapter's native success, score and termination path, and three verified native traps can fake or block success
findings.description: The adapter must recreate RoboDojo's episode bookkeeping: registration, a reward step per action, the success latch, the horizon, and marking an operator stop. The plan has no positive or negative control showing this works. Three upstream behaviours make the gap load-bearing. (T1) env.success defaults to True, and native run_eval counts any env still True as a success, so a stop, model 'done' or error that returns without an end flag is scored as success. (T2) Success and score checks are registered in run_eval, after reset has cleared them. A worker that bypasses run_eval without calling run_reward()/get_score() gets get_reward()=1.0 and latches success before any action. Registering twice adds a second stage, so success then needs two separate reward steps; re-registering the score resets the 25/50 progress. (T3) Setting success False to mean 'incomplete' disables reward evaluation and ends the episode at the next is_episode_end. The official reference Astra adapter needed explicit code for T1, and upstream CLAUDE.md lists 'check_success always True' as a common pitfall. No LLM-agent row has exercised even the 25-point ladder on Standard: GPT-6-Astra Standard make_toast is score 0, SR 0. As written, a pilot outcome could be a harness artefact, either a false success or an unregistrable one, and nothing before launch would show which.
findings.evidence: T1: eval_env.py:114,218 `self.success = [True] * self.num_envs`; :799-803 counts `if self.success[env_idx]` as success; XPolicyLab@5d0be149 policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/deploy.py:331-351 `_mark_incomplete_episode_failed`, called at :712-714. T2: eval_env.py:772-774 (`self.run_reward()`, `self.get_score()` inside run_eval); make_toast.py:21-23 reset -> reward_manager.reset (reward_manager.py:39-42 clears check_list/score_list); reward_manager.py:536-541 returns 1.0 when check_list, final_check_list and trigger_check_list are empty; :64-66 check() appends; :383-389 pops one stage per step; :117-131 _register_score resets score_completed_count. T3: func_parser.py:61-62; reward_manager.py:379,394,533; eval_env.py:845-860. Upstream CLAUDE.md:253 '`check_success` always `True` -> garbage eval metrics'. Live leaderboard index-Ds7ePAw3.js: `"GPT-6-Astra":{..."make_toast":{"score":0,"successRate":0},"make_toast_random":{"score":1,"successRate":0}`. Plan: PLAN.md:68,108,128 (failure-side only); PLAN.md:106 ('native horizon/success', unspecified).
findings.recommendation: Add an offline 'scoring-path control suite' to stage E and to the section 5 deliverables, to run after the adapter tests and before the two model-free resets and preview. It runs through the adapter's real simulator worker and its per-tick take_action path, with no model process or transport. Results are stored under validation/, labeled offline and never model-visible, and the pilot starts from a fresh reset. INPUT_CONTRACT.md:40 already permits this and PLAN.md:90 does not forbid it, so listing it in the revised plan the user approves is enough; no separate authorization is needed. Expected results on layout 0: (a) Registration. After reset plus registration (or the native run_eval entry), check_list holds exactly 1 stage, the score is transition mode with [25, 50], get_reward() is 0 and the score is 0. Log the reset predicate table. (b) Positive latch. Inject bread_0 and bread_1 upright and resting under physics in toast_slot1 and toast_slot2, and log z_diff, which must be in (0.03, 0.065). A standing slice's root sits about 0.0585 m above its lower edge, so the edge must lie at most 6.5 mm above the slot plane. Set toaster joint_1 to at least 0.045 m (ratio >= 0.91 of [-0.0234, 0.0516]) and keep both arms at their reset pose. One hold action should give success True and end_flag True at take_action_cnt 1, with the adapter recording official_success, termination=success and the completion action. A further call must leave the counter and physics unchanged, and the adapter must then stop calling take_action. (c) Ladder. One slot filled with both grippers at least 0.8 open gives 25; both slots give 50, no earlier than the next action. Exactly one reward_manager.step runs per native action. (d) Negatives, each over 5 or more hold actions, must never latch success: one arm displaced at least 0.2 m along a single axis; lever ratio 0.5; shelf count 1 and 3; one bread tilted more than 30 deg. Also, an operator stop at action 5 must record success False and end_flag True through the reference pattern (set success False, then call is_episode_end), with termination=user_stop and completion time N/A. (e) Horizon edge. Success at action 1400 latches, a failing run ends at 1400, and action 1401 is skipped. Also state which entry point the worker uses: native run_eval with an XPolicyLab-style deploy module, or its own loop that must call run_reward()/get_score() exactly once per reset.

findings.title: The 'initially incomplete' checks are undefined against native semantics and give misleading results if implemented literally
findings.description: Stage A requires 'native score is initially incomplete' and stage E 'initially incomplete success'. Natively, env.success reads True at reset, get_reward() returns 1.0 until run_reward() has registered the checks, and the process score is trivially 0. A literal implementation therefore fails spuriously, passes vacuously, or invites T3. Stage A in particular runs before the adapter exists, where a custom reset script is likely to omit registration.
findings.evidence: PLAN.md:68 'native score is initially incomplete'; PLAN.md:108 'Confirm target visibility, initial stability and initially incomplete success'. eval_env.py:218 (success True at reset); reward_manager.py:536-541 (1.0 with empty lists); eval_env.py:772-774 (registration in run_eval only). Expected layout-0 values at reset: bread default_ori (0.7016, 0.0880, 0.7016, -0.0880) maps local -x to world up, so all four breads pass the axis-up test; four breads sit in the shelf, so is_N_A_in_B(N=2) is false; toaster/00001 joint_1 is at rest 0.0, ratio (0-(-0.0234))/0.075 = 0.312 < 0.85; home is true by construction (func_parser.py:54-59).
findings.recommendation: Redefine both checks as an evaluator-only predicate table plus get_reward()==0, taken after registration. Expected layout-0 values: slot1 F, slot2 F, upright x4 T, shelf==2 F (count 4), lever ratio about 0.31 F, home T, score 0. Report env.success as the native 'not yet failed' flag, never as task status.

findings.title: Lever retention is low-risk by the asset's own drive parameters; record them, keep a cheap check, do not gate on it
findings.description: The concern that a released lever might spring back before the arms reach home is largely answered by the USD. In both Standard toaster models the lever joint is a prismatic joint with a damping-only drive (stiffness 0, damping 100, target 0), and gravity is disabled on the lever link. Nothing pushes a pressed lever back up. Pressing raises the ratio: joint +Y maps to base -Z, so 'down' is positive, consistent with the '> 0.85' test. The ratio threshold needs 4.04 cm of travel on 00001 and about 5.25 cm on 00000. Contact while releasing could still drag the lever, which a short simulated hold would show. This is the unverified remainder.

Toaster/00000 (sha256 0d80971f...): stiffness 0.0, damping 100.0, limits [-0.0138, 0.0642], rest 0.00064, link_1 disableGravity True. Metadata toaster/00001: passive functional `toast_botton` with parent_joint `joint_1`. Keep the gap's lever-retention item as a cheap evaluator-only check: hold joint_1 at the upper limit for 200 actions, then release with gripper contact and log the ratio. It should not gate the pilot.

findings.title: Standard full success is attainable for the variant (live leaderboard), but not shown for layout 0, which is geometrically extreme; the LLM-agent baseline on Standard is 0
findings.description: On the live leaderboard, 28 of 64 models have nonzero full SR on Standard make_toast: VPP2 56%, WorldScape-R2SI 44%, InternW0_delta 24%. The official scorer can therefore reach 100 through the native action path on Standard. Layout 0 uses toaster 00001, which appears in 43 of the first 25x3 evaluated Standard layouts; 00000 appears in 32. The reference GPT-6-Astra scored 0 on Standard; no LLM-agent row shows any Standard partial credit. A pilot failure on layout 0 is weak evidence about the agent unless the G1-F1 controls and the C9 reachability check exist.

Keep layout 0 if it was chosen before seeing results, as PLAN.md:24 requires; just disclose its rank.

key_facts: Native env.success starts True (eval_env.py:114,218), and run_eval counts any env still True as a success (eval_env.py:799-803). An early return without the end flag is scored as success. The reference Astra adapter fixes this with _mark_incomplete_episode_failed (XPolicyLab@5d0be149 policy/GPT_6_Astra_Direct_EEF/inspect/deploy.py:331-351, called at :712-714).

Reward checks are registered only in run_eval (eval_env.py:772-774) after reset clears them (make_toast.py:21-23 -> reward_manager.py:39-42). With empty lists get_reward() returns 1.0 (reward_manager.py:536-541), so a worker that skips run_reward() latches success before its first action.
Setting env.success False disables all reward and score evaluation (func_parser.py:61-62; reward_manager.py:379,394,533) and ends the episode at the next is_episode_end (eval_env.py:845-860).

After the end flag, take_action skips physics and the counter (eval_env.py:368-369) but still runs reward_manager.step (:457) and is_episode_end (:465). Success is frozen by end_flag (:852-853); the transition score can still advance while success is True.

claims.claim: Starting the monitor saves fd 1 and fd 2, dup2's pipes over them, and echoes throttled output to the saved fds (physx_warning_monitor.py:478-486, 24-31).
claims.evidence: physx_warning_monitor.py:480-486 does `saved_fd = os.dup(target_fd); os.dup2(w, target_fd)` for _TARGET_FDS=(1,2) (:235). _emit writes to the saved fd and to the /dev/shm mirror (:317-336). Throttling is per key per 1.0 s window (:98-123, :219). Non-PhysX lines use the whole timestamp-stripped line as their key (:654-658).

claims.claim: If the monitor starts first, protocol lines pass through the throttled echo path, and Carb logs interleave with them on the runner's pipe.
claims.evidence: The first half holds. If the monitor starts first, os.dup(1) duplicates the monitor's fd-1 pipe, so every reply goes through reader1, its throttle and the mirror, and is echoed to the saved original stdout (physx_warning_monitor.py:483-492, 633-664). Interleaving holds only for Kit/Carb output written to fd 1 before the worker's dup2(2,1). An example is AppLauncher launched at import time, as main.py:129 does. After that dup2, Carb's fd-1 writes go to the fd-2 pipe and are echoed to stderr. The bigger hazards are dropped duplicate replies and a defeated fd-1 self-heal (see findings).

claims.claim: The monitor's fatal watchdog force-exits with rc=99 45 s after a fatal, even while the main thread is waiting for Astra.

findings.title: The plan has no inventory of the native main.py / eval_policy.sh / run_eval side effects that a bypassing worker must replicate
findings.description:
The plan never says which native entrypoint the simulator worker uses. A text search of PLAN.md, INPUT_CONTRACT.md, README.md, planning_manifest.json and planning_review.json finds no mention of main.py, eval_policy.sh, the PhysX monitor, AppLauncher, render sync, num_envs, process_config or camera frequency. main.py cannot be imported as a library: it parses argv (main.py:64), starts the monitor (:111-121) and launches Kit (:129) at module level. So the reviewers' fix of neutralizing its retry and substitution loop (main.py:353-445) means re-creating its setup in the adapter worker.

The dropped effects fall into four groups:
- Silent when dropped: the monitor flag, the zero-delay render settings, the process_config physics overrides, and the reward registration inside run_eval.
- Semi-silent: num_envs (10 instead of 1) and sim.seed.
- Fail loudly: camera.default_frequency, deploy_cfg/WsModelClient, and the SeedManager keys. Loud failures invite ad-hoc fixes with non-native values, so these need pinned values too.
- Verified no-op for arx_x5: process_randomization.
findings.evidence: main.py:64, 111-129, 261-352, 353-449. eval_policy.sh:5-6, 69, 105-107, 116, 123-131, 142-184. camera_manager.py:182-183 assigns the local `default_frequency` only when the key is present, and it is used at :254-257; camera_config.yml has no such key, so main.py:336-341 is its only source. EvalEnv requires deploy_cfg.port (eval_env.py:178-180), opens a WebSocket handshake in its constructor (eval_env.py:188-196; XPolicyLab@5d0be149 client_server/ws/model_client.py:80-85) and calls model_client.call('reset') on every reset (eval_env.py:245). SeedManager needs eval_cfg num_envs and task_name (seed_manager.py:15, 18), and eval_cfg.seed selects Assets/Eval_Layout/RoboDojo/arx_x5/<seed>/ (:32-38). EvalEnv writes eval_result/... and _stream/ relative to the CWD (eval_env.py:80-100, 818-819, 832).
findings.recommendation:
Add a 'native entrypoint parity' table to Stage B/D. Mark each row as replicated by importing the native helper, replicated by copied glue code, or intentionally not replicated (with disclosure). Rows:
1. Monitor started before AppLauncher, plus eval_cfg.physx_monitor_enabled=True (GAP2-02/03).
2. add_zero_delay_kit_args (GAP2-07).
3. AppLauncher arguments: --headless, device, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. The --enable kit args are redundant because isaaclab.python.kit:26,31 already enables both extensions.
4. eval_cfg fields, with seed=0 as 'seed-directory0'.
5. A credential-free local stub for deploy_cfg/WsModelClient, never the Astra transport (PLAN.md:58).
6. num_envs forced to 1, with an assertion that env.num_envs==1.
7. process_randomization: called and dumped, though it is a no-op for arx_x5.
8. process_config (GAP2-05).
9. camera.default_frequency pinned to 25.
10. sim.seed=[0].
11. Layout selection: assert layout id 0 and the sha256 of its JSON.
12. A fresh worker process per attempt, with monitor.reset() before EvalEnv.reset, since a fatal never clears in-process (physx_warning_monitor.py:258-259).
13. run_reward()/get_score() (GAP2-06).
14. Exception, abandon, substitute and restart handling: not replicated; replaced by the pre-registered classification (GAP2-02/04).
15. CWD and save_dir inside runs/<attempt>/, never vendor/ (PLAN.md:51).

At worker start, write a hash-bound dump containing:
- OmegaConf.to_yaml(env_cfg) after the equivalent of main.py:343, plus the AppLauncher args including kit_args.
- zero_delay_active(), whether the monitor has started, and the effective ROBODOJO_FATAL_FORCE_EXIT_GRACE_S.
- The registered reward stages and score_meta.
- The layout id and its file hash, and the CWD.

Bind its sha256 into the approval/launch manifest (PLAN.md:76, 116). For an offline oracle, run main.py's pure-Python config assembly (main.py:261-343, using utils.pipeline_utils, which imports only os/yaml/json) on the vendored tree. Require YAML identical to the adapter's dump, except for documented rows.

findings.title: Under a bypass the PhysX monitor is off by default; for make_toast it is the only detector of toaster/bread transform failures, and the plan has no non-agent outcome class
findings.plan_location: PLAN.md §4.B, §4.F (lines 116-122); §4.A line 68 covers only model-free install failures
findings.description:
main.py enables the monitor for make_toast because of its Articulation section (the toaster). EvalEnv defaults the flag to False, which disables every broken-env check: in setup_scene, in get_obs_batch, at the start of each action and after each of its 10 physics substeps. It also disables the NaN backstop. That backstop checks robot end-effector poses only, so a transform failure confined to toaster or bread prims (under /World/envs/env_0/) can only be caught by the log PATTERN.

Natively, such a sample is abandoned, never scored, and replaced by the next layout. Under the uc7.1 code there are two outcomes. A robot NaN becomes null in the protocol, is rejected by the parent and is booked as a generic 'infrastructure_error', with libero_success carried over from the last cached status (probably False). A toaster-only break raises nothing and is scored as an ordinary native outcome. Stage F only says 'immediate error finalization' and 'completion time N/A'. Nothing maps simulator physics breaks to native's 'abandoned/not counted' semantics.
findings.evidence: main.py:85-100, 270, 372-374, 401-432. make_toast.yml:1-20. eval_env.py:63, 263-264, 270-275, 359-360, 451-455, 711-723, 743-766, 784-832. scene_manager.py:72, 488. physx_warning_monitor.py:175. agent_speedup_v2_truth.py:111, 124-125. observation.py:90-94. evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:1557-1558, 1265, 1569. PLAN.md:68, 118, 122. UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:153, 166, 170, 202.
findings.recommendation:
Start the monitor (with the GAP2-03 ordering) and pass eval_cfg.physx_monitor_enabled=True. Before approval, pre-register outcome classes: physx_broken_env (log PATTERN or NaN backstop), physx_fatal (including rc=99), layout_unstable (UnStableError at reset) and reset_nan (GAP2-08). For each class, set native_success=null and native_score=null, because native never scores such samples. Do not count it as a native fail or an agent failure, and do not report it with completion time. The attempt is consumed with no automatic re-run (protocol §6:166). Record the agent actions taken before the break.

Model-free test: add a diagnostic-only worker op, refused in live mode with the same gate as uc7.1's oracle op (agent_speedup_v2_sim.py:213-226). After reset it os.write()s 'Invalid PhysX transform detected for /World/envs/env_0/toaster' to fd 1, without a Kit-ms stamp. Poll get_broken_envs() until it returns {0}. Then require the next step to return a structured physx_broken_env error, and require the runner to finalize under that class with native fields null.

findings.title: The monitor collides with uc7.1's stdout protocol unless the protocol fd is split before monitor.start()
findings.plan_location: PLAN.md §4.B line 72 ('Separate the simulator worker from the model process')
findings.description:
The only order that satisfies both contracts is: os.dup(1) for the protocol, dup2(2,1), then monitor.start(), then add_zero_delay_kit_args, then AppLauncher. This fits naturally in uc7.1's lazily constructed worker. If the monitor starts first (for example, copying main.py's module-level start ahead of worker_main), the protocol fd becomes a second reference to the monitor's fd-1 pipe. That has five consequences:
- Replies pass through reader1's throttle, which keys non-PhysX lines by the whole line. A byte-identical reply sent within 1.0 s (repeated error replies, metadata) is dropped. The parent then waits its 120 s response timeout and kills the worker.
- Each distinct reply is kept as a throttle key, up to 4096 per round. LIBERO's 512x512 PNG data URIs measured 0.26-0.37 MB each (t6 request 000014), so three-view replies are about 1 MB each. That is an estimated up to ~1.4 GB retained for 1,400 replies.
- Replies, including evaluator-only truth replies, are mirrored into /dev/shm/physx_monitor_<pid>_<ts>.log.
- The fd-1 EOF self-heal can no longer fire, because the protocol fd keeps the pipe open. Detection is then lost silently if Kit 'steals fd=1'.
- If Kit started before the worker's dup2, as at main.py:129, its startup output reaches the protocol pipe first, and the first reply fails with 'simulator emitted invalid JSON'.
The correct order also puts Isaac start-up inside the first request, which is under the parent's 120 s timeout. Start-up time is unmeasured, because nothing is installed (planning_manifest.json:89-90).
findings.evidence: physx_warning_monitor.py:16-18, 37-38, 105-123, 219-220, 231, 330-336, 472-492, 565-582, 633-664. agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:94-103, 138. libero.py:42, 603-637, 963-966. On this host /proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size = 1048576. Image sizes measured from /workspace/gpt_field/runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/trial/requests/000014-4e083fb9766f4577ba39084f81be8944.request.json (12 URIs, 255,542-373,022 chars).
findings.recommendation:
Write the order above into Stage B as an invariant, and assert at worker start that the protocol fd's os.fstat inode differs from those of fd 1 and fd 2. Add these model-free tests:
(a) Send two byte-identical requests within 1 s and require two replies.
(b) Tee the parent's raw stdout bytes and require every line to parse as a protocol reply, with line count equal to request count. Lines injected on fd 1 and fd 2 and Python prints must appear only on stderr.
(c) Have a diagnostic op dup2 /dev/null onto fd 1, then require '[PhysXMonitor] reader fd=1 got EOF, reattaching.' and continued detection of a later injected line.
(d) Measure cold Isaac start and the first reset against the 120 s timeout in Stage A. Disclose any timeout change as an adapter setting.

findings.title: The fatal watchdog exits rc=99 after 45 s (immediately for CUDA error 700) regardless of the worker's idle wait; how this is reported must be decided with the user
findings.description: Once any fatal pattern is seen, the watchdog thread calls os._exit(99) after 45 s, or immediately for 'Error code 700!', whatever the main thread is doing. Between requests, the uc7.1 worker's main thread blocks on stdin during model waits. In the real uc7.1 t6 run, the 14 Astra latencies had a median of about 24 s and a maximum of 65 s, and 1 of 14 exceeded 45 s. The plan keeps a 180 s per-request deadline plus finite retries. After a step-time fatal surfaces as an error, the runner runs finalize_truth and video finalization against the worker, which can be killed mid-way. os._exit skips atexit, so the /dev/shm mirror is left behind and unflushed pipe bytes are lost. The parent then sees 'worker exited without a response (status 99)' or a BrokenPipe, and books 'infrastructure_error' with libero_success taken from the last cached status. The plan's supervisor correctly prevents the native restart loops. What is missing is a rule for how a forced exit is reported.
findings.evidence: physx_warning_monitor.py:186-191, 204-212, 508-522, 875-936. agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:99. Response latencies come from created_at/completed_at in /workspace/gpt_field/runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/trial/requests/*.response.json (65, 29, 22, 30, 35, 23, 24, 18, 17, 14, 8, 18, 30, 33 s). evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:1557-1605, 1265, 1569. libero.py:603-607, 619-620. PLAN.md:116. eval_policy.sh:165-180. main.py:211-251.
findings.recommendation:
Ask the user to decide:
(1) The label for rc=99 / physx_fatal, and whether it counts toward the pilot. Recommend 'native-invalid, non-agent, not counted', with native fields null.
(2) Whether any re-run, which needs a new approval, reuses layout0 and the same approved plan (allowed with exact bindings, INPUT_CONTRACT.md:38) or follows native's next-layout substitution.
(3) Keep the native 45 s grace and record its effective value; do not enlarge it to cover model waits.
Runner side: call proc.poll() after each Astra response, classify a dead worker before sending, copy the /dev/shm mirror into runs/<attempt>/ during finalization, and never report the cached libero_success for these classes.
Model-free test with ROBODOJO_FATAL_FORCE_EXIT_GRACE_S=2: inject 'fail to launch kernel' and expect rc=99 in about 2-3 s with the pre-registered class. Then inject the CUDA error 700 line and expect an immediate exit.

findings.title: data_source: teleop also turns on PhysX stabilization, and both make_toast overrides are applied only by main.py's process_config
findings.description: PLAN.md:66 treats `data_source: teleop` purely as demonstration metadata, and PLAN.md:26 names only the self-collision override. For teleop tasks, process_config sets sim.physx.enable_stabilization=True, against a native default of False. That changes the solver's contact handling for the toaster lever and the bread. process_config is also the only place where robot_self_collision:false becomes enabled_self_collisions=False. Both reach the simulator only through main.py:328. A bypass that re-implements only the documented self-collision override would silently run make_toast with non-native physics, contradicting PLAN.md:24 ('Preserve the standard task's ... physics and task overrides'). The other process_config keys are unchanged defaults for make_toast: render_interval 10, scene default, camera_config, dual_x5.
findings.evidence: pipeline_utils.py:66-110 (teleop branch at :82-83, self-collision at :105-107, eval_nums at :109). _task.yml:1-8, 67-70. base_env.py:18-41 (enable_stabilization False at :25) and :165-182. task_env.py:12, 32 (BaseEnv receives config.sim).
findings.recommendation: Amend PLAN.md:26/66 to list both overrides: PhysX stabilization on (from data_source teleop) and robot self-collision off. findings.title: Native success and partial-score checks are registered only inside run_eval; skipping it yields a false full success after one action and a partial score of 0
findings.description: make_toast's run_reward() and get_score() only register checks: rm.check appends to check_list, and rm.score registers the transition [25, 50] tiers. They are called only from EvalEnv.run_eval, which only main.py calls. MakeToastCommon.reset empties every list. With nothing registered, get_reward() returns 1.0 whenever env.success is True, and EvalEnv.reset sets success to True by default. So a uc7.1-style driver that calls EvalEnv.reset and then take_action without run_eval gets end_flag=success=True at the first is_episode_end, after one native action. The uc7.1 runner breaks on success. The partial score is 0.0, because score_meta.mode stays None. The plan's 'initially incomplete success' check is made after reset, before get_reward is first evaluated, so as written it may not catch this.

findings.title: Zero-delay render settings come only from main.py; the pinned IsaacLab fork always launches isaaclab.python.kit, which lacks them
findings.description: main.py appends three Kit settings before AppLauncher: checkForHydraRenderComplete=1000, renderer/waitIdle and hydraEngine/waitIdle. They are read only at start-up. Without them, a camera frame 'reflects the state of the previous update, and under load ... can be several frames old'. The plan and contract require head and wrist images synchronized with measured robot state for both arms, and uc7.1's execution requests pair calibrated state with RGB. A bypass that builds AppLauncher without these settings would feed Astra lagging images, which hurts the agent for a reason unrelated to its ability.

findings.title: NaN coverage has gaps even with the monitor on: reset-time set_origin_endpose, and uc7.1's NaN-to-null serializer
findings.description: EvalEnv.reset calls robot_manager.set_origin_endpose() after setup_scene. That path runs quat2mat and mat2quat on the raw end-effector pose, and setup_scene runs only the log-based check, never _check_endpose_finite. So a NaN at reset can still raise a bare LinAlgError when the monitor missed the warning. RoboDojo's own docstring describes this failure, and notes that main.py then consumes the seed unless the monitor has flagged it. Separately, uc7.1 serializes non-finite floats as null, so a NaN that escaped the backstop would reach the parent as missing values rather than as a physics classification.
findings.evidence: eval_env.py:238-243, 263-264, 728-735 ('feeds a NaN-laden 3x3 into mat2quat, which throws LinAlgError'), 754-766. robot_manager.py:125-129, 204-216. main.py:386-399. agent_speedup_v2_truth.py:111, 124-125.
findings.recommendation:
Add model-free tests:
(i) A diagnostic hook returns a NaN end-effector pose for env 0 mid-episode. Expect PhysXBrokenError({0}) from _check_endpose_finite and the physx_broken_env class.
(ii) Inject a NaN before set_origin_endpose at reset. Expect the pre-registered reset_nan / zero-action interface-error class (protocol line 202), never an unclassified LinAlgError.
(iii) The adapter worker must reject non-finite values in policy-bound payloads with a classified error, rather than relying on jsonable's None coercion. Assert that no null appears in any model-visible numeric field.

findings.title: Model-free smokes or previews run through native main.py are acceptable only with an asserted layout id, because main.py substitutes layouts silently
findings.description: The provisioning suggestion to call main.py directly is reasonable for model-free install smokes. But with EVAL_NUM=1, an UnStableError, a broken env or an unflagged exception on layout 0 makes main.py run layout 1 in the same invocation, and eval_policy.sh adds up to 10 process restarts. A preview or smoke produced that way could silently show a different layout than layoutID0.

Mechanism verified. monitor.start() saves dup(1) and dup2's a pipe over fds 1 and 2 (physx_warning_monitor.py:478-492). Readers echo each line to the saved fd through a per-round throttle. The throttle is keyed on the timestamp-stripped whole line and drops repeats within THROTTLE_INTERVAL_S=1.0 (98-123, 219, 633-664). It keeps up to 4096 keys (220) and mirrors emitted lines into /dev/shm (472-476, 317-336). EOF self-heal fires only when no other descriptor holds the write end (565-582). uc7.1 workers dup the protocol fd and dup2(2,1) at the top of worker_main, then build the simulator lazily (agent_speedup_v2_user_check_sim.py:94-103). The parent kills the worker after 120 s without a reply (libero.py:42, 609-617) and rejects non-JSON lines (627-630). So a module-level monitor.start() placed before worker_main routes replies through the throttled echo. main.py:111-121 and the monitor docstring ('must be called BEFORE AppLauncher', line 37) both invite that placement. If AppLauncher stays lazy, this variant even passes a startup smoke, which makes the duplicate-drop hang subtle. Size data: t6 request 000014 carries 12 data URIs of 255,542-373,022 chars, and /proc/sys/fs/pipe-max-size here is 1048576. The ordering invariant and the proposed tests are well founded.

Watchdog verified. After any fatal pattern it calls os._exit(99) after 45 s, or at once for 'Error code 700!' (physx_warning_monitor.py:186-191, 204-212, 875-936), which skips atexit and the mirror unlink (522, 942-960). (2) With the monitor on, a step-time fatal normally surfaces synchronously as PhysXFatalError in the same request (eval_env.py:717-719). verdicts.reasoning: utils/pipeline_utils.py:70-72 and 82-83 set sim.physx.enable_stabilization=True when data_source is 'teleop', which applies to make_toast (_task.yml:67-70). The default is False (env/environment/base_env.py:25). The value is applied through setup_sim_cfg (:165-182) on config.sim (task_env.py:12, 32). robot_self_collision false becomes enabled_self_collisions=False (pipeline_utils.py:105-107). Calling native process_config, which is pure Python (os, yaml, env.global_configs, utils.load_file), applies both overrides.

verdicts.reasoning: EvalEnv.reset calls set_origin_endpose after setup_scene (eval_env.py:238-243). That runs quat2mat and mat2quat on raw end-effector poses (robot_manager.py:125-129, 204-216). setup_scene runs only the log check (263-264) and never _check_endpose_finite, and EvalEnv's own docstring documents the LinAlgError from NaN in mat2quat (728-735). main.py's generic handler consumes the seed unless the monitor has flagged the env (386-399). uc7.1's jsonable maps non-finite values to None (agent_speedup_v2_truth.py:110-128). The proposed tests and the explicit reject-non-finite rule are reasonable.

The finder's partial verdict holds. Sync models run via to_thread (model_server.py:390-396), so request_deadline_unavailable is raised deterministically before any HTTP open (transport.py:108-113, 429-436). An async-inline model blocks the server loop, as the server's own comment warns (model_server.py:551-553). However, the env-side loop runs on its own thread (model_client.py:16-20, 75-79), reconnects once reusing the request_id (protocol/client.py:537-556), and the server replays its cached response (model_server.py:294-311, 352-353). So the async variant is timing-dependent rather than deterministically failing. Both variants are unacceptable.

The robot-NaN path is verified. jsonable maps non-finite values to None (agent_speedup_v2_truth.py:124-125), and the LIBERO PolicyObservation rejects them (observation.py:90-94). The exception is booked as infrastructure_error (evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:1557-1558), with the cached libero_success (1569); SimProcess.status is updated before the observation is parsed (libero.py:658-660). With the monitor off, a toaster or bread transform failure has no detector (eval_env.py:711-713, 743-763). That it 'raises nothing' anywhere downstream is plausible but untested.

If the monitor starts first, worker_main's os.dup(1) duplicates the monitor's fd-1 pipe, so replies go through reader1's throttle and are echoed to the saved stdout (physx_warning_monitor.py:483-492, 633-664). After the worker's dup2(2,1), fd 1 aliases the fd-2 pipe, so later Carb fd-1 output is echoed to stderr. Interleaving on the protocol pipe happens only for output written before that dup2, for example from an import-time AppLauncher as at main.py:129.

The finder's conditions hold. (1) The stale filter drops a line only for env indices that were broken at the last reset and only when it carries a Kit '[N ms]' stamp within the margin (physx_warning_monitor.py:394-408), so in a fresh worker the injected line is recorded. (2) Detection runs on asynchronous reader threads, so the test must poll get_broken_envs(). (3) The raise happens at the next check (eval_env.py:270-271, 359-360, 721-723). (4) Both readers scan lines (_process_log_segment), so this test cannot tell the correct fd order from the wrong one; a duplicate-reply test is also needed.

new_issues: [major] The plan never requires that reset-hash determinism hold across processes, yet the approval is claimed before that check. (1) LIBERO closes the prepare simulator before review (scripts/evaluate_agent_speedup_v2_user_check.py:304-306). (2) The approval is claimed before the run simulator starts (:590-595). The runner's comment there reads 'A reset mismatch below deliberately consumes this attempt but sends zero policy actions'. (3) The run then re-checks the approved hash in a fresh process (scripts/evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:1381-1388, which raises 'Reset observation differs from the frozen reset'). PLAN.md:76 and 108 ask for exact repeated resets ('two model-free resets'), but never require them to come from separate fresh worker processes. RoboDojo's render defaults include DLAA, global illumination and reflections (env/environment/base_env.py:43-57), and PhysX enhanced determinism is off (base_env.py:26). So in-process repeatability does not establish byte equality across processes. A mismatch at run time would consume the single approved attempt with 0 actions. Fix: run the Stage E repeated resets in at least two fresh workers, with the exact run launch topology, GPU and environment, and choose between exact and reviewed state/tolerance binding from that cross-process result before approval.

[major] If the frozen uc7.1 runner loop is reused, it has no horizon outcome. (1) OUTCOME_STATUSES is only success, user_stop, diagnostic_complete, diagnostic_sim_terminated and recovery_exhausted (scripts/evaluate_agent_speedup_v2.py:141-142). (2) validate_configuration rejects any action horizon: 'agent_speedup_v2 uses seed 7, settle 10 and no action horizon' (:211-212). (3) A simulator reporting 'terminated' without success raises RuntimeError('Simulator terminated without task success or an action horizon') (:1456-1457), which is booked as infrastructure_error (:1557-1558). Native make_toast ends at take_action_cnt >= step_lim = 1400 (task/RoboDojo/tasks/make_toast.py:15; eval_env.py:845-860) and then silently skips further actions (eval_env.py:368-369). An unchanged loop would therefore either book a genuine horizon failure as an infrastructure error or keep sending Astra requests against frozen physics with no cap. PLAN.md:21, 122 and 128 assume a horizon outcome but do not say this requires a reviewed change to the frozen loop, disclosed in the core-to-adapter diff (PLAN.md:58). That change needs a new terminal status counted as an agent failure with completion time N/A, and the 1400-action termination test must run through the runner, not only the native env.

[minor] The LIBERO GPU-pinning recipe does not carry over to Isaac. LIBERO launches strip CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and pin EGL rendering with MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID (UC7_1_ASTRA_HIGH_TEST_PROTOCOL.md:101, 115-116, 128; runs/agent_speedup_v2_uc71_relayout_t6_20261028_001/run_once.py:44-47). Native RoboDojo selects the GPU with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=device_id (scripts/eval_policy.sh:105-107), and the fork's AppLauncher sets physics_gpu = active_gpu = the cuda:N index, which defaults to 0 (IsaacLab@afca7b09 app_launcher.py:682-683, 708-711). A wrapper copied from run_once.py would therefore default Isaac rendering to device index 0 on this shared 8-GPU host. On this host the CUDA order also differs from the /dev/nvidia minor order (memory gpu-minor-order-reversed.md). The Stage A 'one selected GPU' check (PLAN.md:68) should bind the GPU environment in the launch manifest and verify which physical GPU Isaac actually uses, for example via nvidia handles in /proc/<pid>/fd. Whether Kit's Vulkan device selection honors CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is unverified.
